Sports.title: Johnny Fisher’s Kristian Prenga Target Could Backfire Horribly
Sports.content:
Johnny Fisher is flirting with disaster by targeting Kristian Prenga for his planned late-February return. Two confidence-building wins against Ivan Balaz and Michael Pirotton may have steadied the ship after his May 2025 stoppage loss to Dave Allen, but stepping straight into the pocket with the man who put Anthony Joshua on the canvas twice is a massive leap in lethality.

Fisher openly favors Prenga over former IBF titleholder Charles Martin, drawn primarily to the marquee value of the Albanian’s recent high-profile outing.

“I think Prenga would be a good one because he’s fought recently against Joshua,” Fisher told EverythingBoxing.

While that Joshua link offers undeniable promotional appeal, it also provides every reason for his corner to slam the brakes on. Prenga proved in July that he possesses sudden, fight-altering power by flooring Joshua twice in the opening round before being halted in the second. If Joshua struggled to stay upright under that initial barrage, Fisher’s punch resistance will face immediate trial.

The issue stems directly from how Fisher operates inside the ropes. His trademark front-foot assault demands constant forward momentum, letting his hands go in high-volume bursts. That aggressive approach requires meticulous defensive exits. Every exchange demands a snapped-back high guard, a sharp change of angle, or a clean exit out of range. Fisher cannot afford to linger in the pocket to hunt for an extra punch. Lingering against Prenga is an invitation for disaster.

Prenga’s failure to finish Joshua in the second round exposed his own tactical flaws, notably an apparent reluctance to press his advantage when his opponent needed time to clear the fog. Some attributed that hesitation to early fatigue from emptying the tank, while others saw it as costly indecision. Fisher cannot build an entire game plan on the hope that Prenga lets another hurt man off the hook. Slipping shots, disrupting Prenga’s rhythm, and forcing misses remain far safer than trading bombs in the pocket.

Martin offers an entirely different, perhaps more educational test. Dealing with Martin’s southpaw stance, deceptive reach, and straight left hand would force Fisher to sharpen his footwork and spatial awareness. While Martin still carries punch power, his style tests tactical discipline rather than delivering the raw, explosive trauma Prenga brings to the opening bell.

Fisher deserves praise for targeting a live wire, but Zuffa must weigh whether his defensive adjustments are genuinely ready for this level of fire. Another devastating stoppage loss would undo his rebuilding progress, leaving the promotion with a badly damaged asset whose flaws were exposed by the very first puncher capable of exploiting them.

Sports.title: Mora Warns Joshua Buatsi: Stop Brawling with Hutchinson
Sports.content:
Sergio Mora argues Joshua Buatsi can simplify his rematch with Willy Hutchinson by sticking to a disciplined jab and compelling the counterpuncher to initiate the action. The difficulty lies in implementing that strategy without muting the devastating rib attack that defines Buatsi, or getting dragged into brawling the moment Hutchinson scores.

Two knockdowns secured the verdict for Buatsi in their first encounter, yet Mora insists the Londoner gave away unnecessary openings by working inside the telephone booth. The former world champion urges Buatsi to command distance, bag rounds on the scorecards, and make the Scotsman gamble.

“Buatsi can make it so easy for himself. I know he’s a great body puncher, and he makes fights entertaining. But he can make this fight so easy if he uses more boxing than fighting, and he fights a little bit longer. If he pops behind the jab. Let Hutchinson make the mistakes because Hutchinson, he’s a good fighter, he’s a good counter-puncher, but he’s a reactive fighter. He’s not a go-get-you fighter,” said Mora to DAZN Boxing.

Strategic compromises exist within that blueprint. Hooking to the body requires closing the gap through the danger zone where Hutchinson’s hand speed can intercept incoming fire. Boxing at range shields Buatsi from check hooks, yet it inevitably caps the number of flush shots he can sink downstairs.

Stabbing jabs into Hutchinson’s chest and solar plexus provides an answer. Buatsi can disrupt breathing without smothering his own reach, keeping the target moving while assessing whether heavier artillery should follow. The body work shifts from an all-out physical press into an earned sequence.

Sharper feints also disrupt a reactive opponent. Buatsi has no obligation to commit fully with every twitch. Subtle level changes and shoulder feints will pull Hutchinson out of his stance, leaving him off balance when he reaches for air.

None of this functions without banking early points. Hutchinson will gladly sit back if he is allowed to dictate the pace from the outside. Mora’s scenario of a stoppage depends on Hutchinson feeling desperate enough on the scorecards to march forward into incoming traffic.

“So if Buatsi can win some early rounds and get Hutchinson to come at him, I could see Buatsi running him into a right hand and hurting him, and dropping him and maybe stopping him,” said Mora.

Securing ring center anchors this entire setup. Forcing Hutchinson to circle eats away at the Scotsman’s legs while preserving Buatsi’s stamina for the late rounds. An active lead hand must continually penalize every reset.

Temperament presents the true obstacle. The moment Hutchinson lands an eye-catching flurry, Buatsi must fight his natural urge to fire back instantly in the pocket. Stepping back behind the jab after tasting leather will reveal whether Buatsi values tactical efficiency over raw violence.

Buatsi faces Hutchinson in a rematch for the vacant WBC light heavyweight title this Saturday, November 7, at Manchester’s AO Arena, live on DAZN.

Sports.title: Outbox or Get Cracked: Shane Mosley’s Bentley Gamble
Sports.content:
Shane Mosley Jr. needed two trips to the scale on Friday, sweating off a stubborn final pound to reach the 160-pound limit after coming in at 161. That extra hour in the sauna creates immediate questions about his legs, particularly against a puncher like London’s Denzel Bentley over 10 rounds at the Copper Box Arena. Bentley checked in right on the mark at 160 on his first try.

Mosley’s stated strategy depends on superior activity and sustained output. With a five-inch reach advantage, his cleanest route to a points win is operating behind a busy, disciplining jab to trap Bentley on the perimeter. But if Friday’s late weight cut robs Mosley of fluid lateral movement, Bentley will not have to work hard to close the distance.

Middleweight madness incoming 👀 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 @2Sharp_D – 160lbs

🇺🇸 @IamShaneMosley – 160lbs 📺 @SkySports + @ParamountPlus | #ZuffaBoxing12 https://t.co/E1Rvtw2vJI — Zuffa_Boxing (@Zuffa_Boxing) November 6, 2026

Mosley made his intentions clear this week, saying that a points victory in hostile territory holds more value for him than an early finish:

“The reason why I feel like it’s even better to beat you on points than to knock you out is because if I can show everybody in here, everybody in the arena that I’m better than you, that’s better to me than knocking you out,” Mosley said to Sky Sports Boxing sit down. “What’s better is if I went to your hometown and in front of your fans and beat you convincingly, where everybody said, ‘Yeah, he won.’ That to me shows greatness.”

Aiming to win a clear decision on British cards requires a dominant volume gap, especially against a hometown fighter. Scraping by on split margins fails the standard of mastery Mosley outlined.

Bentley was initially unfazed by the prediction before recognizing the tactical insult behind it.

“At first I thought, ‘All right.’ I went back and I thought, ‘Wait, I’d rather he say he’d knock me out,’” Bentley admitted. “He’s basically saying he can outpoint me.” His response was blunt: “That’s not happening.”

For Bentley, winning does not require round-by-round territorial dominance. He carries an 82% knockout rate and thrives when opponents throw in prolonged combinations, creating counter-punching lanes for his right hand. If Mosley’s punch output dips in the middle rounds from dehydration, Bentley’s heavy single shots will stand out sharply on the scorecards.

“I want to crack that chin. I want to see if it’s real. Watch,” Bentley said.

Bentley has acknowledged Mosley’s chin and ring experience, so a wild blitz out of the gate is unlikely. Even with the WBO belt absent after Bentley opted for this bout over a mandatory assignment, the terms of the fight are clear: Mosley must execute a disciplined, 10-round boxing clinic at range, while Bentley needs only one sustained opening to punish him on the inside.

Sports.title: Groves Expects Fury vs Joshua Despite Fury Injury Rumor
Sports.content:
George Groves fully expects Tyson Fury to step into the ring against Anthony Joshua, brushing off chatter that an injury could derail the December 11 date. His view is simple. Both men are battle-worn veterans, so expecting either to show up at one hundred percent is unrealistic.

The conversation kicked off after Frank Bruno claimed an insider from Fury’s gym told him an injury could stop the clash from happening. Groves did not have insider details on Fury’s body, yet he cast heavy doubt on the idea that the event is actually in jeopardy.

“I don’t know about any rumors, but there might be a lot of kidology, a lot of rumors floating about. Could have been leaked by anyone,” Groves told talkSPORT Boxing. “I genuinely don’t know, but I’ll be very shocked if that fight don’t happen. I think both guys will fight no matter what.”

Groves offered an unfiltered take on where both boxers stand right now. He views them as past their physical primes, meaning a completely smooth camp is out of the question for either side.

“I don’t think at this stage either one of these two guys who are veterans, way past their best, are going to be in perfect condition going into this fight. That doesn’t matter. They’re going to fight,” Groves said.

It is a harsh reality check for an all-British heavyweight meeting years in the making. Fans are getting the spectacle, but Groves points out that the clock has been ticking the whole time.

Looking back on his own ring days, Groves pointed out that modern training camps are never completely clean. Wear and tear, missed sessions, or personal distractions always creep in, no matter how sharp someone looks at the podium.

Whether Fury carries a genuine knock remains unconfirmed. Bruno’s story is secondhand talk, and Groves made it clear he has no direct intel. Still, Groves remains convinced that both heavyweights will walk through fire to make the bell.

When a guaranteed nine-figure bag is sitting on the table, standard training camp knocks take a back seat.

Walking away from a projected 100 million dollars each over an elbow tweak, sore shoulder, or bruised rib would be professional madness. At this stage of their careers, neither Tyson Fury nor Anthony Joshua has another payday of this magnitude waiting in reserve.

If one pulls out now with a minor complaint, there is zero guarantee the momentum, public appetite, or financial backing survives to reschedule it cleanly.

Both fighters have operated under fire while compromised before. Fury fought through severe cuts and facial trauma, while Joshua has spent years managing the mileage on his body. Every veteran north of thirty-five carries something into the ring; reaching fight night at one hundred percent physical perfection is a myth in modern heavyweight boxing.

Unless one of them suffers a catastrophic structural tear or a medical commission flat-out denies a license, they are walking to the ring on December 11 in Cardiff. At 100 million dollars apiece, you fight through the aches, take your shot, and settle whatever needs healing after the final bell.

Sports.title: Fury: Ryan Garcia Has The Star Power Haney And Shakur Lack
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury believes Ryan Garcia is primed to take over as the premier attraction in American boxing once Canelo Alvarez steps away. Fury points directly to Garcia’s charisma and gift for commanding headlines, putting pure drawing power ahead of pure technical mastery.

While Fury listed talents like Devin Haney, Shakur Stevenson, Abdullah Mason, and Richardson Hitchins, Garcia earned his clear vote. The challenge facing everyone else is something victories in the ring cannot automatically fix: reaching beyond the hardcore boxing bubble.

“Other than Canelo, which Canelo’s obviously on his way out too, then it’s Ryan Garcia in America,” Fury said on Behind the Mic. “He’s got a personality. He talks. He’s entertaining. He’s charismatic.”

Asked if he sees reflections of himself in Garcia, Fury agreed completely, admitting others might possess sharper fundamentals but insisting they cannot generate the same revenue.

It is a crucial division when assessing Canelo’s commercial heir. Observers can debate Garcia’s ring craft against elite competition, yet Fury focuses strictly on ticket sales and viewer attention. Boxing culture often conflates technical brilliance with stardom, even though they demand completely different skill sets.

Garcia keeps the public talking during long layoffs. His unpredictable persona draws viewers who would never bother watching sparring footage or checking divisional rankings. People tune in hoping to see him win or desperate to watch him get knocked out, but either motivation sells pay-per-views.

Fury sounded far more skeptical about the mainstream presence of other top contenders.

“Inside of boxing people know who they are,” Fury said. “Outside of boxing, you go and ask 50 people … they don’t know who they are.”

Haney, Stevenson, Mason, and Hitchins have built formidable resumes. Yet Fury argues that respect from devoted boxing circles will only carry an athlete to a certain ceiling. Becoming the marquee figure who causes general sports fans to clear their weekend calendars demands a bigger presence.

Fury also took aim at modern streaming setups, questioning whether current platforms actually build true mainstream excitement. He recalled previous eras where extensive profile features introduced contenders long before fight night, whereas modern streaming formats often show the event without making casual viewers care in advance.

Because of that shift, self-promotion falls squarely on the fighter. Fury stressed that young talent must chase interviews, drop consistent content, and hustle for their own spotlight instead of waiting for a promoter to do the heavy lifting.

Garcia naturally excels at that playbook. Pure spectacle does not guarantee long-term dominance, since keeping the public invested still requires memorable bouts and dependable results. Even so, Fury’s view holds firm: Garcia knows how to hook an audience before the first bell sounds, while his peers face a much steeper climb proving they can match that commercial reach.

Sports.title: Conor Benn Says Pacquiao Fight Offered For December
Sports.content:
Conor Benn has confirmed he received an offer to square off against Manny Pacquiao this December, but opted against the date to focus on family time and physical recovery. While Benn remains open to meeting the boxing legend in early 2027, major questions remain about which weight class could accommodate both men.

Benn pointed to the brutal toll of his recent cut to 147 pounds, alongside the arrival of his newborn son, as key reasons for passing on the end-of-year window.

“The fight got presented to me for December, and it was just too soon making weight. Got a newborn son,” Benn said to Sky Sports Boxing. “So for me it was really about spending time with my family and just enjoying this period, the festive period, with my family. But if Q1 he wants to get on again, I’m interested.”

While Pacquiao represents a lucrative, marquee target for a return bout, Benn’s physical transformation presents a major hurdle. Having bulked back up to around 185 pounds, Benn insists his days at welterweight are completely finished. He even dismissed campaigning at junior middleweight.

“My future’s at middleweight,” Benn stated. “I thought about light middle. There’s nothing in me at light middle even. That’s how bad the weight cut was.”

Without a designated catchweight, matching an eight-division champion who spent his career far lighter against a fighter settling into middleweight remains an unresolved riddle.

Reflecting on his recent loss to Ryan, Benn admitted that outside noise fueled his miscalculated attempt to hit the welterweight limit.

“I don’t know what I was thinking making 147,” Benn said. “There’s one thing making the weight, and then there’s one thing performing at your best at the weight, and it showed. I paid the price for, say, chasing greatness.”

Still, Benn gave Ryan full credit for landing the decisive blows and finding victory on the night. Though he wanted the chance to battle on after rising from the canvas, Benn refused to fault the referee for waving off the bout, taking full accountability for the outcome.

Facing Pacquiao offers Benn an appealing path forward in 2027, but bridging the massive weight gap will require serious negotiations before anyone can sign a contract.

Pacquiao is a novelty payday trap. Even if Benn wins, nobody gives him real credit for beating a faded icon. If he looks bad winning, he gets ridiculed. If he loses, he is finished at the elite level.

Sports.title: Devin Haney Needs to Stop Living in the Past to Sell Liam Paro Clash
Sports.content:
Devin Haney is digging into his past, using his victories over George Kambosos to hype his December 19 unification clash with Liam Paro at Chase Center. Dominating Kambosos secured undisputed status at lightweight, but rehashing those nights won’t fire up crowds to see him chase another belt.

“My resume speaks for itself,” Haney stated. “I’ve never been afraid to go into a champion’s backyard and put my record on the line. I went to Australia, took George Kambosos’ belts, and became undisputed lightweight champion of the world. Now I’m bringing another Australian world champion, Liam Paro, into my backyard. This time, I plan to take his belt and become a unified welterweight world champion right here at home.”

Rehashing those wins now doesn’t elevate Liam Paro; it just reminds everyone how limited Kambosos actually was. The problem is that nationality is not a fighting style. Paro earned his IBF junior welterweight belt by traveling to Puerto Rico and physically outworking Subriel Matias, a dangerous puncher who was supposed to run through him.

If Haney truly understood how to build a fight, he would talk about Paro traveling to Puerto Rico to derail Subriel Matias or how Paro will actually bring a fight to him. Instead, he defaults to his old comfort blanket because self-promotion has never been his strong suit.

Paro is a tougher, more durable, and fundamentally different stylistic threat than Kambosos ever was. By presenting Paro through the Kambosos lens, Haney actually diminishes his own opponent while making the matchup sound like an easy rerun.

Devin needs to stop pretending the fans only care about belts. Haney should focus on the homecoming angle by promising a style change from his normal pure boxing approach. If he speaks openly about having to stand his ground against Paro’s physical, brawling style, he gives people a reason to watch for drama rather than just waiting on the judges’ scorecards.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Says Usyk Discussed March Trilogy Fight
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury claims Oleksandr Usyk signaled he could be ready to step into the ring again in March. That float keeps the door ajar for a third encounter, even with the Ukrainian holding two clear victories over him. Fury must handle Anthony Joshua first, yet he is already floating Usyk’s name for his next move.

Fury says the conversation happened when the Joshua matchup still hung in the balance. No paperwork exists for a trilogy, and Fury leaves crucial blanks, starting with whether March remains realistic once he steps out against Joshua.

“I actually spoke with Alexander to say, like, if he doesn’t fight, then we’ll do it. And he said he’s busy. He’s going on holiday with his family, but he could do a fight in March. So, maybe we do that in March. I don’t know yet. One fight at a time,” Fury said to Fighthype.

Booking the pairing again guarantees immense global interest, yet justifying it on merit gets tricky after back-to-back Usyk wins. Fury commands massive crowds, but he cannot claim unsettled business in the ring, no matter how vigorously he disputes the scorecards.

He still speaks as if the two losses solved nothing. When asked about those bouts, he doubled down on his claim that the judges got them wrong.

“I thought I won both fights,” Fury insisted. “I’m not bitter towards Alexander. He’s a good man. Like, he’s a God-fearing family man. I wish him all the luck in the world. But when he looks in that mirror every day, he knows he didn’t beat GK.”

That stance gives him an obvious marketing angle. He can insist he got robbed twice, promising to finish the job inside the distance next time. Spectators who watched Usyk take both contests will need stronger proof to believe a third chapter goes any differently.

Joshua might shatter this entire timeline anyway. Fury must defeat AJ and emerge unscathed for March to stay viable. A grueling war would instantly derail such a tight turnaround.

Fury also brushed aside talk about Usyk dropping down to cruiserweight to face David Benavidez, arguing that a Usyk trilogy offers the premier commercial draw.

“He just wants a big payday, and I’m his man to give him that,” Fury stated.

However, Saudis almost certainly pass on financing a third meeting, and outside of Riyadh, nobody else has the appetite to write those checks. Turki Alalshikh cares about global prestige and spectacle rather than standard event profit and loss, but he avoids financing fights that feel settled or stale. When one man has already collected 24 rounds of undisputed evidence across two fights, the storyline vanishes.

Alalshikh wants legacy events that captivate the sporting world, not expensive reruns where the outcome feels foregone. Unless Tyson Fury delivers an explosive, career-altering win that makes fans demand it again, Alalshikh will look to put his budget behind fresh pairings.

If the Saudis say no, the fight essentially dies right there. Here is why neither traditional promoters nor major streaming platforms would step into that breach:

Traditional promoters like Frank Warren’s Queensberry or Bob Arum’s Top Rank operate strictly on commercial reality. To stage Fury vs. Usyk 3 without Saudi site fees, they would have to fund massive eight-figure guarantees entirely through ticket sales, sponsorships, and pay-per-view buys.

The first two fights showed that pay-per-view numbers alone struggle to justify astronomical purses without state subsidies. Putting together $80 million to $100 million in combined purses on a pay-per-view model for a 2-0 rivalry would be financial suicide for any standalone promoter.

Netflix has entered live combat sports, but its entire strategy relies on massive cultural events and spectacle that drive mainstream global viewership without pay-per-view barriers. A technical chess match between two pure boxers, where the Ukrainian has already dominated the series, does not fit the kind of mass-market spectacle Netflix targets.

If Netflix is going to spend tens of millions on a live boxing broadcast, they will chase crossover draws or a massive domestic clash like Fury against Anthony Joshua, not a redundant third bout between Fury and Usyk.

Ghana News.title: NMC to summon nurse over alleged TikTok livestream of distressed pregnant patient
Ghana News.content:
The Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) is expected to summon a nurse for further engagement next week following a controversial TikTok livestream allegedly showing a pregnant patient in visible distress.

The incident, which has triggered concerns about patient privacy, professional conduct and the dignity of people receiving medical care, came to the attention of the Ministry of Health after a post by a concerned individual on social media.

The Ministry’s Public Relations Officer, Tony Goodman, disclosed the Council’s planned action in a Facebook post on Friday, October 6, saying he had been reliably informed that the nurse was expected to be invited for further engagement.

“The Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) is following up on the matter concerning this nurse. I am reliably informed that she is expected to be invited by the Council next week for further engagement,” he wrote.

Livestream sparks outrage

A Facebook user, Dickson Assan, who reported the incident to the Ghana Health Service (GHS), said he came across the TikTok Live session in the early hours of the day and was disturbed by what he witnessed.

The host, who appeared to be a nurse, was broadcasting a visibly distressed pregnant patient, he posted.

He said that during the livestream, the host was seen rubbing the patient’s back, apparently to comfort her. However, the movement attracted inappropriate comments and mockery from some viewers, according to the user.

He said the situation became more troubling when a viewer raised concerns about the appropriateness of the broadcast, only to be met with insults from other participants.

The Facebook user also alleged that the host had displayed a Mobile Money (MoMo) number on the livestream and solicited contributions from viewers while the patient was in distress.

He questioned the conduct of a healthcare worker who, instead of protecting the privacy of a vulnerable patient, appeared to be turning the situation into social media content and an opportunity to solicit money.

Ghana News.title: Meghan’s father Thomas Markle appears in court over child sex abuse material
Ghana News.content:
Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, has appeared in court after being charged over possession of child sex abuse material.

Markle was arrested on a federal complaint alleging he held images that show child sex abuse, the US Department of Justice (DoJ) said.

The 82-year-old was arrested in Florida after the FBI searched two Los Angeles-area storage units he rented for almost 20 years.

He is charged with one count of possessing indecent images of children, the US Department of Justice (DoJ) said. Markle has previously denied allegations of possessing images of child sex abuse, calling them "sick lies".

Markle's court hearing lasted for 30 minutes, and the charges were laid out against him by federal prosecutor Courtenay Derry, according to the BBC's US partner CBS News.

He was brought into court in a wheelchair, escorted by two US Marshals. Markle was wearing black trousers and a black T-shirt.

The court ordered Markle to submit to home detention at his assisted living facility in Florida and electronic monitoring.

No plea was taken during the hearing, and an arraignment date in California will be determined in due course, a joint statement from the DoJ and the US Attorney's Office Central California said.

The Duke and Duchess of Sussex have not commented on Markle's arrest.

FBI director Kash Patel said authorities "moved quickly" when arresting Markle.

"Mr Markle allegedly targeted innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions," Patel said.

He added that the FBI would "use every single resource at our disposal to protect innocent kids – any predator who targets children will have zero safe haven in this country or anywhere they try to hide".

Markle was arrested after the FBI, acting on warrants, searched storage units in LA registered to him which he had rented since 2008, with the last payment being made in October this year.

Inside the units the FBI says agents seized about 78 items, including film negatives, slides and books that they allege contained child sex abuse material.

Thomas Markle appeared in court on Friday

Witnesses "positively identified" Markle in two of the images believed to contain child sex abuse material.

In those images, the man pictured "appears to be in the age range of 30s to 40s", which suggests the alleged abuse dates back decades as Markle is currently 82 years old.

Last month, police in the Philippines obtained a warrant to examine devices allegedly removed from Markle's former home in the country.

Four boxes of material, including computers, phones, hard drives and old video tapes, were handed to officers by Meghan's half brother Thomas Markle Jr.

Markle Sr moved to the Philippines last year after he had a series of strokes, and lived in Cebu until May. He was then reportedly living in a Florida rehabilitation centre learning to walk again after having his leg amputated.

In October, London's Metropolitan Police confirmed that it had received a letter in 2019 making a "number of claims" relating to Markle Sr.

The Met said information contained in the letter, which related to allegations against Meghan's father outside the UK, was passed on to the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, but it did not share it with other law enforcement agencies.

The force has since voluntarily referred itself to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IPOC) over its handling of the letter.

In a statement released in October after the allegations against Markle Sr emerged, the Duchess of Sussex said: "I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed."

Meghan has been estranged from her father since 2018. The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year.

Ghana News.title: Ministry condemns growing trend of sexual blackmail and non-consensual recordings
Ghana News.content:
The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection has condemned the growing circulation of intimate images and videos without consent, warning that perpetrators and those who deliberately share or repost such material could face legal consequences.

It has also urged the Ghana Police Service and other law enforcement agencies to investigate reported cases of indecent exposure, non-consensual recording and sexual blackmail, and take appropriate action against persons found to have broken the law.

In a press statement issued on Friday, November 6, 2026, the Ministry expressed concern over recurring incidents involving the unauthorised recording and distribution of intimate encounters, threats to publish private images and videos, and other forms of technology-facilitated sexual abuse.

It said the conduct violated the dignity, privacy and safety of affected persons and could expose victims to humiliation, intimidation, psychological distress, reputational damage and further exploitation.

The Ministry stressed that consent to an intimate relationship or sexual encounter did not amount to permission to record, publish or publicly expose the encounter.

“Equally, no individual has the right to use intimate images, videos or personal information to threaten, extort, humiliate or exercise control over another person,” it stated.

Reposting intimate content also attracts consequences

The Ministry expressed particular concern about the practice of circulating private images and videos on social media, sometimes accompanied by ridicule, sensational commentary and public humiliation.

It said such conduct compounded the harm suffered by victims and amounted to a further violation of their privacy and dignity.

It cautioned that the deliberate circulation or republication of intimate material without consent could also attract legal consequences, urging social media users, bloggers and content creators to exercise restraint.

“Public interest in an incident does not justify further violations of the privacy and dignity of the persons involved,” the statement said.

The Ministry cited the Criminal Offences Act, 1960 (Act 29), and the Cybersecurity Act, 2020 (Act 1038), as part of Ghana’s legal framework for addressing indecent conduct, sexual exploitation, sexual extortion and the non-consensual sharing of intimate images.

Victims urged to report incidents

The Ministry called on victims and survivors, irrespective of gender, not to give in to threats or intimidation but to report incidents to the appropriate authorities and seek assistance and protection.

It urged the police and other relevant agencies to investigate reported cases thoroughly while safeguarding victims and respecting due process.

The statement also appealed to members of the public to avoid sharing, reposting or amplifying intimate images and videos, warning that doing so could deepen the distress and humiliation of those affected.

The Ministry said it remained committed to public education, promoting responsible digital behaviour, supporting victims and survivors, and working with relevant institutions to prevent sexual exploitation, indecent exposure and other forms of technology-facilitated abuse.

It reiterated that privacy, dignity and bodily autonomy must be respected and that no one should be subjected to humiliation, exploitation or blackmail through the misuse of intimate material.

Ghana News.title: Trump names Stephen Miller as new White House chief of staff
Ghana News.content:
President Donald Trump has named Stephen Miller, the architect of his hardline immigration policy, as his new chief of staff following historic losses in the US midterm elections.

Miller replaces Susie Wiles, who submitted her resignation after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress, delivering a blow to the prospects for Trump's agenda in his final two years in the White House.

Speaking to reporters, Trump said Wiles had "done a very good job", but "we've got to make moves sometimes".

Miller, a Trump loyalist and deputy chief of staff who served as a senior adviser during his first administration, is set to take on the new role on Monday.One of Trump's closest aides, Miller, 41, stuck by the president following his 2020 election defeat and followed Trump back into power last year.

On X, Miller called Trump "the most transformative political leader in American History" who has "single-handedly saved America from those who would destroy it".

He thanked Wiles for her years of devoted service to the president, country and for her friendship.

"The mission now is more clear than ever: Fight with all of our soul to support our President and defend this magnificent Republic," he wrote.

Wiles gave her resignation to Trump on Thursday night, a US official told CBS News, the BBC's media partner. Three sources told CBS she quit because of the election losses.

Trump said in a statement that Wiles would be moved to the "Trump Political Operation". He told reporters that Miller "gets it, very good politically".

Wiles said being on Trump's team was "the honor of a lifetime".

"I'm so proud to have been a part of what we've accomplished together," she said.

"While my role may be changing, my commitment to the President and the mission never will," she added.

It was unclear if her deputies would remain at the White House.

Wiles, 69, is seen as among the most powerful figures in the Trump administration and someone particularly close to the US president.

Asked last month whether Wiles could be replaced soon, Trump said there was "zero chance".

"Susie is here and she's gonna be here for a long time," he said.

Wiles recently had cancer, announcing in September, six months after her diagnosis, that she was in remission.

Miller, on the left, and Wiles on the right, earlier this year

Wiles, 69, is seen as among the most powerful figures in the Trump administration and someone particularly close to the US president.

Asked last month whether Wiles could be replaced soon, Trump said there was "zero chance".

"Susie is here and she's gonna be here for a long time," he said.

Wiles recently had cancer, announcing in September, six months after her diagnosis, that she was in remission.

Wiles is most senior person to leave after midterms

Wiles had planned to stay in her role until the end of the year or early next year, sources familiar with her thinking told CBS News.

However, the president accelerated her departure, the sources said.

Wiles is not the only Trump administration official to leave following this week's midterm elections, which have prompted a reckoning among Republicans about how to address voters' rebuke of Trump's agenda.

Several Department of Justice (DOJ) officials who carried out some of Trump's top priorities have also resigned since Republicans' sweeping losses in Tuesday's midterm elections.

Harmeet Dhillon, the chief of the civil rights division, which focused on non-citizen voting and eliminating diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) initiatives, stepped down on Thursday. She also put a greater focus on protecting gun owners' rights and adopted legal positions that opposed civil rights protections for transgender people.

John Eisenberg, head of the department's National Security Division, who had also worked in Trump's first administration, investigated media leaks and led the division that redacted millions of pages of federal files related to convicted paedophile Jeffrey Epstein.

Jason Reding Quiñones, a US attorney in Florida, was at the centre of Trump's ​efforts to use the DOJ to prosecute perceived political foes. He investigated earlier criminal probes into Trump's handling of classified documents ​after he left office in 2021 and his campaign's contacts with Russia in the 2016 election.

Who is Stephen Miller?

Asked why he elevated Miller to chief of staff, Trump told reporters on Friday: "Stephen's been with me from the beginning. He gets it, very good politically ... and he's a very good manager. He'll do a great job."

Democrats took to social media to criticise Miller as Trump's new pick, accusing the president of doubling down despite voters' anger with his party's agenda.

Democratic Congressman Robert Garcia, who would lead the House Oversight Committee when the party takes control of the chamber, said he would continue to investigate Miller and his "misconduct".

"Stephen Miller is the architect of the unconstitutional ICE raids that have terrorized our communities and kidnapped and killed American citizens and immigrant families," he said, referencing US Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

Democratic House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Miller was "a dangerous xenophobe and reckless extremist who has American blood on his hands".

"His presence in government should be eradicated like a malignant tumor," he said.

Trump administration communications director Steven Cheung praised Miller.

"There is no bigger advocate for the Trump agenda than Stephen, and he will help the Administration deliver on monumental victories for the rest of this historic second term," he said.

Miller comes from an Ashkenazi Jewish family in Santa Monica, California. In high school, he developed a taste for politics and voiced controversial opinions.

He attended Duke University in North Carolina and, in 2009, became an aide to ultra-conservative Alabama Senator Jeff Sessions, the first senator to endorse Trump.

During this time, Miller developed his hardline immigration policies and worked to kill a bipartisan immigration reform bill. He joined Trump's presidential campaign in January 2016 and has been loyal since.

Miller spearheaded Trump's use of executive orders to advance his agenda, staunchly defending the administration's use of executive power.

He championed "zero-tolerance" family separations, drove policies behind travel bans during Trump's first term, advocated for third-country deportations and urged immigration officials to make up to 300 arrests a day.

A staunch supporter of Israel, Miller has also been hawkish about the US and Israel's joint military action in Iran.

Ghana News.title: ‘It was a total miracle’: How rejection led Sylvester Stallone to create film’s ultimate underdog Rocky
Ghana News.content:
In 1976, hit boxing drama Rocky turned its "absolutely broke" and unknown lead actor and screenwriter, Sylvester Stallone, into an A-list sensation. It's a story told in crowd-pleasing new film I Play Rocky.

A young Sylvester Stallone is homeless on the streets of New York in the early 1970s, with only his dog Butkus for company. In between auditioning for roles he never gets, he works gruelling hours gutting fish. He's laughed at for his ambition to be an actor, because being delivered by forceps at birth has left him with partial face paralysis and a speech impediment, which he tries to improve by recording and listening back to his voice.

This is the starting point of I Play Rocky, directed by Green Book's Peter Farrelly, which tells the story of how Stallone created the iconic boxing drama Rocky. It stars relative unknown Anthony Ippolito as a young Stallone, whose frustrated ambition to be an actor led him to start writing screenplays, too. In the film, we see him move to Los Angeles, where he's so poor he has to temporarily sell Butkus – who later gets a role in the film. But he drafts the story of Rocky in three days. After many challenges on the road to getting it made, Rocky became the biggest box-office hit of 1976 and won best picture at the 1977 Oscars. It's the ultimate Hollywood success story.

As Rocky Balboa, Stallone created the template for a new kind of "unstoppable" cinematic hero (Credit: Getty Images)

I Play Rocky shows why Stallone identified so strongly with Rocky Balboa, the washed-up Philadelphia boxer who takes an opportunity to fight World Heavyweight Champion Apollo Creed, even though he has virtually no chance of winning. "Stallone is the personification of an underdog himself," says Nick de Semlyen, editor of Empire film magazine, and author of The Last Action Heroes, about Stallone, Arnold Schwarzenegger and other male stars of that era. "He was absolutely broke and overnight he went to being the hottest thing in Hollywood and at the Oscars. It's hard to think of another flip [in fortune] that's as dramatic in film history."

He saw himself as a serious actor, but he wasn't taken seriously at all. So that's why he decided to write his own stories as he was so frustrated with being typecast – Nick de Semlyen

Anthony Ippolito agrees that there are strong parallels between Stallone and the character he created. "Of course there are differences, because Stallone was and is a very talented writer. He reads a lot and is more of a thinker than Rocky perhaps appears in the film. But it's semi-autobiographical in a lot of ways."

How the script came about

In his recent memoir The Steps, Stallone himself describes the moment when the inspiration for the Rocky took hold, based on his own struggles to make it as an actor. Writing the script, he felt that others would relate to his and the character's feelings of rejection.

"I couldn't possibly be the only person out of billions of people to feel like they were living life in desperate frustration because the door of golden opportunity had been shut in their face over and over," he writes.

Stallone had started acting at college, but the biggest job of his career until then had been a supporting role in The Lords of Flatbush, a film with Henry Winkler, later The Fonz of Happy Days. He had also starred in a soft porn film in 1970 to pay his bills. "He saw himself as a serious actor, but he wasn't taken seriously at all," says de Semlyen. "He was into poetry, he was a big Edgar Allen Poe fan, but he kept being cast as a thug. So that's why he decided to write his own stories as he was so frustrated with being typecast. And he was willing this stuff into existence with Rocky from a place of having absolutely no power in the industry whatsoever. It's a total miracle this film got off the ground."

I Play Rocky sees relative unknown Anthony Ippolito give a remarkably accurate impression of a young Stallone (Credit: Amazon MGM Studios)

"Sylvester Stallone knew Rocky was essentially his only shot at what he wanted," Ippolito tells the BBC. "He was coming up to 30 years old, he'd been trying to make it in the industry for quite a while, and I think he viewed Rocky as 'this is it' for him."

In I Play Rocky, the studio United Artists offers Stallone increasing sums to sell the script, just as long as he lets an A-lister of the era, such as Burt Reynolds or Ryan O'Neal, take the title role. But Stallone was determined that he and he alone should play Balboa. In reality, there are conflicting accounts of how much money he was offered for the script – Stallone himself has said it was $360,000. But, as broke as he was, he wouldn't budge.

Eventually the film was made with him as Balboa, but the budget was only around $1m, a fraction of what its independent producers Irwin Winkler and Robert Chartoff had wanted. Their deal with the studio stipulated that if the film was shot cheaply enough, they would have total control over casting. But it was a risk for everyone involved to attempt a boxing drama with a shoestring budget and an untried, unknown leading man.

The legendary shoot

Rocky was shot at breakneck speed in 28 days by director John G Avildsen. The shoot has became legendary in film history. Most scenes had to be done in one take to save money, and with no special effects budget, Stallone permanently damaged his knuckles creating the scene where Rocky punches sides of frozen meat.

"Throughout the shoot no one really believed in Stallone," de Semlyen says. "When it was finished, the studio didn't like it, they didn't give it a big marketing push, it didn't go to the Cannes Film Festival or any event like it. It was only when they started screening it to people, they were actually quite surprised that people were connecting to it."

Rocky went on to get 10 Oscar nominations and win three, including best picture, while Stallone himself was nominated for best actor and best original screenplay. It also generated a host of sequels, some of which Stallone directed himself, and, more recently, the hugely successful spin-off Creed films starring Michael B Jordan. Stallone has also spoken about an idea to write a Rocky prequel.

Rocky's such a feel-good movie because he doesn't have to win in the end. When Apollo Creed knocks Rocky down, Rocky says, 'Come on, I can take more' – Mike Sielski

With Rocky, de Semlyen says that Stallone created a new kind of stubborn underdog hero who has been a cornerstone of cinema ever since.

"Rocky doesn't give up, he just won't," he says. "There'd been action movies before that, obviously, but there was something about foregrounding this one man, and the idea of one unstoppable force that was quite new. You see that repeated in so many different action films after that. The idea of resilience, of not backing down, would go on to be the fundamental tenet of these movies up to this day."

Why the story has proved so powerful

Journalist Mike Sielski is the author of Going the Distance, a book about the making of Rocky. He tells the BBC that the story itself has "its own staying power, because the story of Stallone and Rocky is this underdog story on both levels. People want to believe the absolute utmost about what [Stallone] went through to make this film."

Stallone with actress Beatrice Straight at the 1977 Oscars, where Rocky won best picture (Credit: Getty Images)

He also points out that Rocky is all the more powerful for its radical ending, which goes against the Hollywood grain by having Rocky Balboa lose his fight with Creed. "That's why it's such a feel-good movie, because he doesn't have to win in the end. When Apollo Creed knocks Rocky down, Rocky says, 'Come on, I can take more'. We all want to think of ourselves as being Rocky at that moment. 'You cannot keep us down.' It taps into something of human nature that we want to see ourselves that way."Indeed, Sielski believes that Rocky was such a phenomenon in the US because its heroic underdog spirit chimed with a society which, in 1976, was "hungry for a reason to feel good again.

"There had been the Watergate scandal, there was Vietnam," he continues. "The films of that era were all about antiheroes, especially if you think of the films that were nominated [for Oscars] in 1977 with Rocky – Taxi Driver, which has no hero in the movie, or Network, which was a satirical take on the anger America was feeling.

"Sometimes you have these situations in culture where you don't know people are hungry for something and nobody's providing it. And then when one entity or person or institution does, it's an explosion. That's what happened with Rocky."

I Play Rocky is released on 6 November 2026, in the UK, Ireland and North America.

Ghana News.title: Self-styled ‘king of Germany’ goes on trial accused of heading criminal group
Ghana News.content:
A self-declared "king" of Germany has gone on trial in Düsseldorf accused of leading a criminal organisation along with three other men described as his senior "subjects".

Peter Fitzek, 61, who calls himself Peter the First, is a member of a bannedReichsbürger (Citizens of the Reich) group that sought to set up a "Kingdom of Germany" (KRD).

Reichsbürger are defined by German intelligence agencies as conspiracy theorists who reject the existence and legitimacy of the post-war German state.

The defendants are accused of plotting against Germany by seeking to establish the structures of an alternative state, including a banking and insurance system and currency.

Fitzek denies committing a crime.

The defendants, including Fitzek and three other men identified only as Benjamin M, Mathias B and Martin S, face up to 10 years in prison.

Speaking just before the trial began, Fitzek criticised his detention as a violation of human rights: "They are isolating me completely."

In 2012, Fitzek, a former chef and karate instructor, declared himself "supreme sovereign" of the "kingdom" and had himself crowned, dressed in ermine robes and brandishing a medieval sword.

He began buying land and property across the country. With around 6,000 members, the KRD became the largest Reichsbürger and self-governance group in Germany.

In 2025, Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt banned the KRD, and Fitzek and the other three suspects were taken into custody.

Prosecutors accuse the group of founding the KRD "to replace the 'system' of the Federal Republic of Germany". According to the indictment, Fitzek and his deputies assumed the status of "divine beings" and issued legal decrees.

The prosecutors allege the organisation operated a banking and insurance system with branches in Dresden, Ulm, Menden and Lutherstadt Wittenberg, as well as a "registration office" that issued fake identity documents and its own currency.

Further charges include organised forgery and tax evasion amounting to millions of euros.

In just five years up to 2025, the KRD is alleged to have taken in about €10m (£8.25m) through unauthorised banking and insurance transactions, as well as via donations, gifts and fee-based seminars.

Prosecutors say these revenues were not declared to the tax authorities and that no income tax or social security contributions were paid on behalf of employees.

They said the KRD accepted substantial donations, including cash, land and 7kg of gold, but did not pay any gift tax.

The KRD is also accused of recruiting other companies by promising them that they would be able to operate free of tax and duties.

In an interview with the BBC in 2022, Fitzek denied having any violent intentions, but labelled the German state as "destructive and sick".

Intelligence services believe some 26,000 people are part of Reichsbürger organisations in Germany.

The groups are very diverse, and intelligence services say a small minority are right-wing extremists and potentially violent.

In a separate case in 2022, dozens of people were arrested, many of them Reichsbürger, for plotting to overthrow the German government in Berlin.

They were accused of planning a violent coup, which included kidnapping the health minister, to create "civil war conditions" to bring down German democracy.

Five people were jailed last year over that plot.

Ghana News.title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff
Ghana News.content:
Is the artificial intelligence (AI) gold rush coming to an end, or is this simply a reality check?

That's the question which is hanging over investors, and which has prompted steep falls on the world's stock markets.

The sell-off in the US on Thursday was most dramatic on the Nasdaq, home to tech industry titans such as Alphabet, Nvidia, Meta and Apple.

It followed sweeping gains by the Democrats in this week's midterm elections in the US, which have given the party full control of Congress.

A number of leading Democrats campaigned against the unhindered expansion of data centres, which have underpinned the growth of artificial intelligence.

Fears this will lead to more regulation of AI appear to have concerned investors. But worries about the industry's prospects have been growing for some time.

AI boom

The release of Chat GPT by Open AI in late 2022 is widely seen as having generated massive public and corporate interest in the practical uses of AI. It also sparked a modern-day gold rush.

Investors flocked to put their money into companies producing computer chips and networking infrastructure, building data centres and providing the energy to power them, as well as developing the AI itself. The value of tech companies soared.

The boom continued into this year. Investments in AI are expected to reach $1trillion in 2026 alone according to research by Goldman Sachs. The sector has scooped up so much available cash that other industries have seen their own borrowing costs increase as a result.

But investors want returns, and in recent months concerns have been growing about whether the AI boom can produce the expected riches.

Those worries have emerged at a time when public comments from AI researchers casting doubt over the safety of artificial intelligence - even suggesting it could represent an existential threat to humanity - have been grabbing headlines and fuelling speculation that a clampdown could lie ahead.

Democrat opposition

While the Trump administration has been all-in on AI, or "super intelligence" as the president likes to call it, many leading Democrats tapped into grassroots concerns about the expansion of data centres and their impact on local communities.

These were largely focused on the facilities' high consumption of water and electricity, which many feared would push up their household bills – as well as the noise, use of land, and general disruption associated with them.

A Gallup poll published in May showed 71% of Americans would oppose the building of a data centre in their community. The figure for a nuclear power station was 53%.

James Talarico, who won the Senate race in once staunchly Republican Texas, was one of those to respond to this scepticism.

"While we want to protect America's leadership in artificial intelligence, we are still grappling with how it will affect everything from how we work to how our children learn," he said.

"We must protect Americans and establish clear, consistent laws for businesses."

With control of both houses of Congress, Democrats are now expected to challenge the president's technology agenda more vigorously, while introducing legislation which could curb the expansion of the industry.

Texas' Democratic governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned against data centres, pledging a moratorium on the construction of new facilities.

Hinojosa's win could present opposition to tech multi-billionaire Elon Musk, who has moved large parts of SpaceX and Tesla's operations to the state, for years a Republican stronghold.

The Tesla boss had spent nearly $450m to back Republican campaigns in the midterms.

Where next for stocks?

As the co-founder of the British-based technology firm Arm Holdings, Tudor Brown, points out, "stock values are based on future earnings not present earnings". If the rewards are not likely to be as great as expected, some investors will choose to sell up.

The falls seen on stock markets over the past 24 hours would appear to have been triggered by the midterm results. But concerns that tech firms have become overvalued were being expressed long before the elections.

The question now is whether this is simply the removal of froth from an over-exuberant market, or a sign that the AI rush is a bubble about to burst, with much wider consequences.

Nandini Roy Choudhury of Future Market Insights thinks investors will assess whether the political shift could result in restrictions on data centre construction, energy consumption and the deployment of AI technology.

She adds there is unlikely to be an immediate widespread recovery in tech stocks as traders are likely to be more selective, favouring firms with stronger balance sheets.

Brown thinks the impact will be limited. Share valuations, he thinks, were inflated by expectations of "almost infinite AI growth", which have been followed by "a bit of a panic".

"There is a natural floor to this", he says. "After that it will reflect I think that actually there's still a lot of money being made in these companies".

Ghana News.title: NDC reschedules submission of national executive nomination forms to 12 noon on November 7
Ghana News.content:
The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has rescheduled the submission of nomination forms for its 2026 National Executive Elections from 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 noon on Saturday, November 7.

The Congress Elections Committee announced the adjustment in a statement on Friday, November 6, citing the party’s participation in the monthly National Clean-Up Exercise scheduled for the same day.

The committee said the decision was taken to accommodate the exercise, which coincides with the original time scheduled for aspirants to begin submitting their completed nomination forms.

It has consequently advised all aspirants contesting the national executive positions to take note of the revised commencement time and make the necessary arrangements.

The submission exercise will continue at the NDC National Headquarters under the previously announced arrangements.

The statement was issued by Dr Peter Boamah Otokunor, spokesperson for the Congress Elections Committee.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
