World.title: Musokotwane presents k284.8 billion 2027 budget
World.content:
Minister of Finance and National Planning Situmbeko Musokotwane has presented a proposed National Budget of 284.8 billion kwacha for the year 2027, equivalent to 28.4 percent of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

Dr Musokotwane says 2027 will be highly financed through domestic revenues of about K233.7 billion, representing 82.1 percent of the total budget.

Speaking when he presented the 2027 national budget in Parliament today, Dr Musokotwane added another source of financing will be borrowing from domestic and external sources amounting to K41.9 billion, representing 14.7 percent of the total budget.

Dr Musokotwane highlighted one of the government’s strategic focus since 2021 has been to strengthen fiscal sustainability through improved resource mobilisation and expenditure rationalisation.

Presenting the 2027 National budget expenditure, Dr Musokotwane revealed that about 90.5 billion kwachas will go towards general public services, 75.9 billion to economic affairs, while over K38.2 billion kwacha will be spent on education, a sector that has been given the highest allocation of the total budget at 13.4 percent.

Meanwhile, the health sector has been allocated K30.3 billion, representing 10.6 percent of the Budget on the health function.

To strengthen social protection and reduce vulnerability, Dr Musokotwane proposed an expenditure of K16.2 billion or 5.7 percent of the Budget, of which K10.4 billion will be spent on the Social Cash Transfer programme to support over 1.6 million beneficiary households up from 1.5 million in the 2026 Budget.

“The monthly transfer will be increased to K450 for eligible beneficiary households and K650 for households with eligible persons with disabilities. K5.2 billion will be spent on the public service pension funds to reduce waiting time from retirement to when the pension is paid,” he said.

As part of the government’s commitment to strengthen domestic revenues, Dr Musokotwane proposed adjustments in various taxation including the Value Added Tax rate that he proposed to adjust from 16 percent to 16.5.

The Minister also proposed to increase Corporate Income Tax rates by 5 percentage points on all income currently taxed at 20 percent and below.

“To rationalise the company tax regime which is currently characterised by preferential rates and arbitrage, I propose to increase Corporate Income Tax rates by 5 percentage points on all income currently taxed at 20 percent and below. This measure will ensure neutrality, fairness and alignment of the tax system,” he stated.

He also proposed to increase withholding tax on dividends paid by mining companies to 15 percent from zero percent, noting that this will align with tax treatment of dividends distributed by companies in other sectors.

Other tax adjustments by Dr Musokotwane was the proposal to introduce a top marginal rate of 39.5 percent PAYE tax for individuals earning above K37,000 per month.

He explained that those earning K37,000 per month and below will continue to be taxed under the current regime and will therefore not be affected by this measure.

Meanwhile, to lower capital costs and enhance Zambia’s competitiveness as a high value tourism destination, Dr Musokotwane proposed to suspend customs duty on safari vehicles, hospitality equipment and communications infrastructure.

The theme for the 2027 Budget is: Grow Zambia: From Stabilisation to Unlocking Opportunities, Creating Jobs and Improving Livelihoods for All.

The Budget presented provides a clear policy direction with specific interventions to achieve the Grow Zambia Agenda and will require concerted efforts from various stakeholders.

World.title: Engineers challenged to catalyze Grow Zambia Agenda
World.content:
Government has urged engineers to play a pivotal role in contributing to the achievement of the Grow Zambia Agenda through quality infrastructure development.

Ministry of Infrastructure and Urban Development Permanent Secretary

Albert Malama, said infrastructure remains a key driver of economic growth, and engineers are at the centre of delivering the projects that will transform the country.

Mr Malama said this when he officiated at the second annual public forum for the Association of Consulting Engineers of Zambia (ACEZ) on construction contracts held at Urban Hotel in Lusaka.

He said the government recognises the important role that professional bodies such as ACEZ play in supporting national development, and values their expertise and technical guidance in the infrastructure sector.

“Government recognises the important role that professional bodies such as the Association of Consulting Engineers of Zambia play in supporting national development, and values their expertise and technical guidance,” Mr Malama said.

He noted that the successful delivery of infrastructure requires collaboration, mutual understanding and clearly defined responsibilities among different stakeholders.

Mr Malama commended ACEZ for bringing together engineers, lawyers, quantity surveyors, architects, procurement specialists and contractors to discuss the distinctive nature of construction contracts.

He said challenges in the construction industry cannot be addressed by one profession in isolation, and the forum had created an opportunity for a more balanced and holistic discussion.

“A project can encounter serious challenges if the contractual arrangements are poorly understood or inadequately administered,” Mr Malama said.

He cited issues relating to risk allocation, payment obligations, variations, extensions of time, design responsibilities and dispute resolution as having significant implications on project delivery and quality.

Mr Malama urged engineers to appreciate the distinctive nature of construction contracts, as this will ensure projects are delivered on time, within budget and to the required quality key to achieving the Grow Zambia Agenda.

The forum was held under the ACEZ core values of transparency, accountability, dynamism, innovation, equity and sustainability.

Meanwhile ACEZ president Trephor Musonda appreciated government for the support shown to the association.

He said the association was encouraged to receive positive response from government to officiate the event.

World.title: Zambia, US Deepen collaboration in conservation
World.content:
Zambia and US have agreed to deepen private sector investment in Zambia’s green economy, focusing on wildlife conservation, electric mobility and sustainable agri-food systems

The Minister of Green Economy and Environment Gilbert Siame has since invited US investors to partner with government in developing sustainable businesses that will benefit the investors, and local communities,

Speaking when US Embassy Charge d’Affaires Mick Coker paid a courtesy call on him at his office, Dr Siame said Zambia needs to turn its bilateral relationship with the US into practical investments.

Dr Siame highlighted nature based tourism and wildlife conservation as key opportunities, stressing the need for investment models that share benefits fairly and protect natural resources while preventing wildlife crime.

He also identified electric mobility and sustainable agri-food systems as priorities, noting the President’s directive for public electric vehicles creates opportunities for electric cars, charging stations and improved food production.

Meanwhile Charge d’Affaires Mich Coker reaffirmed the longstanding relationship between Zambia and the United States, describing it as built on decades of mutual respect, shared values and common interests.

Mr Coker opportunities for deeper cooperation, particularly through American companies bringing innovation, technology and expertise to support Zambia’s development priorities.

He further expressed interest in exploring cooperation in the immediate, medium and long term developments advancing the Grow Zambia Agenda, adding that shared interests provide a strong foundation for advancing bilateral engagements.

World.title: Govt. targets 2 million hectares of land for LIFE Project
World.content:
Government is targeting 2 million hectares of land for the Lobito Corridor Integrated Forest Economy (LIFE) Project.

Minister of Green Economy and Environment, Gilbert Siame, says government is in a hurry to kick start the project in the first quarter of 2027.

Dr Siame disclosed this when a team from the World Bank Group paid a courtesy call on him at his office in Lusaka today, as part of the Bank’s appraisal mission covering Lusaka and Copperbelt Provinces.

The Minister called for the accelerated preparation of the project since discussions, design and investment plans have already been agreed.

He said the LIFE Project provides an opportunity to translate President Hakainde Hichilema’s Grow Zambia Agenda into practical investments in the forest economy by expanding productive forestry, restoring degraded landscapes,

attracting private investment and strengthening local processing and value addition.

Dr Siame also encouraged the private companies, financial institutions, cooperatives, women and young entrepreneurs to identify investment opportunities and build partnerships, including out grower schemes to realise the project.

He is optimistic that the World Bank Group will soon approve the LIFE project to help spur economic growth in the country.

And World Bank Group Country Manager for Zambia, Martine Valcin, said the Bank is ready to help Zambia achieve her goal in line with the Grow Zambia Agenda.

Ms Valcin said the LIFE Project would reward communities by protecting and restoring natural forests and attracting results-based climate finance.

The meeting was attended by Zambia Forestry and Forest Industries Corporation (ZAFFICO), senior government and bank officials on talks surrounding the forest ecosystem and economy.

World.title: CCPC calls for strong collaboration with the media
World.content:
The Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (CCPC) has called for stronger collaboration with the media to improve public understanding and reporting of competition and consumer protection matters.

CCPC Executive Director, Eunice Hamavhwa, says limited media coverage and occasional misinterpretation of the Commission’s regulatory decisions, highlight the need for greater awareness of its mandate and operations.

Ms Hamavhwa was speaking during a one day Media Training Workshop for journalists on the mandate of the CCPC in Lusaka.

“The Commission has organised a media training workshop to equip journalists with a better understanding of its legal framework, enforcement processes and broader responsibilities,” she said.

She noted that accurate and balanced reporting is essential in raising public awareness of consumer rights and promoting fair competition in the Zambian economy.

Ms Hamavhwa has also appealed to journalists to take greater interest in competition issues.

“You should take interest in cartels, abuse of market dominance, mergers and acquisitions, as well as unfair business practices that affect consumers,” Ms Hamavhwa said.

Ms Hamavhwa further said that the Commission would like to strengthen its working relationship with the media through increased engagement and information sharing.

World.title: Construction of bulking centre elates Luwingu farmers
World.content:
Small scale farmers in Chief Tungatis Chiefdom in Luwingu district in Northern Province says the construction of a bulking centre in the area has ensured a secure storage for their crops.

Fikonkonta Marketing Centre Secretary, Sylvester Kamfwa, says small scale farmers previously lacked a secure storage and central trading area.

He told the media in an interview in Luwingu district that the construction of fikonkonta marketing centre with support from World Vision Zambia has made it easy for the farmers to secure their farm produce.

“We used to have challenges with storage of crops, some farmers used to make post-harvest losses but now we have a secure storage facility,” Mr Kamfwa explained.

He added that the 10 000 capacity storage has made it easy for farmers to have a uniform price of crops which are on sale.

“Before the construction of this bulking centre, farmers would keep their produce in their homes and would sell their crops at different prices but now, we normally set prices for specific crops,” Mr Kamfwa added.

Meanwhile, Mercy Ngosa, a small-scale farmer, said the construction of the centre has motivated more women to venture into farming.

She said the use of scales to price products enables farmers to get an income which is equal to their input.

“As women, we feel motivated to work hard and produce enough because we now see the benefit that comes with farming, we have a storage facility making it easy to ensure our crops are safe,” she explained.

Ms Ngosa has, however, appealed to government to link the bulking centre with ready markets such as schools and hospitals.

World.title: Chilengi calls for prioritisation of community development in malaria elimination
World.content:
Minister of Health, Roma Chilengi, has called on governments to prioritise community development as a long-term strategy for eliminating malaria, noting that poverty and underdevelopment contribute to the persistence of the disease.

Professor Chilengi made the remarks during the High-Level Dialogue on Malaria Elimination in Botswana, which he attended on behalf of President Hakainde Hichilema.

Prof Chilengi said although enhanced surveillance, improved case management and targeted interventions remain important in controlling malaria, governments should also address the underlying developmental challenges that contribute to its transmission.

Speaking during the Ministerial Perspectives on Alignment, Delivery and Resilience, the Minister observed that countries which have successfully eliminated malaria share a common pattern of sustained development, stating that the disease is less prevalent in developed urban areas.

He said there is a historical correlation between the global distribution of malaria and poverty, adding that addressing development inequalities will significantly contribute to efforts to eliminate the disease.

Prof Chilengi has warned that environmental and financial challenges undermine malaria control efforts and lead to the disease re-emerging when countries experience disruptions to their interventions.

“When we are shaken, Malaria simply comes back again, but I think the one thing we must not lose sight of as governments is to focus our attention on developing our communities and our population and Malaria will go away,” he said.

The Minister further stressed the need to strengthen surveillance systems to ensure timely detection and response to malaria cases, particularly in areas where transmission persisted.

He has called for targeted interventions to interrupt transmission by identifying and treating infected individuals, thereby limiting the spread of the disease through mosquito vectors.

Prof Chilengi has advised countries to maintain their commitment to effective malaria control measures, placing greater emphasis on sustainable development as the foundation for lasting elimination.

This is in a statement issued to the media by the First Secretary for Press at the Zambia High Commission in Gaborone, Botswana, Julia Malunga.

World.title: Africa: CANEX Aims to Empower African Creatives to Compete in Global Markets and Drive Economic Growth
World.content:
CANEX WKND 2026 opens in Lagos, Nigeria, an initiative of the Afreximbank aimed at boosting creatives from across the African continent.

Creatives from across the continent are gathering in Lagos, Nigeria, for the Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX). This initiative brings together Africa's creative talent, investors, policymakers, and industry leaders to unlock the economic potential of the continent's cultural industries.

Dubbed CANEX WKND, the four-day event attracted more than 15,000 registrations from across the global creative community, under the theme "One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World."

Hosted by the Federal Government of Nigeria and organised by the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) through its Creative Africa Nexus programme, the event runs from 5 to 8 November. It aims to transform Africa's growing cultural influence into sustainable businesses, increased trade, investment, and employment opportunities.



"CANEX was established to offer a comprehensive suite of solutions aimed at developing the capacity of Africa's creators and enhancing the value retained within the continent, through CANEX finance," said Dr George Elombi, President and Chairman of the Board of Directors of Afreximbank.

From film and television to music, fashion, publishing, sport, gastronomy, and visual arts, CANEX WKND is positioning the creative economy as an increasingly important contributor to Africa's economic transformation.

For a continent with the world's youngest population, the creative industries offer significant opportunities to harness the talents, innovation, and entrepreneurial ambitions of young people. However, translating this potential into sustainable livelihoods requires more than talent and international recognition. It requires access to finance, skills development, markets, technology, and the commercial infrastructure necessary to build viable businesses.

This is the gap Afreximbank's CANEX initiative seeks to address.

The bank recognises that financing is not the industry's only challenge; a holistic approach is needed for the industry to thrive.

"We can put financing skills into music and movie productions, yet the value we derive could still be low. We must, therefore, focus on building the creative ecosystem, focusing not just on idea generation, creation, and production, but particularly on value capture from those activities that we now know attract the greatest value. These include vending and production, and CANEX was created for that purpose," said Elombi.

He noted that the budget has increased significantly since CANEX started to meet the needs and demands.

"When CANEX began, we had a budget of U. S$500 million for the creative economy. We soon found out that it was too small, so we raised it to U.S. $ 1 billion, and that was also too small. In 2024, we raised it to U.S.$2 billion," he noted.

One of the key discussions of this event is to encourage creatives and provide a platform for practical discussions on financing creative enterprises, commercialising intellectual property, and strengthening the continent's position in global creative markets.

"Africa already has its cultural influence; our challenge is to build economic power. Look at Afrobeats, Nollywood, our fashion, literature, and visual arts: our creativity is thriving more than ever before. However, recognition is not the same thing as ownership, and global popularity does not automatically translate into prosperity," noted legendary Nigerian actor Richard Mofe-Damijo.

Mofe-Damijo emphasised the need for access to better finance, stronger protection for intellectual property, reliable institutions that work, and businesses that can grow beyond success stories.

Financing will also take centre stage at the Creative Economy Finance Summit, presented by Afreximbank in partnership with the Creative Economy Practice at Co-Creation Hub. The summit will bring together financial institutions and investors to examine how creative-economy transactions can be structured, financed and de-risked.

Among many topics, discussions will also explore one of the world's most compelling topics, artificial intelligence, examining how African creatives can leverage digital technologies to develop products capable of competing internationally.

Close 

On the list of prominent figures from across the continent and diaspora are Nobel Laureate and writer Professor Wole Soyinka, Emmy Award-winning actor Uzo Aduba, filmmaker and actor Funke Akindele, actors Richard Mofe-Damijo and Thuso Mbedu, and former professional footballers Didier Drogba and Jay-Jay Okocha, musicians Davido, Fally Ipupa, Flavour, Libianca and Charlotte Dipanda.

Cultural ministers from across the continent are also in attendance, including from Côte d'Ivoire, South Africa, and Rwanda, alongside representatives from the International Finance Corporation and Afreximbank.

Speakers highlighted that strengthening access to financing, protecting intellectual property, and improving distribution channels are essential for African creatives to compete internationally and retain a greater share of the value they generate. For Afreximbank, supporting the creative industries is also part of a wider strategy to diversify African economies, promote intra-African trade, and strengthen the continent's participation in global markets.

World.title: Kenya: Kenya Cult Leader Paul Mackenzie Sentenced to 200 Years
World.content:
Paul Mackenzie was found guilty in October of the murder of 190 children.

A court in Kenya has sentenced Paul Mackenzie to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and an adult. He told them to starve themselves to death as part of his apocalyptic religious cult.

Kenyan religious sect leader Paul Mackenzie was sentenced to 200 years in prison on Friday, at the culmination of a trial following the discovery of hundreds of corpses in the woods.

A self-proclaimed pastor and longstanding leader of a new age Christian apocalyptic cult called the Good News International Church, Mackenzie was convicted in October of 191 counts of murder in the deaths of one adult and 190 children.

Justice Diana Kavedza said the sentence was comprised of 100 years for 183 counts of murder by starvation and another 100 years for eight counts of murder by direct homicide.

He could have faced the death penalty, which is still technically on the books in Kenya.

However, like several countries that have kept capital punishment in their legal code but stopped actually using it, Kenya has not executed anybody since 1987.

While the charges against Mackenzie pertained to 191 deaths, some 400 people were found dead in what became known as the "Shakahola Forest Massacre." Mackenzie's so-called church had been operating since 2003, based in the coastal town of Malindi.

Mackenzie had denied the charges, saying that he did not force the cult followers to starve.

A total of 28 accomplices were given various prison sentences for their roles in the deaths.

World.title: Tanzania: Tanzania Opposition Leader Lissu Cleared of Treason but Jailed for Incitement
World.content:
A Tanzanian court on Friday sentenced opposition leader Tundu Lissu to four years in jail for inciting unrest, after earlier in the day clearing him of treason - meaning he avoided a possible death sentence. The verdict follows a disputed presidential election and a deadly crackdown on protesters, in a case that has drawn international condemnation and raised concerns about political freedom in the country.

A panel of three judges at the High Court in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania's commercial capital, convicted the 58-year-old leader of the country's main opposition party, Chadema, over remarks he made calling for electoral reforms.

"We are satisfied that through his statements, the accused intended to disrupt elections and instigate violence," a judge told a courtroom packed with supporters, French news agency AFP reported.



Lissu has been detained since April 2025. He has denied any wrongdoing, arguing that his campaign was lawful and the charges against him politically motivated.

Facing heavy security, Tanzania protesters fear repeat of election violence

Campaign in the dock

His arrest came six months before the October 2025 vote, shortly after he launched a drive for changes to Tanzania's electoral system under the slogan "No Reforms, No Election".

Prosecutors argued that his statements were intended to disrupt the vote and threaten the government, amounting to treason.

Lissu, a lawyer who represented himself during the trial, maintained that his comments had been taken out of context and that he had committed no crime.

"My hope is that you will carry that heavy historical burden without bias, with courage and with the dignity carried by your judicial oaths," he told the panel in his closing arguments.

Tanzania's Hassan makes historic Russia visit amid frayed ties with West

Criticism abroad

The trial drew criticism from British and European Union lawmakers, who described it as politically driven and called for Lissu's immediate release.

"The use of capital punishment against a political opponent risks turning the justice system into an instrument of political repression," they wrote in a letter to President Samia Suluhu Hassan.

Security was tightened across Dar es Salaam and around the courthouse ahead of Friday's verdict, as Lissu's supporters gathered for the hearing.

Groups were mobilising to travel to the city, police said on Wednesday, warning against "those who want to stage a coup".

Elections, coups and crackdowns: Africa's mixed democratic record in 2025

Close 

Death toll in dispute

Lissu's arrest, Chadema's disqualification and alleged abductions of government critics helped fuel protests during last year's presidential election.

Hassan won with 98 percent of the vote after her two main challengers, including Lissu, were excluded. The opposition dismissed the result as a "mockery" of democracy.

A government-appointed commission put the death toll at at least 518, blaming protesters for the violence. Opposition groups and human rights organisations say the authorities killed thousands.

Accusations that security forces used excessive force have been rejected by the government. The election was fair and transparent, Hassan has insisted, blaming foreigners for the unrest.

World.title: Namibia: Distance No Longer a Death Sentence
World.content:
Namibia's air ambulance is expected to reduce some journeys that take hours by road to minutes or a few short hours by air, depending on the distance and emergency.

A 12-year-old boy who needed urgent medical attention died while waiting to be transferred from Katima Mulilo to Windhoek, a tragedy that has now become one of the reasons behind Namibia's first State-owned air ambulance service.

The boy's death, followed by the loss of patients who could not be transported quickly enough after a road accident along the Otjiwarongo road, exposed the cost of delays in Namibia's emergency healthcare system.

Health minister Esperance Luvindao recounted the painful experiences on Wednesday as the country officially launched its first State-owned air ambulance service,

a move expected to reduce the time critically ill and injured patients spend travelling to specialised hospitals.



"Unfortunately, in the early hours of the next morning, I got a call that this 12-year-old boy had passed away," Luvindao said, recalling the incident involving the patient from Katima Mulilo.

"This was heartbreaking. Because I knew that a young life had just been lost," she narrated. The minister said another emergency occurred in April 2026 when a road accident along the Otjiwarongo road left patients needing urgent transportation to Windhoek. "Unfortunately, this was not possible and lives were lost," she said.

The experiences, she said, forced the health ministry to look for solutions that could save lives while the government continues with plans to build more hospitals.

The launch, officiated by Vice President Lucia Witbooi in Windhoek, marks a major change in how the country intends to respond to medical emergencies, particularly in remote areas where patients face long journeys to reach referral hospitals.

For patients who need urgent specialist care, the difference between reaching a hospital in time and waiting hours could determine whether they survive.

Witbooi said the service was intended to ensure that a person's chances of survival were not determined by where they live.

"No Namibian should lose their life simply because they live far from a hospital," she said.

She added that the country's vast geographical size and the distance between remote communities and referral hospitals had long created challenges for emergency medical care.

The air ambulance is expected to reduce some journeys that take hours by road to minutes or a few short hours by air, depending on the distance and emergency.

The service includes a Learjet air ambulance equipped with medical equipment to provide critical care during flights.

Government Air Transport Services will provide aircraft and pilots in collaboration with the ministries of health and works and transport. It will also use helicopter evacuation services through cooperation with the Namibian Police and the Namibian Defence forces to respond to emergencies in areas where helicopters are needed.

Specialised medical personnel will accompany patients requiring urgent care, while emergency service centres at national referral hospitals will help ensure patients receive treatment immediately after landing.

Luvindao said the service was developed as a practical response to the country's healthcare challenges, rather than waiting for the construction of more referral hospitals.

"While we build those hospitals, Namibians want service. While we build those hospitals, there is another 12-year-old boy that might have severe head injuries and need urgent transportation. And so it is our role to make a plan, not just for the future, but for now," she said. She said the government was working towards constructing four hospitals in the coming years, but acknowledged that such projects require substantial financial resources and time.

Close 

The air ambulance, she said, would complement existing ground ambulance services and provide an additional option for patients whose conditions require urgent specialist intervention.

The ministry has also activated an emergency callcentre to coordinate requests, verify referrals and dispatch the service.

Luvindao said the centre would serve as a single point of coordination to ensure that patients with justified medical needs are transferred promptly.

The service will prioritise patients who require urgent specialist treatment, including those with serious trauma, neurological, cardiac and obstetric emergencies, as well as patients whose conditions make road transport unsafe or too slow.

The initiative requires cooperation between the health sector, aviation authorities, emergency responders and security institutions. - [email protected]

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - November 6, 2026
World.content:
Guinea-Bissau Cancels Controversial Newborn Vaccine Trial

Guinea-Bissau has cancelled a proposed hepatitis B vaccine trial on newborn babies following international criticism that it was unethical and potentially exploitative. The trial was funded by the US, under Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who has a long record of expressing scepticism about vaccines. The study planned to involve 14,000 newborns, with half receiving the vaccine and the other half being denied the shot, despite WHO recommendations. Health experts warned that withholding the vaccine could expose babies to infection in a country where nearly one in five people has hepatitis B. The government had previously prohibited vaccine trials involving children, while police have seized a batch of vaccines from the research centre at the centre of the controversy.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Atiku Vows to Fight Court Ruling Sidelining His 2027 Presidential Bid

Former Nigerian Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has vowed to challenge a Federal High Court ruling invalidating his nomination as the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate for the 2027 elections and nullifying the party's David Mark-led leadership. Atiku accused the ruling All Progressives Congress of using the courts to undermine his campaign, insisting that his campaign would continue despite the judgment. The ADC Presidential Campaign Council says its legal team is preparing to seek interim relief, including a stay of execution, while pursuing an appeal. The ruling followed a legal challenge by former ADC deputy chairman Nafiu Bala Gombe over the party's leadership transition.

UN Warns of Growing Drone Threats in Abyei

The United Nations has warned that drone attacks in the disputed Abyei region are adding a new dimension to security threats, following strikes that killed at least 30 people and injured about 59 in October. UN peacekeeping chief Jean-Pierre Lacroix told the Security Council that the attacks, the first of their kind in the area, highlight growing threats influenced by wider regional conflicts and armed groups. The warning comes amid rising tensions following deadly intercommunal clashes that killed 124 people in September. Meanwhile, the UN has raised concerns over continued drone strikes on infrastructure in Sudan, including power and water facilities, while warning that funding shortages could force the closure of a key border clinic serving about 100,000 people.

Attacks on Water Systems Triple in Conflict Zones, UNICEF Warns

Attacks on water and sanitation infrastructure in conflict zones have tripled from 2021 to 2025, putting millions of children at greater risk of disease, malnutrition and violence, according to a new UNICEF report. The report documented more than 135 attacks across 15 countries in 2025, compared with fewer than 45 incidents across eight countries in 2021. It highlights damage to water treatment plants, pipelines and other essential facilities in countries including Sudan and the Gaza Strip. UNICEF Executive Director Catherine Russell said that attacks on water and sanitation systems "deprive children of safe drinking water and the essential services that rely on water to function effectively". UNICEF is calling on parties to conflicts to protect water infrastructure, workers and civilians, warning that repairing damaged facilities cannot replace the protection required under international humanitarian law.

WHO Adds Two Ebola Vaccines to DR Congo Trial

The World Health Organization has announced that two additional Ebola vaccine candidates will join clinical trials in the Democratic Republic of Congo as the country battles its largest-ever outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain. The vaccines, developed by Oxford University in partnership with the Serum Institute of India and US-based Moderna, will be evaluated for the first time during an outbreak of this Ebola strain. The DR Congo has been battling a deadly outbreak of Ebola disease for nearly six months. It has become the largest in the country's history. As of 1 November, the outbreak had recorded more than 10,500 confirmed cases and 5,126 deaths. The WHO said that the new candidates could provide an important tool in controlling the outbreak, although they will require national approval before joining the ongoing trial.

Close 

Six More Bodies Found in Kenya Building Collapse

Rescue teams in Nairobi have recovered six more bodies from the rubble of a collapsed multi-storey building in the Eastleigh neighbourhood, raising the death toll from the disaster. Kamukunji MP Yusuf Hassan confirmed the latest recoveries. He expressed condolences to families still waiting for news of missing relatives. Four people were previously rescued alive. Police have maintained that multi-agency teams are supporting the operation. They urged members of the public to keep away from the affected area to allow emergency responders and specialised equipment to operate safely. The search operation remains focused on recovering those still believed to be beneath the debris.

World.title: Uganda: Muhoozi Announces Military Exit, Says He Will Focus On Christ
World.content:
Uganda's Chief of Defence Forces (CDF), General Muhoozi Kainerugaba, has announced plans to retire from the military leadership position in the coming months, saying he intends to dedicate his life to Christ.

In a statement posted on his official X account, Muhoozi said he had accomplished the tasks he believed God had assigned him and was ready to hand over the office to another officer.

"My time as CDF is coming to an end. I have accomplished all the tasks my God gave me. In a few months I will handover this office to a qualified officer. I shall dedicate my life to Christ after that," he stated.

The announcement signals a possible leadership transition at the helm of the Uganda People's Defence Forces (UPDF), although Muhoozi did not specify a date for the handover or identify his potential successor.

Muhoozi, the son of Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni, has served as Uganda's military chief since March 2024, when he was appointed to replace General Wilson Mbadi.

His announcement comes amid continued public attention on his military leadership and political pronouncements, which have frequently attracted regional interest.

The UPDF has not been cited in the statement as having issued a separate announcement detailing the planned transition.

World.title: Guinea Bissau: Guinea-Bissau Cancels Controversial US-Funded Hepatitis B Vaccine Trial on Newborns
World.content:
Guinea-Bissau has cancelled a proposed hepatitis B vaccine trial on newborn babies following international criticism that it was unethical and potentially exploitative.

The trial was funded by the US, under Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who has a long record of expressing scepticism about vaccines.

The study planned to involve 14,000 newborns, with half receiving the vaccine and the other half being denied the shot, despite WHO recommendations. Infants are at the greatest risk of being chronically infected with hepatitis B (HBV); the infection is typically passed on from mother to baby. There is no cure for the disease and it can go on to cause long-term liver damage and liver cancer. The WHO recommends that all babies receive the HBV vaccine at birth and also a booster dose, which is known to provide years of protection.

Health experts warned that withholding the vaccine could expose babies to infection in a country where nearly one in five people has hepatitis B.

The government had previously prohibited vaccine trials involving children, while police have seized a batch of vaccines from the research centre at the centre of the controversy.

World.title: Ghana: Inadequate Funding Stalls Women, Peace and Security Plan - - FOSDA
World.content:
THE Director of the Foundation for Security and Development in Africa (FOSDA), Mrs Dorothy Barnes, has called for adequate and dedicated funding for the implementation of Ghana's National Action Plan on Women, Peace and Security (WPS), saying inadequate financing has undermined the delivery of key activities under the programme.

She said only three out of the 46 activities under the Second Ghana National Action Plan (GHANAP II) had been fully implemented, while 24 were partly delivered, 11 recorded limited delivery and eight were not implemented.

Mrs Barnes made the call when she delivered the keynote address at a stakeholder validation meeting on the final evaluation of FOSDA's monitoring of the GHANAP II project in Accra on Tuesday.

The meeting brought together stakeholders from government institutions, security agencies and civil society organisations to contribute to the evaluation report.



Related Articles

She said although Ghana had made progress in promoting gender equality, peace and security, including the passage of the Affirmative Action Act, inadequate funding remained a major obstacle to the effective implementation of the action plan.

Mrs Barnes noted that institutions relied substantially on donor support and resources allocated to other programmes to undertake activities under GHANAP II because there was no dedicated budget for its implementation.

"Ghana is in a stronger position on women, peace and security than it was at the beginning of GHANAP II, which was in 2020. We have also witnessed encouraging developments in women's leadership and representation," she said.

"At the same time, gender mainstreaming must go beyond having policies, offices and focal persons. It must be reflected in budgets, recruitments, promotions, operational practices, accountability mechanisms and the everyday experiences of women and men within our institutions," she added.

The GHANAP II sought to increase women's representation in peacebuilding and decision-making roles by 30 per cent, eliminate sexual and gender-based violence and protect human rights.

Mrs Barnes also expressed concern about the limited availability of shelters and psychological support for victims of gender-based violence.

Close 

"Women and girls experiencing violence should not have to travel long distances or face additional financial and social barriers to access protection and justice," she said.

She called for a shift from broad commitments under the action plan to a focused, measurable and adequately resourced implementation framework as Ghana prepared to develop its third action plan on women, peace and security.

The Senior Programme Liaison Officer at the High Commission of Canada, Mrs Bertha Desmennu, commended the government and other stakeholders for their contributions to GHANAP II.

She said advancing the women, peace and security agenda required sustained commitment and collaboration among relevant stakeholders.

Mrs Desmennu reaffirmed Canada's commitment to supporting the agenda in Ghana through civil society organisations, including FOSDA, and other institutions.

She said the evaluation findings provided valuable evidence to strengthen accountability, inform future programming and support the development of the next national action plan.

BY LAWRENCE VOMAFA AKPALU

World.title: Two women's college basketball teams score on their own baskets in the same day
World.content:
Apparently, knowing which basket you’re supposed to score on is no longer a prerequisite for playing college basketball. Of course, I’m joking, but if you saw the lowlights from the New Mexico State and Northwestern State women’s basketball teams, you might not be so sure. Each team delivered a spectacularly embarrassing moment Friday by gifting the opposing team points while scoring on the wrong basket.

Yes, you read that correctly. Twice. On the same day in college basketball, two different women’s teams scored on their own baskets.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

The first disaster came during Northwestern State’s matchup against Arkansas, when Lady Demons guard Karma Wynn inexplicably put the ball into the Razorbacks’ basket on an inbounds play in the backcourt. This was after an offensive foul, too. They were guarding the basket, got a stop, and Wynn still brain-farted and gave Arkansas free points.

ROYALS IMPLODE WITH 3 ERRORS AS METS' CARSON BENGE SCORES LITTLE LEAGUE HOME RUN TO OPEN GAME VS KC

The reaction from the Northwestern State bench said just about everything you need to know. An assistant coach buried her head into her clipboard, while teammates just about leaped out of their seats in shock. Arkansas was handed two free points, and the Razorbacks went on to win big, 89-59.

But just when you thought we'd reached peak basketball stupidity, New Mexico State decided to raise the bar. This one has an interesting twist, so stay in your seat.

With just over 20 seconds remaining against Southern Utah, New Mexico State trailed 61-60. Guard Emma Christiana made a great play by stealing an inbounds pass, then kept going toward the wrong end of the court. She effortlessly laid the ball into her own basket, but judging by her initial reaction and those of the people in the stands, they had no idea Southern Utah had taken the lead in the most insane way.

With the game on the line, Christiana scored two points for the other team. Even crazier: The scorekeeper didn't notice the blunder either. On the broadcast, you would've thought, by the scoreboard, that New Mexico State took the lead.

WNBA FAN GOES VIRAL FOR HALF-COURT SHOT HORROR SHOW THAT LEFT HIM SPRAWLED ON THE COURT

Apparently, even the person responsible for keeping score couldn't comprehend that someone had just scored on the wrong basket. At that point, you almost have to wonder whether anyone in the building knew what was happening. What a mess.

And somehow, despite literally helping Southern Utah take a 63-60 lead, New Mexico State pulled off the win. Freshman Stacy Chovino scored twice in the final seconds, including the game-winning basket with two seconds remaining, on the correct basket, to give the Aggies a stunning 64-63 victory.

Imagine winning a basketball game after scoring for your opponent in the final 30 seconds. That's almost more impressive than the mistake itself.

Two teams. Two own baskets. One afternoon.

World.title: Secret Service arrests armed Venezuelan migrant near White House over alleged Trump assassination threat

An illegal immigrant from Venezuela was arrested near the White House Thursday after he was allegedly found inside a stolen vehicle carrying multiple guns and reportedly threatening to kill President Donald Trump, according to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

U.S. Secret Service officers approached the suspect Thursday evening after spotting him "acting suspicious in his car while it was parked on Constitution Avenue in Washington, D.C.," DHS told Fox News.

The suspect told officers he had heard voices in his head telling him to travel to the nation's capital and kill Trump, DHS said.

Officers subsequently learned that the vehicle had been reported stolen, and the suspect admitted to having weapons inside, according to DHS.

CAR RAMS INTO WHITE HOUSE BARRICADE, SUSPECT ARRESTED: OFFICIALS

A search of the vehicle reportedly turned up three guns, including an AR-15-style rifle and two handguns, along with dozens of rounds of ammunition.

The suspect was identified as Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos, who illegally entered the country through Texas in March 2024 and was subsequently arrested by U.S. Border Patrol, according to officials.

He was later released into the country under the Biden administration, authorities said.

After his arrest, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) lodged a detainer for Chrinos with the U.S. Marshals Service, which currently has custody of Chrinos.

The U.S. Secret Service said the incident reflects a growing threat posed by armed individuals "drawn to the White House complex."

"This is the latest example of Secret Service personnel relying on extensive training and experience to de-escalate a volatile situation that posed an imminent threat to our protectees and other Americans," U.S. Secret Service Director Sean Curran said in a statement.

"While our personnel are trained to respond to situations like this, and we remain confident in our tactics, we are alarmed by the increase in threat cases that continue to arise."

To disrupt threats before they arrive in Washington, Curran said the agency will continue to "focus on proactively investigating and identifying individuals" who raise suspicion.

SECRET SERVICE DETAINS, QUESTIONS INDIVIDUAL WHO DROVE VEHICLE INTO BARRICADE NEAR WHITE HOUSE

DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin also commended the Secret Service for intervening before the suspect could harm anyone.

"This is just an example of the incredible work done by the men and women of the Secret Service every single day as they put their lives on the line to protect our nation’s leaders," Mullin said in a statement.

Chrinos was charged with carrying a rifle outside a home or business, three counts of unlawful transportation of a firearm, three counts of possessing an unregistered firearm, three counts of possessing unregistered ammunition, possession of certain dangerous weapons, carrying a pistol without a license, unauthorized use of a motor vehicle, theft and receiving stolen property.

World.title: South Florida candidate sues election official, alleging bias in a contentious, razor-thin race
World.content:
MIAMI — South Florida Democratic congressional candidate Eliott Rodriguez filed a federal lawsuit against the Miami-Dade supervisor of elections Friday, citing bias after she declined to recuse herself from the recount process. Incumbent Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar is named in the lawsuit as well.

The lawsuit seeks to bar Miami-Dade supervisor of elections, Alina García, from acting as a deciding member of the county canvassing board for the 27th Congressional District, where the results are razor-thin.

Salazar was leading Rodriguez by 1,103 votes or 0.44 percentage points as of Thursday evening. Florida law requires automatic recounts when there is less than a 0.5-point margin. The canvassing board oversees the recount.

Rodriguez’s campaign demanded Thursday that García recuse herself from oversight of the recount.

The Rodriguez campaign alleged the attorney representing Salazar in the recount, Robert Fernández, is García’s son-in-law and requested immediate confirmation, saying the relationship would raise additional serious concerns, according to the complaint.

The campaign also cited in the lawsuit an interview García gave to The Miami Herald on election night stating, “Maria Elvira is the winner, with or without a recount” and that it was “possible but not probable” there were enough remaining ballots to flip the results.

She added that recounts almost never end up going the other way. “Usually the trend we see is what continues,” García was quoted as saying. In other words, if Salazar is ahead, it will likely remain that way.

The Miami Herald also reported that Oren Rosenthal, general counsel for the supervisor of elections, estimated he’s seen about 20 recounts, and with the margin that Salazar was leading by on Tuesday night, he said it was unlikely the result will be overturned.

In a press release, García stated, “I want to reiterate that I was elected by the people to perform the duties of the Supervisor of Elections. Nothing disqualifies me form performing those duties including serving on the Canvassing Board. Accordingly, as I have stated previously, I have not recused myself, nor will I.”

Juan-Carlos Planas, general counsel for the Miami-Dade Democratic Executive Committee, ran against García in the 2024 supervisor of elections race.

“If candidates are going to hire relatives from the supervisor of elections, we’re going down a very dangerous precedent,” he said. “Can you imagine going into court and litigants are hiring relatives of the judge? The judge would be removed from office.”

On Thursday evening, the day before the final counting of ballots and certification of results was scheduled to take place, an attorney representing Rodriguez sent a letter to García demanding she step away from matters involving the race.

“This goes beyond any ethical standards. The canvassing board is a quasi-judicial body so she sits as a quasi-judicial official,” Planas said. “This is a quasi-judicial body and therefore she should recuse herself like any other judge would.”

García, a Republican who served one term in the Florida state House before winning the election for supervisor of elections in 2024, has posed in pictures with fellow Republican leaders, including Salazar and President Donald Trump. She is the first elected supervisor of elections. It was previously a nonpartisan position appointed by the county’s mayor.

Few pundits considered the race competitive this time around, but the district shifted 14.26 points toward Democrats compared with the 2024 presidential election.

Salazar’s office did not respond to a request for comment.

“My opponent is behaving like an election denier, attempting to turn this process into a political circus because he does not like election outcome,” Salazar posted on X Thursday night.

Salazar and Rodriguez are both Cuban American and former journalists. Salazár has won three consecutive terms to represent the heavily Hispanic 27th Congressional District. She and Trump comfortably won the district in 2024.

There were signs of trouble for Salazar in September when she released an ad where she broke with Trump on his immigration policies.

“Mr. President, some of your immigration enforcement efforts have gone too far,” she said in the ad while standing in front of the White House.

Her district has been particularly impacted by Trump’s harsh immigration enforcement, including a record number of deportations of Cubans. While Trump criticized Salazar after the ad, he eventually endorsed her before Election Day.

World.title: Cornell faculty senate issues no confidence vote on administration’s handling of sexual assault
World.content:
Members of the Cornell University faculty senate on Friday issued a vote of no confidence on the administration’s ability to manage the response to an alleged sexual assault at a fraternity house in 2024, according to the university.

The governing body took up the issue after a former student, known as Jane Doe, alleged she was sexually assaulted and forced to take drugs at the Chi Phi fraternity house from Oct. 19 to 20, 2024. The allegations, detailed in a lawsuit the woman filed in September, led to widespread criticism of the university and calls for reform from students and alumni.

The senate’s resolution states that the body “has no confidence in the ability of the central administration to effectively address the ongoing crisis of sexual assault at Cornell University.”

It does not recommend removals or suggest how to manage the controversy’s fallout. It passed by a vote of 75-50, with five abstentions and five members not voting, according to a copy of the results obtained by NBC News.

The vote will not directly affect leadership decisions at the institution, including whether President Michael Kotlikoff remains in his role. The board of trustees, which has the authority to replace him, can consider the finding in its decisions but suggested in a statement Friday that no immediate changes were expected.

“The Board of Trustees remains confident that President Kotlikoff and his administration are the right leaders to thoughtfully and comprehensively address the serious problem of sexual assault on our campus,” chair Anne Meinig Smalling said.

Smalling highlighted recent changes implemented by leadership.

“They have already taken several important steps to this end, including adding staff to the Cornell Office of Civil Rights, expanding in-person sexual assault prevention education, and hiring more victim advocates,” Smalling said. “The administration will continue to build on that progress with more initiatives to be launched in the weeks and months ahead.”

A demonstration by Cornell students in support of Jane Doe, in Ithaca in October. Spencer Platt / Getty

Faculty senators who sponsored the resolution called the decision “a reckoning” for the university.

“It is a call for real, systemic change; not a slow-moving taskforce, weakly enforced ban on fraternity parties, or expensive [public relations] damage control, but meaningful, evidence-based steps to reduce the incidence of sexual assault on campus and provide significant support to and justice for survivors,” the sponsors wrote in a statement.

Jane Doe and her attorney have alleged that Cornell failed to support her through the reporting process and subsequent investigation.

“We are hopeful that this will be yet another step forward to educate and support the Cornell community by addressing the longstanding scourge of sexual assault on campus,” said Jane Doe’s attorney Thomas Giuffra.

Jane Doe accused seven members of the fraternity of participating in a sexual assault, which she told police began with a consensual threesome but resulted in unwanted sex and ketamine consumption.

All seven men accused in the incident deny the allegations. Two were expelled from the university after an internal civil rights proceeding, and others faced less severe punishments from the school.

Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said he declined to pursue a criminal case in November 2024 based on a six-page statement from Jane Doe.

New York Attorney General Letitia James was appointed by Gov. Kathy Hochul last month to investigate the matter and consider whether criminal charges are supported. Two of the defendants initiated court proceedings aimed at disqualifying James based on what they argue are biased statements of support for Jane Doe that James posted on social media.

On Thursday, several defendants joined an Article 78 proceeding in Sullivan County that was recently filed by lawyers for one of the fraternity brothers, Gillio Lopes. Diego Sarabia, Scott Kretzschmar, Scott Norris and Winston Lee, who are co-defendants in Jane Doe’s lawsuit, were added to the petition in support of Lopes’s request.

Two remaining defendants, Matthew Ingalls and Jonathan Newell, do not have representation in the civil case and did not respond to Lopes’s attorneys.

On Wednesday, James announced her appointment of a former federal prosecutor to direct the investigation. That attorney, Jacqueline Kelly, will lead a team under James to conduct an independent inquiry into the sexual assault allegations.

Lopes’s lawyers argued in court papers that unless James recuses herself, the appointment does not change their position on the existence of a conflict. James has said her office is fully capable of conducting a fact-based, unbiased review.

James has also said her comments were merely an expression of empathy for Jane Doe.

Lee’s attorney previously filed a separate motion in Tompkins County Supreme Court seeking to block James from any grand jury proceeding, arguing that she had exhibited bias. A decision is expected Nov. 13.

A Cornell University police vehicle outside Chi Phi fraternity in Ithaca in October. Heather Ainsworth for NBC News

At a virtual news conference after the vote Friday, the proposal’s lead sponsor, Paul Ortiz, said the idea came “after hearing from scores of current students, alumni, staff and faculty that the Jane Doe case was the tip of the iceberg.”

“The bravery of the survivors of sexual assault at Cornell past and present who told us their stories proved that no administration or administrator at this university could have been unaware of the chronic crisis of sexual assault at Cornell,” said Ortiz, a labor history professor. “Not in the 1970s, not in the 2010s; most certainly not now.”

Ortiz said he and other faculty members are planning an oral history project to highlight stories of sexual assault survivors at Cornell.

The Cornell president last month fielded questions from professors and other university employees at a senate meeting. At that Oct. 14 session, Kotlikoff vowed to reassess Greek life at the university and examine preventative measures to reduce the number of reported sexual assaults on campus.

The president said additional resources were being added to support victims when they come forward. That includes assistance dealing with Cornell’s bureaucracy for students who make sexual assault complaints, Kotlikoff said.

Kotlikoff told the faculty members that he didn’t know until recently that Jane Doe dropped out of school after the incident.

Senators recently debated whether to postpone the vote until after the university’s outside review by former acting attorney general Sally Yates, who was commissioned by the board of trustees to examine how the matter was handled.

A proposal to postpone the no-confidence decision failed to pass at the Senate’s Oct. 28 meeting.

World.title: Pete Hegseth strikes defiant tone in face of impeachment threat
World.content:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Thursday dismissed a renewed effort in the House to bring articles of impeachment against him as early as next week.

In a video on social media, Hegseth said, “A disgruntled, defeated congressman, along with all his Democrat allies, has also dropped sham articles of impeachment against yours truly, just like they tried against President Trump twice.”

Hegseth was referring to Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., who said Wednesday that he plans to reintroduce articles of impeachment when the House is back in session. Lawmakers are scheduled to return to Washington on Monday.

“It’s all about the politics of personal destruction,” Hegseth added. “Didn’t work against President Trump, and it won’t work with me. You can rest assured of that.”

In the more-than-five-minute video, Hegseth only briefly touched on the Iran war — a driving force behind the effort to impeach him, as well as GOP losses in this week’s midterm elections.

Massie, who lost his GOP primary after he crossed Trump, urged Trump on Thursday to replace Hegseth while he still has a GOP majority in the Senate.

“My Hegseth impeachment resolution is a much gentler version of what’s coming when Dem’s control Congress. They’ll have hearings & trials,” he said on X.

“There is one contingency in which I won’t reintroduce the articles of impeachment: Hegseth resigns,” Massie wrote Wednesday.

Numerous Democrats have indicated a desire to oust Hegseth since their midterm election wins, including House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York, who is poised to be the next speaker.

Trump said Wednesday that he is not planning to replace Hegseth, and he said Thursday that Hegseth “has done a fantastic job” and “probably has opposition” over the actions he has taken, including purging military leadership.

Trump has told some allies he is considering replacing Hegseth, asking them who they think should succeed him, two people familiar with discussions told NBC News this week. He has previously insisted that he was not considering dismissing department heads just days before they were shown the door.

Massie tried to force a vote on impeaching Hegseth in September, but his efforts were stunted when House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., sent the House home early.

He would need several Republicans to join all Democrats in supporting the impeachment measure for it to succeed.

The House has impeached only two Cabinet officials in history — former President Joe Biden’s homeland security secretary, Alejandro Mayorkas, in a partisan vote, and William Belknap, the secretary of war in the 1870s. No Cabinet members have ever been convicted by the Senate.

World.title: We want to hear your experience with changes to student loan repayment plans
World.content:
President Donald Trump’s “big, beautiful bill” has transformed the sprawling federal student loan system — and student borrowers are feeling the effects of the most consequential changes.

This year, the approximately 7.5 million student borrowers under the Biden-era Saving on a Valuable Education, or SAVE, plan had to select a new one. So far, about 2 million borrowers have done so, after the Education Department warned that the SAVE plan was “illegal” and would be discontinued. The remaining borrowers who did not select a new plan were set to start receiving notices this month informing them that they missed a final deadline and were automatically moved to a new plan.

The Trump administration has said ending the SAVE plan would help streamline repayment programs while ensuring borrowers are paying off what they owe to the federal government. But student advocacy groups fear lower-income borrowers who had benefited from smaller monthly payments — or even qualified to make no payments at all based on their income — will end up with significantly higher bills under the other available plans.

World.title: Muscle health is key to longevity. Here’s how to measure yours.
World.content:
Muscle health is linked to how well we fight off disease and our longevity. But healthy muscles aren’t just about the size of a bicep or how much we weigh.

An international team of kinesiologists and nutrition experts recently urged doctors to pay more attention to skeletal muscle quality and the ratio of muscle to fat as a key to “metabolic regulation, immune function and overall vitality and functioning.”

“Muscle health estimation could be as important as measuring somebody’s blood pressure,” said longevity expert Dr. Nicolaas Deutz, a professor in the Department of Kinesiology and Sport Management at Texas A&M University and a co-author of the expert review. Kinesiology is the study of physical activity and body mechanics.

Healthy muscles not only help you move safely, they’re also the body’s main storage system for blood sugar, which maintains an active metabolism and lowers inflammation in the body.

Muscle health is usually associated with muscle size in younger people, but that relationship becomes less clear as we get older, said Deutz.

In fact, mass is only a part of overall muscle health. For instance, women generally have lower overall muscle mass than men, yet their muscle health is generally comparable to men’s.

A more complete picture of muscle includes strength, balance, physical function, activity levels and the amount of fat stored within the muscle itself, said Dr. Fatima Cody Stanford, an obesity medicine physician-scientist at Mass General Brigham.

How to prevent muscle loss

There’s growing awareness of how muscle health plays a role in longevity and metabolic diseases such as Type 2 diabetes, especially in the wake of the phenomenal popularity of GLP-1 medications. Drugs such as Ozempic and Zepbound have been shown to improve blood sugar, blood pressure and cardiovascular risk, but they’re also linked to loss of both fat and lean mass, including skeletal muscles.

Stanford, who is also associate professor of medicine and pediatrics at Harvard Medical School, said people taking GLP-1s need adequate nutrition to preserve muscle function.

“As a person loses substantial body weight, the body requires less muscle to carry that weight, and reductions in fat within muscle may improve muscle quality and function,” Stanford said. “At the same time, older adults, individuals with frailty or low baseline muscle mass, and people who are losing weight rapidly warrant particularly close attention to strength, function, protein intake and resistance exercise.”

A sufficient amount of high-quality daily protein — including fish, poultry, eggs, dairy, tofu, beans, lentils, nuts and seeds — helps protect against muscle loss, Stanford said.

The U.S. dietary guidelines encourage people to prioritize protein with nutritious, minimally processed foods at every meal, recommending 1.2 to 1.6 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight.

Staying active — working in the yard, walking or weight training — strengthens different muscle groups, Deutz said.

If lifting heavy gym weights isn’t appealing, resistance exercises can effectively preserve muscle strength and function, particularly during weight loss.

“Body-weight exercises, resistance bands, machines or supervised strength work can all be appropriate depending on the individual’s mobility, fitness level and medical history,” Stanford said.

How to measure muscle health

Muscle power is the ability to produce force quickly, and handgrip strength is one of the simplest ways to measure it.

“An often-overlooked consideration is muscle power — the ability to produce force quickly, which declines earlier and more rapidly with aging than muscle strength,” said Stephen J. Carter, associate professor in the kinesiology department at the School of Public Health — Bloomington Indiana University. “From a practical perspective, muscle power is more relevant to daily life than simply strength.”

Grip strength measures the force generated when squeezing a handheld tool called a dynamometer.

While “low” strength depends on factors like age and BMI, a large analysis of grip strength of over 20,000 older men and women defined it as less than 57 pounds for men and 35 pounds for women.

Fortunately, targeted resistance training can successfully improve the numbers.

Carter recommended resistance training, such as free weights, weight machines, resistance bands or body-weight exercises like push-ups, two to three times weekly, progressing gradually to a higher intensity to build more muscle.

World.title: ICE arrests Wisconsin state patrol trooper with pending asylum case at airport, attorneys say
World.content:
ICE detained a Wisconsin state patrol trooper with a pending asylum case at an airport, his attorneys said Thursday.

Carel Aaron Van Der Merwe, an asylum-seeker from South Africa who has a valid federal work authorization, was detained by ICE as he waited to board a domestic flight, according to a statement from the Christopher & De Leon Law Office released Thursday and obtained by NBC affiliate WEAU. He is currently being held at a detention facility in Juneau, Wisconsin, ICE records show.

According to the attorneys’ statement, Van Der Merwe tried to explain that he had a valid work permit and has a asylum application, but the ICE officers “said they did not care, placed him in handcuffs and shackles, and transported him to immigration detention.”

The 21-year-old came to the country legally as a child from South Africa and is included in his father’s asylum application, according to the statement. He has been a Wisconsin state patrol trooper for nearly a year, his attorneys said.

A Department of Homeland Security spokesperson said in a statement to NBC News, “To be clear: work authorization or a pending application do not confer legal status in the U.S.”

ICE arrested Van Der Merwe during a targeted enforcement operation at the Dane County Regional Airport in Madison, Wisconsin, on Thursday, DHS said in a statement.

“He entered the country in March 2019 with legal permission to stay until September 2019,” the spokesperson said in the statement. “In defiance of our nation’s laws, he overstayed his admission. This illegal alien will receive due process and remain in ICE custody pending removal proceedings.”

“This administration is working diligently to ensure that aliens in our country illegally can no longer fly unless it is out of our country to self-deport,” the spokesperson said.

Attorney Marc Christopher, who represents Van Der Merwe, said in a statement that the arrest was “inhumane and despicable.”

“Putting a Wisconsin State Trooper behind bars while his asylum case sits unresolved does not make our communities safer,” he said.

In another statement, Christopher said, “Wisconsin trusts Carel to protect the public.”

“DHS owes his family and our community an explanation of why keeping him behind bars is necessary,” he said.

World.title: Taylor Swift is the ‘fakest’ celeb Knicks fan, players say; team rushes to her defense
World.content:
The New York Knicks rushed to Taylor Swift’s defense Friday after players Tyler Kolek and Miles McBride questioned the singer’s fandom.

The defending world champions were quick jump on their white horse and laud the singer in the wake of their players stirring up some bad blood with blue-and-orange Swifties.

“Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years, has a long history with Madison Square Garden, and we are incredibly appreciative of her support of the organization,” a Knicks spokesperson said in a statement to NBC News.

Kolek might even have some explaining to do to his girlfriend and self-identified Swiftie, Alexi Sousa, who wanted to know “what he had to say about my girl.”

The Knicks famously boast a front row of world famous fans at their Madison Square Garden home dates.

When Kolek and McBride appeared on an NBA 2K TikTok livestream on Thursday and were asked who is “the fakest celeb fan you’ve seen courtside,” they dared coming for the 5-foot-10 Pennsylvania native and 14-time Grammy winner.

“Maybe Taylor Swift?” Kolek said. “I don’t know if I’ve seen her at any other games.”

McBride agreed, but acknowledged that he and Kolek had damaged their reputation and were headed for anti-hero status.

“I would agree,” McBride said. “Swifties (are) not going like that answer.”

Sensing he was in trouble, Kolek tried to backtrack and say Swift’s life as showgirl might make attending Knicks games a challenge.

“I guess she’s got a lot going on so she can’t come all the time,” Kolek said. “But it’s a little performative.”

Swift’s role in Knicks history will live as long as fans remember Game 4 of the NBA finals, when she sat courtside with Alana Haim, Este Haim and Mariska Hargitay at Madison Square Garden.

They donned t-shirts with Knicks-ian puns and watched New York shake off a 29-point deficit to beat San Antonio.

The Knicks, three days later, clinched the series in San Antonio and brought the NBA championship back to New York for the first time since 1973.

Swift is no stranger to the Knicks as she famously visited practice in 2014 and got a lift from Amar’e Stoudemire for a memorable slam dunk.

World.title: Sunday on 60 Minutes: Trump talks Democrats' sweeping midterm wins
World.content:
Sunday on 60 Minutes, hear from President Trump in his first sit-down interview since Democrats' sweeping midterm victories.

60 Minutes Correspondent Ross Douthat interviewed Mr. Trump at the White House Friday, days after CBS News projected that Democrats would win control of the House and Senate. Democrats picked up more than 40 House seats, with more than two dozen races still uncalled. In the Senate, Democrats picked up seven seats, with two races — Mississippi and Alaska — still too close to call.

Douthat asked Mr. Trump about Republican losses, congressional investigations, the wars in Iran and Ukraine, and the economy.

World.title: Trump told 60 Minutes to expect post-midterm firings
World.content:
President Trump announced that Stephen Miller would replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff just hours after he told 60 Minutes that he'd be shaking up his team.

When 60 Minutes Correspondent Ross Douthat asked Mr. Trump whether he expected to fire anyone after Republicans lost both chambers of Congress, the president said: "I do, yeah. Little bit."

"I love my Cabinet. I think they're good," he said. "But I'll … be doing maybe a few changes."

Mr. Trump suggested Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is safe for now, despite CBS News reporting that he asked advisers this week whether the Pentagon chief should stick around. When Douthat asked whether he has confidence in Hegseth, Mr. Trump said: "I do."

"Look, we've won two wars. We've won Venezuela and taken out billions and billions and billions of dollars already. And we will be taking out many billions of dollars and get along very well. And, you could call it a territory, you could call it whatever you want. We won that war in less than one hour," Mr. Trump said.

After announcing Wiles' departure on Friday, Mr. Trump told reporters he "wanted to make a change," adding, "sometimes in life, you have to make moves." Wiles submitted her resignation on Thursday, a move that was tied to the GOP's midterm defeats, CBS News reported.

Wiles is among the most powerful people to leave the Trump administration. A few Cabinet officials departed earlier this year — Attorney General Pam Bondi, Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem and Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer — but otherwise, the president who rose to nationwide fame by firing people on television has largely left his team intact.
