World.title: Sheinbaum calls for INE ‘cleanup’ after corruption scandal: Friday’s mañanera recapped
World.content:
Listen to this article

Sheinbaum’s mañanera in 60 seconds

🏛️ Sheinbaum says INE corruption goes beyond Guadalupe Taddei: The president asserted that corruption in the awarding of electoral materials contracts occurred “during the entire period of Lorenzo Córdova,” Taddei’s predecessor as INE president, and “probably before as well.” Taddei resigned as National Electoral Institute president last week amid allegations of corruption.

The president asserted that corruption in the awarding of electoral materials contracts occurred “during the entire period of Lorenzo Córdova,” Taddei’s predecessor as INE president, and “probably before as well.” Taddei resigned as National Electoral Institute president last week amid allegations of corruption. 🧹 “ The INE has to be cleaned up”: Sheinbaum recalled the “el INE no se toca” (“don’t touch the INE”) protest slogan and suggested it was used “to hang on to this whole electoral mafia” that allegedly existed before Taddei became INE president. She said the institute must guarantee clean elections, transparency and republican austerity.

Sheinbaum recalled the “el INE no se toca” (“don’t touch the INE”) protest slogan and suggested it was used “to hang on to this whole electoral mafia” that allegedly existed before Taddei became INE president. She said the institute must guarantee clean elections, transparency and republican austerity. 🕊️ Sheinbaum condemns murder of Cuernavaca city councilman: She called the killing of Morena councilman Gabriel Rivas Ríos, an environmental activist, “sad and infuriating,” saying there was “no doubt” it was ordered and carried out specifically against him. Rivas had criticized the Alto Verde residential project proposed for Cuernavaca, and Sheinbaum said she asked the Security Cabinet to support the Morelos Attorney General’s Office’s murder investigation. She said Rivas hadn’t requested federal protection.

She called the killing of Morena councilman Gabriel Rivas Ríos, an environmental activist, “sad and infuriating,” saying there was “no doubt” it was ordered and carried out specifically against him. Rivas had criticized the Alto Verde residential project proposed for Cuernavaca, and Sheinbaum said she asked the Security Cabinet to support the Morelos Attorney General’s Office’s murder investigation. She said Rivas hadn’t requested federal protection. 🇪🇸 Sheinbaum explains absence from Ibero-American Summit: She said she skipped the Madrid gathering because she will travel to China for the APEC leaders’ summit later this month. Sheinbaum noted that Foreign Affairs Minister Roberto Velasco represented her in the Spanish capital. She will seek a call with Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez to discuss the summit’s outcomes.

Why today’s mañanera matters

Alleged corruption in the awarding of National Electoral Institute (INE) contracts to a small group of electoral materials suppliers was a central focus of President Sheinbaum’s Friday morning press conference.

Guadalupe Taddei resigned as president of the INE last week after it came to light that lucrative contracts were awarded to electoral materials companies linked to a businessman with whom she had a close personal relationship. Taddei and that businessman, José Alfredo Hernández Casillas, are reportedly among 25 people who have been added to the Finance Ministry’s Blocked Persons List and who will be investigated by the Federal Attorney General’s Office.

On Friday morning, Sheinbaum asserted that corruption in the INE also occurred when Lorenzo Córdova was president of the institute between 2014 and 2023.

Also of note at today’s mañanera were the president’s remarks about the murder of a Cuernavaca city councilman. Gabriel Rivas Ríos, a Morena party member, was killed on Wednesday in Cuernavaca, capital of the state of Morelos.

Sheinbaum: ‘The INE needs to be cleaned up’

Sheinbaum asserted that corruption in INE’s rewarding of electoral materials contracts predates the 2023-2026 tenure of Taddei as the institute’s president.

Corruption occurred “during the entire period of Lorenzo Córdova,” she said.

“And probably before as well,” Sheinbaum added. “The audit will have to determine that.”

Sheinbaum noted that Córdova and other INE officials participated in various protests against an electoral reform proposal during the presidency of Andrés Manuel López Obrador. She recalled that the slogan of the protests was “El INE no se toca,’ or “Don’t touch the INE.”

“The INE has to be cleaned up. Maybe they said ‘don’t touch the INE’ in order to hang on to this whole electoral mafia that was built with them,” she said.

“The National Electoral Institute is an institute that must guarantee the will of the people, that must guarantee clean elections,” Sheinbaum added.

“In its operation, it must guarantee … transparency and republican austerity,” she said.

Sheinbaum laments murder of Cuernavaca councilman

Asked about the murder of Rivas, Sheinbaum said she knew him and described him as an environmental activist.

She described his murder as “sad and infuriating” and conveyed her condolences to his family and colleagues.

Sheinbaum said that when she heard about the homicide, she requested that the federal Security Cabinet “dedicate time and effort” to supporting the Morelos Attorney General’s Office in its investigation into the crime.

“It was a direct homicide. Some people on a motorbike shot him directly,” she said.

“There is no doubt it was a homicide that was ordered and carried out specifically against him,” Sheinbaum said.

She noted that Rivas had recently been critical of a real estate development in Cuernavaca that could cause “environmental problems.” She was referring to the Alto Verde residential project, whose construction was proposed on a site called La Cazahuatera.

The land where La Cazahuatera is located is “considered one of the last remnants of lowland deciduous forest within the urban area” of Cuernavaca, the news outlet Infobae reported.

In addition to contributing to efforts to solve Rivas’ murder, Sheinbaum said her administration would also work with Morelos Governor Margarita González Saravia “to see what can be done with this [real estate] development that he was fighting against.”

After a reporter noted that many environmental activists have been murdered or attacked in Mexico, Sheinbaum said that a lot of them now have government protection.

“They’ve approached us [to ask for protection],” she said, adding that government protection helps to “avoid” attacks on activists.

Sheinbaum said that Rivas hadn’t requested protection from the federal government.

“That doesn’t mean that we don’t condemn the homicide,” she added.

Sheinbaum explains her absence at Ibero-American Summit in Spain

Sheinbaum told reporters that she decided not to go to this week’s Ibero-American Summit in Madrid as she will travel to China for the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders’ summit later this month. She said visiting Spain as well as China would mean spending more time outside Mexico than she would like.

Sheinbaum said she advised Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and King Felipe VI of her decision not to travel to Madrid.

“I wrote a letter to them … because they were the ones that invited me,” she said.

Sheinbaum noted that Foreign Affairs Minister Roberto Velasco represented her at the Ibero-American Summit, a gathering of leaders and officials from Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking countries.

She said she would seek a call with Sánchez to discuss the outcomes of the summit.

Mexico’s Foreign Ministry said in a statement that “the summit’s four agreements match Mexico’s priorities: care systems, academic mobility, disaster protection, and artificial intelligence that serves people.”

By Mexico News Daily chief staff writer Peter Davies (peter.davies@mexiconewsdaily.com)

World.title: Bucking expectations, Banxico lowers the interest rate, despite some inflation concerns
World.content:
Mexico’s central bank (Banxico) lowered its benchmark interest rate 25 basis points to 6.25%, surprising analysts, who as recently as this week expected the rate to remain unchanged.

In a split vote, the three bank governors supporting the reduction argued that there are no perceived demand pressures in the economy and that the degree of monetary restriction implemented is still in effect.

In a statement, Banxico adjudged that the disinflationary process has continued, indicating that, “given the prevailing slack conditions, the pass-through of exchange rate movements to prices would be limited.”

In what is viewed as guidance for future actions, the statement added that “going forward, the Governing Board believes that maintaining the rate for an extended period at the level achieved will support the convergence of inflation to its target and will be appropriate to meet external macroeconomic challenges.”

At the same time that Banxico reduced the interest rate, it raised its headline inflation forecast for the fourth quarter from 3.5% to 3.7%, acknowledging that risks remain tilted to the upside.

“This is mainly due to higher-than-anticipated levels for non-core inflation,” the statement said.

The bank also incorporated an upward adjustment to its estimate of core inflation for the last quarter, from 3.6% predicted in September to the 3.7% they now anticipate.

Although the economy continued to expand in the third-quarter, Banxico believes that “slack conditions are still expected throughout the forecast horizon, and downside risks to economic activity persist.”

Still, Banxico maintains that inflation will reach its target — 3% with a tolerance range of plus or minus 1 percentage point (2% to 4%) — by the fourth quarter of next year.

Banxico’s economic research identified four upside risks to its inflation forecasts: the persistence of core inflation; further depreciation of the peso; disruptions from trade policies or an inflationary impact from geopolitical conflicts; and, climate-related effects and unspecified cost pressures.

Looking ahead, the Governing Board said that maintaining the rate at its current level for an extended period “will support the convergence of inflation to its target and will be appropriate to address external macroeconomic challenges.”

Thursday’s surprise decision — 30 of the 36 institutions consulted by Citi expected the rate to remain unchanged — impacted the currency exchange market immediately.

The reduction pushed the dollar as high as 18.96 pesos during the day, although it later moderated its advance and closed at 18.7499. The peso lost 18.3 centavos, or 0.99%, compared to Wednesday’s close.

With reports from El Economista and El Financiero

World.title: My grandmother spent her life caring for others. Finding care for her changed my direction
World.content:
My grandmother Ene spent decades working as a hospital nurse. She cared for thousands of people she had never met before, then came home and looked after her own family. When my grandfather was struggling with Parkinson’s disease, she nursed him too.

To me, she was simply the best grandmother imaginable. Caring for people was part of her working life, but it was also how I knew her as a wife, mother and grandmother.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by RetireMexico.com (@retiremexico.official)

When she needed care for herself in her final years, I wanted to find somewhere that reflected that. Somewhere she would receive personal attention and feel comfortable living.

The options fell short. The places available felt like hospitals, lacked the personal care I had hoped for and were very expensive. I kept wishing there was somewhere better for her. She had given so much, and I struggled with how little of that seemed to be reflected in the choices available to her.

Ene died in the winter of 2025. Her experience stayed with me and eventually became part of the reason I started RetireMexico.

Making a home in Puerto Vallarta

Before settling in Mexico, I had spent years traveling. Home often depended on where the next flight took me. In 2021, I settled in Puerto Vallarta.

I have worked in marketing and sales since 2013. Along the way, I founded Spring Hub, a coworking space in Tallinn, Estonia, and Vivian Agency, the marketing agency I still run.

Those projects gave me experience building businesses. My grandmother’s final years brought me to a subject I understood much more personally. I had been a family member trying to find care for someone I loved, struggling to find an option that felt right.

When aging loved ones refuse help

Alejandra Arenas, who now co-leads RetireMexico with me, came to this work through experiences of her own.

Alejandra was born and raised in Puerto Vallarta. As a child, she watched her great-aunt live with dementia over six years of summer visits. Her great-aunt had been a pianist. Eventually, as Alejandra described it, she was “just pressing keys.”

Her great-uncle Armando cared for his wife around the clock without outside help.

Later, while in high school, Alejandra volunteered at a senior home on the outskirts of Puerto Vallarta. She helped organize movie nights and art activities. The residents received physical care, but some felt their families had set them aside.

“A home can meet every physical need and still fail the person living in it,” she told me.

Then there was Jim, her mother’s closest friend in Puerto Vallarta. An American who had lived there for more than 25 years, he developed cancer and later dementia. By then, he had no family or old friends left, only his cat.

Jim refused nearly all help, even as strangers began taking advantage of him. Alejandra and her mother became his caregivers, learning as they went how to protect him and manage the responsibilities that came with his declining health. They cared for him until he died in 2019.

For Alejandra, that experience raised a question that sits at the heart of our work. How do you help someone accept support while respecting the independence they still have?

“Finding the right care is only half of it,” she said. “The other half is finding the right moment, and helping someone still largely independent make that move without feeling erased.”

Finding a path forward

My grandmother’s experience and Alejandra’s years of caregiving were different, but they gave us plenty to talk about. We both knew how difficult these decisions could become when someone you loved needed help.

We began building RetireMexico as a free directory of senior living communities in Mexico, gathering information and checking the details with the homes themselves.

The work involves practical questions about staffing, rooms, costs and the care a residence can provide. Our own experiences also keep us asking about daily life. Who notices when a resident is withdrawn? What happens when someone refuses help? Will the person moving in have a say in how they live?

I still wish I could have found a better place for Ene. I cannot change the choices available to her then. But her experience continues to shape the questions I ask on behalf of other families.

Enelin Toneva is a contributor to Mexico News Daily.

World.content:

Rival poll. Celeste-Tel, polling for radio network Onda Cero, 29 October to 3 November: PP 31.8%, PSOE 25.7%, Vox 19.2%.

What the Latest Polls Show

SW Demoscopia, a Spanish polling firm, put the Spanish Socialist Workers’ Party (PSOE) at 31.0% and the PP at 28.5% in fieldwork from 26 October to 5 November. It projected 127 seats for the PSOE, 116 for the PP and 63 for Vox.

Celeste-Tel, polling for the radio network Onda Cero from 29 October to 3 November, reached the opposite result. It had the PP at 31.8%, the PSOE at 25.7% and Vox at 19.2%.

PolitPro, a poll aggregator, put the PP at 29.8%, the PSOE at 26.0% and Vox at 18.8% on 6 November. Its projection gives the PP 128 seats, the PSOE 112, Vox 81 and the Broad Front, a new left-wing alliance led by former Barcelona mayor Ada Colau, 29 seats, so no single party reaches the 176 needed for a majority.

The state-run Center for Sociological Research (CIS) showed the widest Socialist lead, at 34.0% to 22.2% for the PP in fieldwork from 1 to 6 October. We found no November CIS poll.

File photo: Gran Vía, one of Madrid’s main avenues.

The Calendar Ahead

Spaniards vote on Sunday 29 November, after Sánchez called the election on 5 October. Congress had rejected two housing decrees on 2 October, with the PP, Vox and Junts, a Catalan party, voting against them.

Both Sánchez and Feijóo have accepted a one-on-one television debate on Monday 16 November, hosted by the private broadcaster Mediaset. No start time has been confirmed.

The new Congress meets on 23 December, and a prime minister is chosen only after that. The official campaign runs from 13 to 27 November.

Campaign Themes Take Shape

Sánchez launched his pre-campaign in Dos Hermanas, near Seville, on 10 October with housing as the central theme, before a crowd his Socialists count at more than 5,000. Feijóo has said the vote is a choice between four more years of the present situation and a chance for change.

Madrid Mayor José Luis Martínez-Almeida, a PP politician, warned that the campaign would be “dirty”, blaming the left. Isabel Díaz Ayuso, the PP president of the Madrid region, told people not to vote by post, while Feijóo’s spokesman Borja Sémper urged Spaniards to vote either in person or by post.

What It Means for US Readers

A close, fragmented result would leave the choice of prime minister to talks among parties after the new Congress meets on 23 December. That timetable is why a name may not be settled in the days after the 29 November vote.

A lasting government matters to investors holding Spanish bonds and shares. Market prices can move fast and should be read next to the polls.

What Is Not Known

The polls disagree sharply. SW Demoscopia and the state-run CIS have the Socialists ahead, while Celeste-Tel and GAD3 put the PP in front, and we cannot say which will prove closer to the result.

It is unclear whether the PP and Vox together can reach 176 seats. A GAD3 poll for the newspaper ABC, reported on 12 October, projected about 198 seats for the two parties combined, while SW Demoscopia’s figures leave them short.

The start time and final format of the 16 November debate have not been confirmed. Atresmedia, a private broadcaster, has proposed a four-way debate on 26 November, and the parties disagree on which channel should host it.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is Spain’s general election?

Spain votes on Sunday 29 November 2026 for all 350 seats in Congress, the lower house, and 208 directly elected seats in the Senate, the upper house. A majority in Congress is 176 seats.

Who is favored to become prime minister?

Polymarket bettors gave Alberto Núñez Feijóo about 88%, against about 11% for Pedro Sánchez, at 6:22 p.m. ET on 6 November. Those prices are bets rather than polls, and the latest SW Demoscopia survey has the Socialists ahead.

When is the next scheduled event in the campaign?

Sánchez and Feijóo have accepted a Mediaset television debate on Monday 16 November. The start time has not been published.

World.title: Canada’s Budget Sets US$44 Billion Deficit
World.content:
CANADA · ANALYSIS

Key Facts What is happening Canada’s budget, tabled on 5 November, projects a CA$62.3 billion (US$44.4 billion) deficit for 2026-27.

The gap Two weeks earlier, Parliament’s budget watchdog, the Parliamentary Budget Officer (PBO), projected CA$63.3 billion (US$45.2 billion) and a peak of US$50.1 billion.

What to watch The Bank of Canada, the central bank, announces its next interest rate decision on 9 December.

What it means for you US exporters still face tariff risk, because current tariff rates and the state of talks with Washington are unconfirmed.

Prediction markets Polymarket, a prediction platform, prices no change on 9 December at 72.5% and a 25 basis point (quarter of a percentage point) rise at 28.0% (6 November, 5:15 p.m. ET).

Canada’s federal budget, tabled on 5 November, projects a deficit of CA$62.3 billion (US$44.4 billion) for 2026-27. That is slightly below the CA$63.3 billion (US$45.2 billion) that Parliament’s independent budget watchdog expected two weeks earlier.

For readers in the United States, the budget matters because it sets Canada’s borrowing, its currency and its stance in trade talks with Washington. This analysis compares the government’s numbers with the watchdog’s and explains what both mean for exporters and investors, building on the USA & Canada Intelligence Brief of 3 November 2026.

The Budget Numbers and How They Compare

Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne tabled Budget 2026 on Thursday 5 November. Finance Canada, the federal finance ministry, projects deficits of CA$62.3 billion (US$44.4 billion) in 2026-27 and CA$62.5 billion (US$44.6 billion) in 2027-28, or 1.8% of GDP (gross domestic product, the size of the economy) in both years.

The deficit then narrows to CA$57.6 billion (US$41.1 billion) in 2028-29 and CA$52.9 billion (US$37.7 billion) in 2030-31. Budget 2026 also puts the 2025-26 deficit at CA$39.3 billion (US$28.0 billion), CA$27.5 billion (US$19.6 billion) lower than the government’s Spring Economic Update, an interim fiscal statement issued on 28 April 2026, had expected.

The Parliamentary Budget Officer (PBO) is Parliament’s independent fiscal watchdog. Its Economic and Fiscal Outlook of 20 October 2026 was gloomier than the budget, as the list below shows.

US dollar values in this article use CA$1 = US$0.7133, the rate from RT, a market-data provider, at the close on 5 November 2026.

2026-27 deficit: CA$63.3 billion (US$45.2 billion) from the PBO, against CA$62.3 billion (US$44.4 billion) in the budget.

Peak deficit: CA$70.2 billion (US$50.1 billion) in 2027-28 from the PBO, against CA$62.5 billion (US$44.6 billion) in the budget.

We have not reconciled the two sets of numbers line by line. The PBO’s outlook was published on 20 October, before the budget.

Budget 2026 draws its economic assumptions from a September 2026 survey of private-sector forecasters. That survey expected oil to average US$85 a barrel in 2026, against US$73 in the spring.

Five months of data do not settle the full-year outcome. The budget projects CA$62.3 billion (US$44.4 billion) for all of 2026-27, so the first five months are a small share of the projected gap.

Who Is Who in Ottawa’s Budget Debate

Several institutions shape the numbers and the reaction to them. Each has a different job and a different stake.

Mark Carney, Prime Minister, leads the Liberal government.

François-Philippe Champagne, Minister of Finance and National Revenue, tabled the budget on Thursday 5 November.

Annette Ryan, Parliamentary Budget Officer, leads the independent office that costs policy and publishes the projections cited here; the House of Commons approved her appointment on 21 April 2026 by 164 votes to 153.

Tiff Macklem, Governor of the Bank of Canada, the central bank, sets the policy interest rate, which affects the government’s borrowing costs.

Pierre Poilievre, leader of the Conservative Party, heads the official opposition in the House of Commons.

Budget 2026 says Canada is now positioned to balance operating spending with revenues in 2027-28, one year ahead of the 2028-29 target. Operating spending means day-to-day costs, excluding capital investment.

Before the budget, the PBO judged that the government’s two fiscal anchors, its self-imposed budget targets, were only half met. It said the operating balance would be reached in 2028-29, while the deficit-to-GDP ratio would not fall every year.

The Bank of Canada on Wellington Street, Ottawa. File photo.

What Is Driving the Deficit

Rates have moved up. On 28 October the Bank of Canada raised its policy rate by 25 basis points (a quarter of a percentage point) to 2.50%.

Governor Macklem said there could be a need to raise the rate further. He added that, given the uncertainties, the bank will “proceed carefully.”

The Canadian Dollar, Tariffs and US Exporters

The loonie, as the Canadian dollar is known, closed at US$0.7133 on 5 November 2026, or about 1.40 Canadian dollars per US dollar, according to RT, a market-data provider. On 6 November it traded near US$0.708, about 0.8% lower, or roughly 1.41 per US dollar.

No official source reviewed for this article links the deficit to the currency. A higher policy rate usually supports a currency, while a wider deficit can weigh on sentiment, but neither Finance Canada, the PBO nor the Bank of Canada commented on the loonie in the material reviewed.

The PBO’s outlook counts all US tariffs and Canadian countermeasures in effect on 1 October 2026. It assumes the US measures stay in place, which it calls a status quo assumption rather than a forecast of the negotiations.

For US exporters, the budget matters through retaliation and demand. Canadian countermeasures hit US sellers directly, while weaker Canadian growth reduces what Canadian buyers can spend on US goods.

Scenarios

These are scenarios, not forecasts. The first is a stable path, in which deficits stay close to the budget’s CA$62 billion (US$44 billion) a year through 2027-28 and oil prices stay supportive.

Finance Canada’s own stress test is mild. In its global supply disruptions scenario the 2026-27 deficit is CA$62.4 billion (US$44.5 billion), against CA$62.3 billion (US$44.4 billion) in the base case.

The second is a slippage path, in which spending or weaker revenue pushes deficits toward the PBO’s higher figures, such as its CA$70.2 billion (US$50.1 billion) peak. The budget’s CA$62.5 billion (US$44.6 billion) for 2027-28 would then be too low by about CA$7.7 billion (US$5.5 billion).

The third is a tariff-shock path, in which tariffs deepen and growth falls below the forecasters’ current path. The PBO itself warns that outcomes depend on commodity markets, global growth and how fast firms adjust.

Parliament Hill, Ottawa. File photo.

What It Means for You

If you export to Canada, plan for tariff risk rather than assume a clean trade deal. The PBO’s outlook assumes current US tariffs stay in place.

If you hold Canadian dollar assets or bonds, watch the government’s borrowing and the Bank of Canada. The budget still shows deficits of CA$52.9 billion (US$37.7 billion) or more in every year to 2030-31.

If you travel or invest across the border, the exchange rate of roughly 1.40 to 1.41 Canadian dollars per US dollar is the number to track. It can move again around the 9 December rate decision.

This analysis has no data on direct exposure for Latin America. Readers there should treat Canada’s deficit mainly as a signal about North American trade conditions.

What Is Not Known

We have not reconciled why the budget’s deficit for 2027-28 is lower than the PBO’s peak. The PBO has not yet published a reaction to Budget 2026 that we reviewed.

Current US tariff rates and the status of talks after the PBO’s 1 October cut-off are unconfirmed here. No US exporter data and no official comment linking the deficit to the loonie were found.

What to Watch

9 December 2026, 09:45 Eastern Time: the Bank of Canada rate announcement, the last on the 2026 schedule.

Next PBO assessment of Budget 2026: no date confirmed in the material reviewed.

June 2027: the end of Governor Macklem’s seven-year term, which began on 3 June 2020.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, a crypto-based prediction platform, priced the 9 December Bank of Canada decision at 5:15 p.m. ET on 6 November 2026 as no change 72.5% and a 25 basis point increase 28.0%, with US$219,575 traded.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Frequently Asked Questions

How big is Canada’s budget deficit in 2026?

Budget 2026 projects CA$62.3 billion (US$44.4 billion) for 2026-27. Parliament’s budget watchdog had projected CA$63.3 billion (US$45.2 billion).

When will Canada’s deficit peak?

The budget shows CA$62.5 billion (US$44.6 billion) in 2027-28, then a decline. The watchdog expects a higher peak of CA$70.2 billion (US$50.1 billion) in 2027-28.

When was Canada’s 2026 federal budget tabled?

Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne tabled it on Thursday 5 November 2026. It projects deficits of CA$52.9 billion (US$37.7 billion) or more in every year to 2030-31.

What is the Parliamentary Budget Officer?

The PBO is Parliament’s independent fiscal watchdog. Annette Ryan leads the office, which costs government policy and publishes economic and fiscal projections.

What is the Bank of Canada’s interest rate?

The policy rate is 2.50% after a 25 basis point (quarter of a percentage point) increase on 28 October 2026. The next decision is on 9 December.

Does the deficit affect the Canadian dollar?

No official source reviewed here draws a direct link. The Canadian dollar closed at about 1.40 per US dollar on 5 November 2026, according to RT, a market-data provider.

World.content:
ANTIGUA GUATEMALA · Culture

Flowers fill the colonial centre on 14–15 November, and Kany García plays the Ermita de la Santa Cruz on 28–29 November. Only dated, confirmed events are listed here.

Chicken buses at a bus station in Antigua Guatemala. File photo. photo: Aaron Smith, from The Rio Times archive

ANTIGUA GUATEMALA — The city’s biggest November weekend is free: the tenth Festival de las Flores (Flower Festival) fills the colonial centre on Saturday 14 and Sunday 15 November. Two weeks later, Puerto Rican singer Kany García plays two nights at the Ermita de la Santa Cruz, and the Saturday show is already sold out.

This is the monthly guide to things to do in Antigua Guatemala in November 2026, for residents and visitors alike. It lists only events with a published date and a source we could check on 6 November, so earlier events such as All Saints’ Day on 1 November are left out.

14 and 15 November: Festival de las Flores

Saturday 14 and Sunday 15 November Festival de las Flores, tenth edition Historic centre of Antigua Guatemala · Free entry The theme this year is “Ciudad Floreciente” (Flourishing City). The agenda lists flower contests, a flower market called Mercadito de las Flores, outdoor music, dance, poetry and theatre, and workshops.

Saturday 14 November, 06:00 WAWA te lleva al Festival de las Flores 2026 Antigua Guatemala · Ticketed · Sold through eticket.gt, a Guatemalan ticket seller WAWA is a transport service that takes festival-goers to Antigua, so they avoid traffic, long walks and parking. Tickets are sold through eticket.gt, and the listing does not show a price, so check the final price at checkout.

Sunday 15 November, 06:00 WAWA te lleva al Festival de las Flores 2026 Antigua Guatemala · Ticketed · Sold through eticket.gt, a Guatemalan ticket seller The same service runs again on the Sunday. The ticket page does not say where the vehicles depart from, so check that with WAWA before you buy.

The festival route for pedestrians runs from 1a Calle to 6a Calle, between 1a Avenida and 7a Avenida, according to the festival’s published agenda. The flower contests are split into five categories: Barrio con Mejor Actitud (best neighbourhood spirit), Libre (free category), Fachadas (building fronts), Bicicletas (bicycles) and Monumental.

The festival began in 2017, when a group of Guatemalan creatives founded it. Banco Industrial, a Guatemalan bank, supports this edition, and the organisers plan to keep reusing and composting the flowers afterwards.

Times and street closures for 2026 had not been published when we checked on 6 November. The festival’s own account on Instagram, @festivaldefloresantigua, is the place the organisers point visitors to for updates.

Last year the municipality opened eight lots at Q20 a car per day (about US$3) and ran three free shuttle routes into the centre. Those are 2025 figures, so treat them as a guide until the city confirms this year’s plan.

26 to 29 November: Concerts at the Ermita de la Santa Cruz

Thursday 26 November, 20:00 Tributo Internacional a Ricardo Arjona Ermita de la Santa Cruz · Tickets on eticket.gt, a Guatemalan ticket seller The listing is a tribute concert to Ricardo Arjona, the Guatemalan singer-songwriter. The listing does not show a price, so check it at checkout.

Saturday 28 November, 20:00 Kany García Ermita de la Santa Cruz · Sold out · eticket.gt, a Guatemalan ticket seller Kany García is a Puerto Rican singer-songwriter. The ticket seller eticket.gt marks this first night “AGOTADO” (sold out), so the only route to a seat is a late release or an official resale.

Sunday 29 November, 20:00 Kany García Ermita de la Santa Cruz · Tickets on eticket.gt, a Guatemalan ticket seller The second night was still on sale on 6 November, while the first night was already marked as sold out. Tickets cost Q990 (about US$130) for Gradas (stands) and Q1,145 (about US$150) for Sillas AMEX (chairs), service charge included.

The venue has a fourth date on its listing, but it falls in February 2027 and is outside this guide. We could read prices only for the Kany García show on 29 November, so this guide quotes no others.

Planning Your Antigua Guatemala Month

November is the hinge between the rainy and dry seasons. Guatemala’s national weather service, INSIVUMEH (the Instituto Nacional de Sismología, Vulcanología, Meteorología e Hidrología), says rain recedes in November, and its director has said the cold season starts nationwide this month.

The service’s outlook says the first cold front could arrive in the second or third week of November. Pack a warm layer for evenings, especially for an outdoor concert venue.

Prices for Kany García are in quetzales (Q), Guatemala’s currency. We convert at Q7.64 per US dollar, the market rate from RT, a financial-data provider, on 6 November 2026, rounded to the nearest dollar.

The Bank of Guatemala, the central bank, publishes its own daily reference rate. Antigua sits at about 1,500 metres above sea level, so days are mild and nights can be cool.

Cobbled streets are hard on suitcase wheels and thin soles, so wear comfortable shoes. All three concerts start at 20:00, so plan how you will get home afterwards and check the last transport options with your hotel or host.

Buy tickets only through eticket.gt, the Guatemalan ticket seller that lists the ticketed events in this guide. Always compare the date, venue and time on the checkout page with the details here before you pay.

Before you travel, read the current Guatemala travel advisory from your own government. In the United States, that is the State Department’s advisory at travel.state.gov, which is updated by region and can change.

We looked for a number of weekly listings that appear on third-party calendars, including a Wednesday movie night at Caoba Farms, a country-music night at Antigua Brewing Company and a weekend yoga session at Fuego Yoga. We could not confirm any of them with the venues, so they are not in this guide.

If you want evergreen things to do in Antigua, the Ermita de la Santa Cruz and the colonial centre are the obvious starting points. For anything else, ask the venue directly and confirm the date before you plan around it.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the biggest events in Antigua Guatemala in November 2026?

The tenth Festival de las Flores on 14–15 November and Kany García at the Ermita de la Santa Cruz on 28–29 November. A Ricardo Arjona tribute concert at the same venue is on 26 November.

Is the Festival de las Flores free?

Yes, entry is free. Only the optional WAWA transport service is ticketed, and its listing does not show a price.

How do I buy tickets for Kany García in Antigua?

Tickets are sold on eticket.gt, a Guatemalan ticket seller. The Saturday 28 November show is sold out, while Sunday 29 November was still on sale on 6 November. On eticket.gt the 29 November show costs Q990 (about US$130) for Gradas and Q1,145 (about US$150) for Sillas AMEX (chairs), with the service charge included.

How can I reach the Festival de las Flores without a car?

WAWA runs a ticketed transport service at 06:00 on 14 and 15 November, sold on eticket.gt, a Guatemalan ticket seller. The page does not list departure points, so ask WAWA before you buy.

World.title: What to Do in Florianópolis in November 2026

FLORIANÓPOLIS · Culture

Brazil’s island city has a quiet November: three holidays, a free geek festival in the Botanical Garden on 28–29 November and a handful of tech and business days. Here is what we could confirm, and how to plan around it.

FLORIANÓPOLIS — This is the monthly guide for people who live on the island or are staying for weeks, with things to do in florianópolis november 2026 checked against organiser pages on Sympla, a Brazilian ticketing platform. We list only events whose date, time and venue we confirmed; everything we could not confirm is left out.

November is a month of holidays and professional meetings rather than one giant festival. Three national holidays fall in it: Monday 2 November, Sunday 15 November and Friday 20 November.

Friday 20 November, Black Consciousness Day, is a national holiday under Brazilian federal law 14.759 of 2023, so it makes a long weekend. Book beach parking and restaurant tables early for that weekend.

The Rest of the Month at a Glance

The first days of November are already behind us. ENAF Floripa, a fitness-industry fair at the CentroSul convention centre, ran from 30 October to 1 November and has ended.

What remains falls into two groups: work-oriented days in the middle of the month and a big public weekend at the end. The cards below are in date order.

11 to 17 November: Talks, a Digital Cities Forum and a Property Summit

Wednesday 11 November, 19:30–21:30 Palestra Pública Gratuita: Síndrome do Esgotamento Energético IIPC Florianópolis, Avenida Rio Branco, 354, Edifício Maxim’s, room 810, Centro · Free · Sympla A free public lecture, in Portuguese, from IIPC, the Instituto Internacional de Projeciologia e Conscienciologia, a Brazilian institute. The Sympla page says registration is free and compulsory because places are limited, and asks guests to arrive early. The listing gives only the title, time and address, so we cannot describe the content.

Thursday 12 November, 08:00–17:00 Fórum de Cidades Digitais e Inteligentes da Grande Florianópolis Atrium Office, Rua Jair Hamms, 38, Pedra Branca, Palhoça · Price not shown · Sympla The forum is run by Rede Cidade Digital, an initiative that says it has run free events for mayors and municipal managers since 2012. It is aimed at mayors, public managers and civil servants, with talks on public-private partnerships, artificial intelligence in city halls and smart public security.

Tuesday 17 November, 08:00–20:00 MB Summit Florianópolis 2026 Mercure Florianópolis Hotel, Rodovia Admar Gonzaga, 600 · Price not shown · Sympla MB Summit is a one-day congress for real estate brokers, with talks on sales, marketing and technology. It matters mainly to people working in Florianópolis property; the talks appear to be in Portuguese.

26 to 29 November: INOVAR SC and Passeio Geek

Thursday to Friday 26–27 November INOVAR SC 2026, 13th edition Tribunal de Justiça de Santa Catarina (state court), Rua Doutor Álvaro Millen da Silveira, 208, Centro, and ACATE (the state technology association), Rod. José Carlos Daux, SC-401 · Free, limited places · Sympla Thursday morning is at the state court, with a panel on a 2030 social innovation agenda for Santa Catarina. Thursday afternoon and Friday afternoon are at ACATE, with sessions on artificial intelligence for social good, the games industry and inclusive entrepreneurship, plus a live humanoid-robot demonstration; the closing is at 17:00 on Friday.

Saturday to Sunday 28–29 November, from 10:00 on Saturday to 19:00 on Sunday Passeio Geek, 5th edition Jardim Botânico de Florianópolis, Rodovia Admar Gonzaga, 742-782 · Free, bring 1 kg of non-perishable food · Sympla An open-air pop-culture festival with cosplay and K-pop contests, video-game tournaments, board games, a geek fair and a planetarium. It is the best fit for families this month.

Entry is free and supportive: the organiser, Geek Cursos, an innovation school, asks visitors to bring 1 kg of non-perishable food. A ticket is not required on the day, but the organiser asks for an online registration beforehand. The listing says nothing about parking or accessibility, so ask the organiser through Sympla before you go.

Practical Notes for November

Most of the events above are in Portuguese, and the pages are too. Sympla is the main ticket and registration site for them; its listings show whether an event has ended.

The Sympla pages for the Fórum de Cidades Digitais e Inteligentes da Grande Florianópolis and MB Summit state the same cancellation terms for paid orders. Orders can be cancelled up to 7 days after purchase, provided the request comes at least 48 hours before the event.

If you plan beach days, check water quality first. IMA, the Santa Catarina state environment institute, publishes bathing-water results by beach at balneabilidade.ima.sc.gov.br, and marks each point as suitable (próprio), unsuitable (impróprio) or undetermined.

We did not find a Florianópolis summary for November, so look up your beach on the portal on the day you go rather than rely on a general statement. Results change from one sampling to the next.

The 2 November and 20 November holidays fall on a Monday and a Friday. Expect banks and many offices to be closed, while Sunday 15 November already sits on a weekend and brings no extra day off.

We have not quoted prices in reais, because none of the pages we checked shows a ticket price in the text we could read. If a price appears at checkout, convert it at the day’s rate before you commit.

Sympla is the platform where all of these events are listed, and each page states the date, hours and address. Open the page on the day, because an organiser can change a time or mark an event as ended.

Plan the week around the calendar: the Fórum de Cidades Digitais e Inteligentes da Grande Florianópolis on Thursday 12 November is a working day in Palhoça, a neighbouring city on the mainland, while MB Summit on Tuesday 17 November is in Florianópolis itself. Check your route before you leave.

What We Could Not Confirm

Several smaller listings that circulated for November, including a lifestyle weekend, a tech day and a few evening talks, could not be matched to an organiser page, so we left them out. We also did not find official opening hours for the Botanical Garden.

Check the Sympla event page or the Prefeitura de Florianópolis, the city government, for any late change. This guide is updated as listings are confirmed.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the main events in Florianópolis in the rest of November 2026?

Four listed events stand out: the Fórum de Cidades Digitais e Inteligentes da Grande Florianópolis in Palhoça on 12 November, MB Summit on 17 November, INOVAR SC on 26–27 November and Passeio Geek on 28–29 November.

Are there public holidays in Florianópolis in November 2026?

Yes, three national holidays: Monday 2 November (All Souls’ Day), Sunday 15 November (Republic Day) and Friday 20 November (Black Consciousness Day). Only the 2nd and the 20th give a day off in the working week.

Which November events in Florianópolis are free?

INOVAR SC offers free but limited places, and Passeio Geek is free with a request to bring 1 kg of non-perishable food. The IIPC lecture on 11 November is free, with compulsory registration.

ARUSHA: This is the monthly guide for people who live in Arusha, a city in northern Tanzania, or are staying for weeks rather than a weekend. It lists only events that a venue, organiser or ticket platform has published for November 2026.

November is a quiet month for public festivals in Arusha. One trade fair, one evening of wine, food and music and one dance competition have confirmed dates, and we say plainly below what we left out.

No Tanzania-wide public holiday falls in November 2026, so offices and shops keep normal hours. Prices in Tanzanian shillings (TZS) are converted at about TZS 2,629 per US$1, the market rate on 6 November.

Sunday 8 November: A Produce Trade Fair

Sunday 8 to Tuesday 10 November HortiLogistica Africa 2026 TGT Grounds, the fair’s venue in Burka Estate, Arusha · Day pass TZS 20,000 (about US$7.60) for Tanzanian citizens; US$20 for regional and international visitors A horticulture trade fair hosted by the Tanzania Horticultural Association (TAHA), the national body for fruit, vegetable and flower growers. It suits anyone working in farming, food supply chains or exports, and it is open to curious residents who register first. Tickets are sold online only, and the organisers say there is no on-site registration.

The organiser sells day, two-day and three-day passes. Tanzanian citizens pay TZS 20,000 (about US$7.60), TZS 40,000 (about US$15.20) or TZS 50,000 (about US$19) respectively.

Regional and international visitors pay US$20, US$40 or US$58 for the same passes. The local rate applies to citizens, not to foreign residents, so expatriates should expect the international rate.

The organiser has not published daily opening hours. Check the visitor page at hortilogisticaafrica.com before you go, and buy your pass early because walk-ins are not accepted.

Saturday 28 November: Two Events, Two Venues

Saturday 28 November Rooted: A Love Letter to Arusha River Trees Country Inn, Usa River, Arusha · Ticket TZS 130,000 (about US$49) · Start time not published An evening the organiser describes as “savored through wine, food, music, style and atmosphere”, at a country inn in Usa River, a village outside Arusha town. Tickets are sold through Nilipe, a Tanzanian online ticket platform. The listing gives no programme or start time, so check it again closer to the day.

Saturday 28 November Dance Battle Festival, Season 4 Elimu Yetu, a venue in the city centre, Arusha · Regular TZS 10,000 (about US$3.80), VIP TZS 30,000 (about US$11.40) · Start time not published A dance competition sold through Nilipe, the Tanzanian ticket platform, for the same evening in central Arusha. The listing describes a touring show with seven cities and four categories. It gives no line-up or start time.

The two events share a date, so you will need to pick one. The dance battle is the cheaper ticket, while the Usa River evening is the premium option.

Listings We Left Out and Why

The Tanzania Mining and Investment Conference (TMIC), organised by the Ministry of Minerals with the Tanzania Chamber of Mines, runs from 19 to 21 November 2026 at the Julius Nyerere International Convention Centre in Dar es Salaam, the country’s commercial capital. It is not in Arusha, so we do not list it as an Arusha event.

Other November conferences and touring expos that appear in online listings either lack a confirmed Arusha venue or have no clear organiser page. We have left them out until organisers publish firm details, and we will add them if they do.

Planning Your Arusha in November

November falls in the short-rains season, known in Swahili as vuli. Wet spells are possible in Arusha at this time of year.

Pack a light rain jacket and a warm layer for evenings. Allow extra travel time on rainy days, especially for the venues outside the centre.

Independence and Republic Day, the next national holiday, falls on Wednesday 9 December. Christmas Day on Friday 25 December and Boxing Day on Saturday 26 December follow.

If you travel on the evening of 28 November, agree a taxi fare before you set off and arrange a driver back from Usa River, since the inn is outside the city centre. Check the entry rules for your passport before you book.

Tanzania Immigration Services runs an online application portal at visa.immigration.go.tz, where you can check the current fee for your nationality. Tanzania uses East Africa Time, which is three hours ahead of UTC and eight hours ahead of New York in November.

Carry some shillings for taxis and small purchases. For fresh listings, check the Nilipe event pages and the HortiLogistica Africa website.

Pass prices are quoted in both currencies, so compare the shilling and dollar rates before you pay. Confirmed public events in Arusha for November 2026 remain thin, and we will update this guide as organisers publish more.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the biggest event in Arusha in November 2026?

HortiLogistica Africa 2026, a horticulture trade fair, runs from Sunday 8 to Tuesday 10 November at TGT Grounds in Burka Estate.

How much are HortiLogistica Africa tickets?

A day pass costs TZS 20,000 (about US$7.60) for Tanzanian citizens and US$20 for regional and international visitors. Three-day passes cost TZS 50,000 or US$58.

Are there any public holidays in Arusha in November 2026?

No Tanzania-wide public holiday falls in November 2026, so offices, shops and venues keep normal hours.

What is on in Arusha on 28 November 2026?

Rooted: A Love Letter to Arusha at River Trees Country Inn in Usa River (TZS 130,000, about US$49), and Dance Battle Festival Season 4 at Elimu Yetu, a venue in the city centre (TZS 10,000 to 30,000, about US$3.80 to US$11.40). Both are sold on Nilipe.

World.title: What to Do in Recife in November 2026: Céu and Circus
World.content:
RECIFE · Culture

Recife’s big circus festival ends this weekend, and the singer Céu plays on 14 November. Here is what is confirmed, with prices in US$.

Marco Zero square in central Recife. File photo. Photo: Wilfredor, CC0 via Wikimedia Commons

RECIFE — This is the November culture guide for expats, digital nomads and long-stay visitors in Recife, the capital of Pernambuco state in north-east Brazil. It covers things to do in Recife in November 2026 with dates, venues, ticket platforms and practical notes.

The month opens with the final weekend of the Festival de Circo do Brasil, a ten-day circus and street-arts festival. Mid-month brings a Céu concert on Saturday 14 November and a long holiday weekend from Friday 20 November.

We only list events we could confirm on an organiser or ticket page. Listings with no confirmed Recife date or venue were left out, and that is why this guide is shorter than the usual city calendar.

Prices are in reais (R$). We convert at R$5.51 per US$1, the RT market data close for 6 November 2026.

Circus Festival Finale: 6 to 8 November

The 20th Festival de Circo do Brasil, themed “Rebuliço” (Portuguese for a lively commotion), runs from 30 October to 8 November in Recife and the surrounding metropolitan area. The organisers describe a mix of shows, workshops and open-air activities with artists from Brazil and abroad.

Paid shows are sold through Sympla, a Brazilian online ticketing platform. Prices for the shows listed below run from R$10 to R$60 (about US$1.80 to US$10.90).

Saturday 7 November, 20:00, and Sunday 8 November, 17:00 {Fé}sta Teatro do Parque · R$30 to R$60 (about US$5.45 to US$10.90) · Sympla

Sunday 8 November, 18:30 Rebuliço no Cabaré das Palhaças Teatro de Santa Isabel · R$10 and R$20 (about US$1.80 and US$3.60) · Sympla This is the festival’s closing show at the Santa Isabel, performed by a company of women clowns from Pernambuco.

Saturday 14 November: Céu Turns 20 on Stage

Saturday 14 November, 18:00 to Sunday 15 November, 02:00 SESSIONS apresenta: Céu 20 anos – ao vivo em Recife Cachaçaria Carvalheira, Avenida Sul Governador Cid Sampaio, 4921, Imbiribeira · Paid event · Sympla Céu is a Brazilian singer-songwriter, and the show is billed as a 20-year anniversary concert. The promoter is Golarrolê, a Recife events company, and the show is presented by the SESSIONS concert series. Sympla lists three ticket types: Inteira (full price), Meia (half price, with proof of eligibility) and Social (discounted, with a donation of non-perishable food or clothing).

The Sympla page does not show prices in the version we read. Check the listing for current prices and availability, because we could not see whether tickets are close to selling out.

The listing sets an age rating of 18, and guests must show an original, valid photo ID at the entrance. Card payments carry a 10% convenience fee and a 2% transaction fee on top of the ticket price, and instalments of up to 12 payments are offered.

The venue is in Imbiribeira, a southern district of Recife. The show runs past midnight, so plan your ride home in advance.

Holidays and the Long Weekend

Sunday 15 November is Republic Day, which marks the proclamation of the Brazilian republic in 1889. It falls on a Sunday this year, so it does not create a day off.

Friday 20 November is Black Consciousness Day, a national holiday since Federal Law 14,759 of 21 December 2023. Banks and public offices close, and the day gives you a three-day weekend from 20 to 22 November.

We did not find a confirmed Recife programme for that weekend at the time of writing. Check the city hall and Sympla listings closer to the date.

Planning Your Recife November

November is one of the drier months in Recife. The national weather institute INMET (Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia) lists a 1981–2010 average of 38.7 mm of rain, with lows near 22.7°C (73°F) and highs near 30.1°C (86°F).

Averages hide individual days, so carry a light rain jacket and check the forecast before outdoor screenings. INMET says November 2019 saw only 3.9 mm, so the range between years is wide.

Carry some cash and a card for small purchases around the venues, and book a ride home before the last show ends. Recife is hot and humid, so drink water and wear light clothes for the open-air parts of the festival.

The Recife metro’s Linha Sul (South Line) has closed an hour earlier, at 22:00, from Monday to Saturday since 12 October 2026. The operator, CBTU (Companhia Brasileira de Trens Urbanos, the federal urban train company), links this to roof repairs at Afogados and Joana Bezerra stations.

No completion date has been published. The Céu show runs past midnight, long after the last train, so use a licensed ride-hailing app rather than walking, and keep phones out of sight in crowds.

Check CBTU for the latest timetable before you travel. For events in this guide, buy tickets only from the Sympla page linked in the sources.

Some organisers change venues or times after listing, so look again the day before you go.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the main events in Recife in November 2026?

The 20th Festival de Circo do Brasil closes on Sunday 8 November. Singer Céu plays Cachaçaria Carvalheira on Saturday 14 November.

Are there public holidays in Recife in November 2026?

Republic Day falls on Sunday 15 November, so no weekday is lost. Black Consciousness Day is a national holiday on Friday 20 November, which makes a three-day weekend.

Where can I buy tickets for Recife events?

Most paid shows in this guide sell through Sympla, a Brazilian ticketing platform. Céu tickets are on Sympla, and the circus festival also sells paid shows there.

Can I take the metro home from late shows in Recife?

Not for late shows. From Monday to Saturday, the Linha Sul now closes at 22:00 because of roof repairs, so book a ride-hailing car for late events.

World.title: Machado Joins Families at Venezuela Prison
World.content:
Key Facts —Who. Opposition leader María Corina Machado, the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize winner, went to El Rodeo I, a prison near Caracas. —What. She read the names of more than 400 people she says are held for political reasons. Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado, who won the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize for her campaign for democracy, went to the El Rodeo I prison near Caracas on Friday 6 November 2026. She joined families who have kept a vigil there for more than 300 days, putting Venezuela’s political prisoners back in front of US readers who follow Washington’s policy toward Caracas.

What We Know

El Rodeo I is a prison in Miranda state, near the capital Caracas, that human rights groups often cite in reports on detention for political reasons. The Nobel Peace Prize is the international award Machado received in 2025 for her campaign for democratic rights in Venezuela.

Machado went to the prison on Friday and stood outside, in front of it. She came to back families who have kept a continuous vigil there for more than 300 days.

Latin America Power Index · November 2026 edition Venezuela ranks 12th of 14 with 29.4 points. Strongest pillar: military means (81); weakest: economic relationships (0). Alignment group: Closer to Beijing. Some pillar data are incomplete for Venezuela; see the index notes. WatchSovereign in selective default; inflation of 252%; public debt at 309% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

The families are mothers, wives, sons and daughters who demand freedom for relatives held for political reasons. Machado said she came so that they know they are not alone.

She read aloud the names of more than 400 people she says are held for political reasons, meaning jailed for opposing or criticising the government. She said many other cases are unrecorded because relatives fear reporting detentions, and that many of those held are disappeared.

Machado said twenty-three political prisoners have died in state custody since 2015. She added that the names she read “alone add up to 1,756 years of prison.”

She then made a pledge to the families and the detainees. “We will not rest until the last political prisoner, civilian and military, obtains full freedom,” she said, adding that this means all of them.

She called out to the prisoners from a spot where she could be heard inside. Venezuelan news reports say the prisoners answered with freedom chants.

We could not independently confirm the chants or the exact words shouted. She closed by telling the families, “I am here with you, you are not alone,” and called for freedom for all political prisoners.

Machado returned to Venezuela in late October 2026. In December 2025 she warned of threats against prisoners at El Rodeo I.

Venezuelans hold flags and “Venezuela Libre” (Free Venezuela) signs at a diaspora rally in Quebec City, Canada, in July 2024. (Photo: Wilfredor / Wikimedia Commons, CC0)

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether the authorities responded to the visit or allowed any contact with prisoners. We also do not know what Venezuela’s government, led by interim president Delcy Rodríguez, says about her presence outside the prison.

Sources give different counts of the prisoners now held at El Rodeo I, so we do not state one. It is also not known whether any releases are planned.

It is not known whether Machado will return to the prison or visit other facilities. It is also unconfirmed what, if anything, the prisoners shouted back.

What It Means for US Readers

Many US readers follow Venezuela closely, including the treatment of political prisoners and the debate over sanctions. A Nobel laureate at a prison gate keeps that question visible, though we do not know how the authorities will respond.

Machado’s Nobel Prize gives her statements wide reach with international audiences, which is why her words are quoted at length here. We report them as her claims and figures, not as findings verified by others.

This event is a political signal, not a policy decision or a market event. Readers tracking Venezuela should watch for any official response and for any word on releases.

Frequently Asked Questions

Where did Machado go on 6 November 2026?

She went to El Rodeo I prison in Miranda state, Venezuela, and stood outside in front of it.

Why did she go?

She went to back families who have kept a continuous vigil outside for more than 300 days. They are demanding freedom for relatives held for political reasons.

What did she say?

She said twenty-three political prisoners have died in state custody since 2015 and vowed not to rest until the last one is free. She also read the names of more than 400 people.

How did the prisoners respond?

Venezuelan news reports say prisoners answered with freedom chants. We could not independently confirm this or the words shouted.

In December 2025 Renault Morocco signed three collective agreements, covering Somaca, the Tangier plant and Renault Commerce Maroc. The Tangier agreement, with the UMT union, was renewed for the third time.

The agreements cover about 10,000 workers and include new provisions on job security through training for automation and new technology. Mohamed Bachiri, Renault’s managing director in Morocco, called it a decisive step for the group’s social model.

A voluntary departure scheme means employees choose to leave, usually with a payment, rather than being dismissed. At 850 people it would be a visible share of the plant workforce.

The press reports say management briefed team leaders and began listing the workers concerned. We cannot say whether the scheme exists, and the report stays unconfirmed until Renault Morocco or a union speaks.

In Plain English, Who Is Who

Renault Morocco is the group’s Moroccan business, which runs the Tangier and Somaca factories. The UMT, or Union Marocaine du Travail, is one of the country’s main labour unions and represents Tangier workers.

Somaca is Renault’s other Moroccan factory, in Casablanca. Renault Commerce Maroc is the group’s sales entity in the country.

For US readers, Morocco is a car-export base, since 84% of Renault’s Moroccan output goes abroad. Investors who follow Renault should wait for a company statement before treating the report as fact.

World.title: A Proposed 15% Tax Would Reach Costa Rica Residents’ Foreign Dividends and Interest
World.content:
Costa Rica residents who earn interest, dividends, rent or capital gains outside the country would pay a 15% tax on that income under a bill the government has sent to the Legislative Assembly, a change tax specialists say would break with the country’s long-standing territorial tax system.

The bill, presented by the Finance Ministry on Sept. 22, would tax five types of passive income earned abroad by Costa Rican tax residents: interest, dividends, royalties, rent and capital gains. It would apply to individuals as well as companies, trusts, investment funds and other structures that are tax residents in Costa Rica.

The proposal sets no minimum threshold. Daniel Pelecano, director of tax and legal services at Grant Thornton, said that means small and large investors would be taxed on the same terms. Costa Rica has generally taxed income based on where it is generated rather than where the earner lives. A 2023 reform, Law 10.381, taxed some foreign passive income, but only for certain entities in multinational groups that failed to meet economic-substance requirements.

The new bill would repeal those limits and make tax residency the deciding factor for passive income. It keeps the territorial rule for active income, such as earnings from work or a business. In the bill’s statement of reasons, the Finance Ministry argues that the 2023 rules reached very few taxpayers. It also says residents receiving the same foreign dividends or interest are treated differently depending on whether they belong to a multinational group.

The ministry says the bill takes into account tax already paid or withheld abroad in order to avoid double taxation. Tax specialists say the mechanism works as a deduction rather than a direct credit, with the foreign tax subtracted from the income before Costa Rica applies its own rate.

Tax lawyer Gabriel Zamora Baudrit illustrated the effect with $100 in US dividends that have already had $30 withheld. Costa Rica would apply its 15% rate to the remaining $70, collecting $10.50 and bringing the combined tax burden to 40.5%. Under a direct credit capped at the Costa Rican amount, the $30 already paid would exceed Costa Rica’s $15 charge, leaving nothing more to pay. Zamora said the bill’s formula falls short of that standard and amounts to a new tax on residents’ foreign passive income, not simply a 15% rate.

Companies that already pay corporate income tax would follow a different route. Rather than paying the flat 15%, they would add the foreign passive income to their taxable profits, which are taxed at rates of up to 30%. Marianela Masís, director of tax and legal services at PwC Costa Rica, said the bill is not a full worldwide income tax because it is limited to certain passive income. She said those most affected would be tax residents who now receive passive income from abroad and fall outside the special regime for multinational groups.

Specialists said retirees who live on returns from investments abroad could fall within the bill’s scope. How pension funds would be treated remains one of several open questions, along with the double-taxation formula, the lack of a threshold and how far the exception to territoriality should reach.

Central Bank President Róger Madrigal said in October that the tax could discourage residents from investing abroad, depending on how foreign tax rates compare with local ones. He said dollars brought back into the country would only affect the exchange rate if they were converted into colones and that the local financial system was deep enough to absorb any inflow.

The bill has only begun its passage through the Assembly, and its text could change. Tax specialists say it would need 38 votes if lawmakers classify it as a new tax, or 29 if it is treated as a reform of existing law. The Finance Ministry has not published an estimate of how much the tax would raise. The proposal comes as the government confronts a revenue shortfall that has already forced cuts across the 2027 budget.

World.title: Local Elections Drove Costa Rica’s CPTPP Reversal, Sources Say
World.content:
Concerns about the 2028 municipal elections helped drive Costa Rica’s decision to abandon its bid to join the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), according to four people linked to the accession process who spoke to local reporters on condition of anonymity. The government has not responded to their accounts.

President Laura Fernández announced on Oct. 28 that she would shelve the accession and dismissed Foreign Trade Minister Indiana Trejos the same day. The previous administration of Rodrigo Chaves had announced, days before the current government took office, that it had concluded negotiations on the substantive terms of Costa Rica’s entry.

The CPTPP has been in force since 2018 and has 12 members: Japan, Australia, New Zealand, Brunei, Chile, Mexico, Canada, Peru, Vietnam, Singapore, Malaysia and the United Kingdom.

The sources’ accounts center on an Oct. 9 meeting at Casa Presidencial, where the president and Chaves, now Minister of Finance and of the Presidency, convened 46 organizations to review the agreement. One attendee said about 40 municipalities in agricultural areas, along with other business groups, opposed the deal.

That attendee said pushing ahead could have jeopardized those municipalities’ ties to the ruling Pueblo Soberano party. Attendees said Chaves defended the agreement at the meeting on free-market grounds. At the same meeting, the president asked Trejos to organize working groups with productive sectors and set Nov. 23 as the deadline to decide whether to sign the accession protocol, according to the sources. Some of them described the meeting as a formality, arguing the decision had already been made.

Agricultural groups protested outside Casa Presidencial on Oct. 9, and several organizations marched against the agreement on Nov. 3. Chaves publicly backed the reversal on Oct. 29. In a government video, he said he fully supported the president’s decision and noted that he had authorized the Foreign Trade Ministry to begin negotiations, citing access to a market of about 600 million consumers.

The sources also described friction over how the deal was handled. One said the government’s new approach included criticism of the way the Foreign Trade Ministry negotiated and of its failure to share information with business chambers. Trejos reportedly sought permission from the bloc’s 12 members to make the negotiated protocol public. According to the sources, that permission was not granted, and the text has not been released.

Costa Rica already has trade agreements with six CPTPP members: Mexico, Canada, Peru, Chile, Singapore and the United Kingdom. One source said the main additional benefit of membership would have been access to the Japanese market. The Presidency had not answered questions about the accounts submitted by local reporters on Nov. 3. The government has not publicly explained the reasons for the reversal beyond the president’s Oct. 28 announcement.

The bloc’s ministerial meeting in Vietnam, scheduled for Nov. 23 to 27, would have been Costa Rica’s first as a participant. With the accession shelved, the country’s existing bilateral agreements remain its main framework for trade with the Asia-Pacific region.

World.title: Your $1,000 Now Buys 46,810 Fewer Colones Than in January
World.content:
The US dollar slipped again in Costa Rica this week, leaving anyone who earns in dollars and spends in colones with noticeably less buying power than at the start of the year. The average rate on Monex, the Central Bank’s wholesale foreign exchange market, closed at 450.26 colones on Thursday, Nov. 5, according to Central Bank data. That was down from 453.81 on Oct. 26 and the lowest daily average since at least that date.

The Central Bank’s reference rate for Friday, Nov. 6, stood at 453.34 colones to sell dollars and 448.27 to buy them. A day earlier, the reference rate was 454.41 to sell and 449.63 to buy. The longer view shows the scale of the shift. On Jan. 2, the Monex average was 497.07 colones, which means Thursday’s close was 46.81 colones lower, a drop of about 9.4% since the start of 2026.

In practical terms, $1,000 converted at the Monex average on Jan. 2 would have brought 497,070 colones. At Thursday’s average, the same amount brings 450,260 colones, a difference of 46,810 colones, or about $104 at current rates. The decline cuts both ways. People paid in dollars and spending in colones, from exporters and tourism businesses to retirees receiving pensions from abroad, lose purchasing power as the rate falls, while households that earn colones and owe dollar-denominated rent or loans pay less to cover them.

The weak dollar has already squeezed some sectors that sell to foreigners, including medical tourism, where revenue measured in colones has fallen. The Monex average first dropped below 450 colones on July 17, when it reached 449.95, at the time the lowest level since the market opened in 2006. The Central Bank described the Costa Rica’s dollar surplus as extraordinary earlier this year and has bought dollars in the market to limit sharper falls.

The broader picture is one of abundant dollars, with the Costa Rica’s dollar supply hitting a record two decades after the end of scheduled devaluations. Monex is the wholesale market where banks and other authorized institutions trade dollars with one another, so its average does not match the price at a bank window. Banks and exchange houses set their own buying and selling prices around the Central Bank’s reference rate, which is published every business day.

World.title: 5,000 Shareholders, No Dividends and a Court Order for Hospital CIMA’s Top Executive
World.content:
A civil court in San José has ordered Clifton Neal Orme, the legal representative of Hospital CIMA, to appear in person and testify in a case brought by minority shareholders who say they have spent years trying to recover their investment in one of Costa Rica’s best-known private hospitals.

The order, issued Oct. 20 by the Second Collegiate Civil Court of First Instance is part of a pre-trial evidence proceeding. That type of proceeding gathers testimony and documents before a full lawsuit is filed, and the court has made no finding of wrongdoing. Neal must personally answer the shareholders’ questions as a party to the case and identify and produce any documents put to him.

He must also present an account of his administration, including a detailed list of the company’s assets and liabilities for 2025. The company, registered as Hospital San José S.A., must hand over a certified copy of the minutes of its Feb. 23, 2026, shareholders’ meeting and its financial statements for 2025.

The court warned that if Neal fails to appear without justification, refuses to answer or responds evasively, it may apply article 42.2 of the Civil Procedure Code. Under certain conditions, that provision allows a judge to treat the facts raised in the questioning as true. A hearing set for Oct. 29 was called off because the court had not yet appointed an English interpreter for Neal, who does not speak Spanish. The hospital must deposit 92,660 colones (about $204) to cover four hours of interpretation, and the court will set a new date once the case file is ready.

The proceeding was filed by shareholder Francisco Castro, who holds 17,336 shares. Panacea JSG S.A., a company represented by 79-year-old investor José Jop, joined as an interested party with 528,748 shares, or about 1.91% of the hospital’s capital.

The court rejected the shareholders’ request for a court-appointed expert to audit the company. Their combined stake of about 1.92% falls short of the 10% that article 26 of the Commercial Code requires for that measure, the court ruled, though it granted their other requests for financial and corporate records. Hospital CIMA’s legal representation said the company will comply with whatever the court requires of it through the proper legal channels. Because the matter is ongoing, it said it would not comment on specific proceedings or on the documents requested.

The case is the latest chapter in a long-running dispute between the hospital and its small investors. Sebastián Vargas, the attorney representing Jop, has said the company has more than 5,000 individual and corporate shareholders, some of whom say they have gone more than two decades without a dividend or a way to sell their stakes.

According to audited financial statements cited in local press reports, the company posted cumulative losses of more than 16.9 billion colones (about $37 million at current exchange rates) between 2019 and 2024. Hospital San José S.A. also appears among the large taxpayers that reported losses or zero taxable income to the Finance Ministry for four consecutive fiscal years, from 2021 through 2024.

The same statements show the balance owed to the hospital by International Hospital Corporation (IHC), a Dallas, Texas-based company related to the controlling shareholder, rose from $11.9 million in 2023 to $13.3 million in 2024. IHC designed and built the hospital, which opened in Escazú in 2000 and has long served the country’s medical tourism market.

Only one minority shareholder is known to have won a case against the hospital. In 2023, a court granted physician Manfred Freer the right to withdraw from the company and be paid for his shares, plus dividends, interest and costs, after finding the hospital had recorded profits in two consecutive periods without distributing them. The Supreme Court’s First Chamber upheld that ruling on April 10, 2025.

During that case, the hospital argued that withholding profits reflected a shareholder agreement to reinvest in its operations and maintain quality of care. A court-ordered appraisal later valued each of Freer’s shares at $6.32, against the $1 per share the hospital had maintained. The dispute has also reached the criminal courts. In December 2025, the hospital and Neal filed a criminal complaint for alleged extortion against Jop and Vargas after Jop raised options for recovering his money, including going to the press.

The Pavas Criminal Court dismissed that complaint, and the Specialized Criminal Court for Organized Crime upheld the dismissal on Sept. 30, 2026. Public registry records list Neal as vice president of Hospital San José S.A. and Gary Brent Wood as its president. No new date has been set for Neal’s testimony. Evidence gathered in pre-trial proceedings of this kind is typically used to decide whether to file a full civil lawsuit.

World.title: Pope Leo XIV Departs for First Latin America Journey to Uruguay Argentina and Peru
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV leaves Rome on Friday, November 6, 2026, for a twelve-day apostolic journey to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. The Holy See Press Office published the full itinerary in September and reconfirmed it this week, with no changes. The trip marks the first Latin America visit of his pontificate. It covers three countries and ten cities, with roughly a dozen flights, nine public Masses, seven cathedral visits and two stadium prayer vigils. Matteo Bruni, director of the Holy See Press Office, said the Pope is enthusiastic about the journey and that the program remains intact.

In Uruguay, from November 6 to 8, Leo XIV visits Montevideo, Paysandú and Florida. The motto is “I bring you news of great joy.” He arrives at Carrasco International Airport in the afternoon of November 6, holds a welcome ceremony at Plaza Independencia, meets authorities and the diplomatic corps, and visits President Yamandú Orsi. He celebrates vespers at the Metropolitan Cathedral.

The next day he flies to Paysandú for Mass, returns to Montevideo for a meeting in the Casavalle neighborhood and a session with the education community at the Catholic University of Uruguay, then leads a prayer vigil at Centenario Stadium. On November 8 he celebrates Mass at the National Shrine of Our Lady of the Thirty-Three in Florida before flying to Buenos Aires.

Argentina receives him from November 8 to 11. The motto is “Welcome everyone. Go and proclaim.” He arrives at Aeroparque Jorge Newbery, visits the monument to General José de San Martín, holds a welcome ceremony at Casa Rosada and meets President Javier Milei.

The program includes a visit to the Pequeño Cottolengo Don Orione in Claypole, Mass at the Monumento de los Españoles, a meeting with workers at the Catholic University of Argentina, an interreligious gathering, vespers with bishops and synodal teams at the Metropolitan Cathedral, a flight to Córdoba for Mass and a clergy meeting, a youth vigil back in Buenos Aires, a visit to the federal prison complex and Mass at the Basilica of Our Lady of Luján.

This is the first papal visit to Argentina since St. John Paul II in 1987. Argentina is the homeland of the late Pope Francis. Peru is the longest and most personal stage, from November 11 to 17. The motto is “Let us open our hearts.” Leo XIV arrives at Callao Air Base, holds a welcome ceremony at the Government Palace and meets the president. He visits Lima, Chiclayo, Cusco and Pucallpa.

Events include meetings with Peruvian bishops, a public gathering on challenges facing the country, a youth vigil at the National Stadium, Mass near Pimentel, a private visit to the San Óscar A.
