Climate change has also been raised as a possible factor influencing some of the atmospheric processes involved, although no direct link to the current exceptionally early disruption has been established.

For now, meteorologists are continuing to monitor developments, with the coming weeks expected to provide a clearer indication of whether the disturbance will translate into significant changes in winter weather across the Northern Hemisphere.

World.title: From gastronomy to sports: What to discover in Spain's Region of Valencia
World.content:
The Region of Valencia has long been a popular destination, with tourists flocking to hot spots like Alicante and Benidorm.

 

But as travellers look to develop a deeper connection with the countries they visit, other destinations are starting to have their moment in the spotlight.

Speaking at World Travel Market in London, José Manuel Camarero Benitez, the regional vice-minister for tourism for the Region of Valencia, shared with Euronews Travel how they have avoided the overtourism problems that other areas of Spain are facing.

“It’s not just promoting tourism – we try to manage tourism,” Camarero said. “We are not aiming to promote the same places, and telling people to go do the same things at the same time.

“We try to attract people outside of the peak season. For example, even now in November, we have sunshine and temperatures above 20 degrees so you can enjoy diving, swimming and other activities.”

The tourism board is currently running a campaign entitled “could this be happiness?”, which encourages visitors to discover happiness in the small things, like feeling the sand between your toes or seeing the shimmer of the sea.

The province of Castellón is ready for its moment in the spotlight Jack Coble/Unsplash

Castellón: The next hot destination

The provinces of Alicante and Valencia are already well known and loved, but Camarero thinks it’s time for Castellón to shine.

“I always say Alicante has been our success for 60 years in the Valencia region, now Castellón will be the next success,” he added, noting that the city is particularly known for its gastronomy.

Offering a diversity of experiences, you can dig into langoustine in Vinaròs, hike through the Sierra de Irta mountainscape, see ancient cave art in Ares del Maestrat, and go canyoning in Montanejos.

A big year for sport

The region of Valencia is also preparing for a big year of sport in 2027.

Over the course of the year, Valencia city will host the Copa del Rey basketball tournament, the European Indoor Athletics Championships, SailGP, and the MotoGP Valencia Grand Prix, while Alicante will host the start of The Ocean Race.

For golf fans, Alicante will also host the IAGTO European Convention in May, and Camarero is encouraging players to come discover the region’s offerings.

“It’s the best opportunity to come to Alicante to see all 30 sites and discover not only golf as a sport, but golf as a lifestyle, with gastronomy, culture and the other things you can enjoy during your stay,” he said.

Sustainability as key

The region of Valencia has long prioritised sustainability, with Valencia serving as the European Green Capital in 2024.

That will continue in 2028, with Benidorm handed the European Green Leaf award, which is for cities with between 20,000 and 100,000 inhabitants, last month.

“Sustainability is not just a word for us, it’s both the present and the future,” Camarero said.

World.title: A trip to the Philippines offers hidden gems, slow food and colourful events
World.content:
An archipelago of more than 7,000 islands in Southeast Asia, the Philippines offers everything from coastline and tropical rainforests to volcanic peaks.

 

Speaking to Euronews Travel at World Travel Market in London, Marga Nograles, COO at Tourism Promotions Board Philippines, described the country as tropical, and one that welcomes visitors in every season.

There is an “authentic experience for every traveller” at any time of the year, Nograles said. “From December to May, we have whale watching activities, which can be done in four destinations around the Philippines. Around that time also, we [have] perfect island hopping experiences, [for travellers] visiting all our award-winning beach resorts.”

For adventure tourists, she recommended visiting Siargao Island from September to January for watersports when waves can reach as high as around nine feet.

“We have many surfers coming into the Philippines at that time,” she said. “That is also the best for canyoneering and doing the sardine run.”

The Ruins in Bacolod Tourism Promotions Board Philippines

Hidden gems in the Philippines

Beyond the capital, Manila, Nograles shared the Philippines’ must-visit destinations.

“Siquijor remains one of our hidden gems, with beautiful beaches, waterfalls, and rich local tradition,” she said.

The third smallest province across the country, Siquijor features white sand beaches, crystal clear waters and rich marine biodiversity. Visitors can enjoy kayaking, trekking and snorkelling in the Caticugan Marine Protected Area, among other popular activities to do on the island.

In Pampanga, Nograles recommended Clark for being an accessible getaway and an area that has a “rich history, exciting culinary culture, and growing leisure opportunities”.

She also spotlighted how Camiguin, an island home to 14 volcanoes, was listed among The New York Times’ 52 Places to Go in 2026, making it the only province in the Philippines to receive such international distinction.

“Its volcanic landscapes, waterfalls and natural springs make it a wonderful destination for nature and adventure,” she said.

The coastal country offers visitors no shortage of seafood dishes Avel Chuklanov/Unsplash

Food tourism: Where to eat in the Philippines

Nicknamed the “heart of the Philippines”, Iloilo City was named as a Creative City of Gastronomy in 2023 by UNESCO and is home to more than 300 restaurants.

"It's very interesting to come visit because their cuisine is heavily inspired by the culture and traditions of that city," Nograles said.

UNESCO recognises Iloilo for its culture of "fiesta" and tradition of festive banquets. Since 2021, the province has also held Timplada, an event that showcases local cuisine. This includes educational activities focused on Iloilo culinary heritage.

Bacolod, an urbanised city on the northwest coast of Negros Island, became the first international Slow Food Hub in Asia and the Pacific, according to the Slow Food Foundation.

“Bacolod City is a slow food hub in Asia and the centre for sustainable gastronomy,” said Nograles. “Negros Occidental also is the organic capital of the Philippines.”

She recommends visiting Carbin Reef in Negros Occidental. It’s a sandbar where visitors can sample "kinilaw", which is a traditional Filipino seafood dish where raw fish is marinated in vinegar, diced into cubes and accompanied with tomato, red onions, ginger and lemon zest.

MassKara Festival in Bacolod Sherwin Ballesteros/Tourism Promotions Board Philippines

Colourful celebrations of faith, flowers and harvest

Nograles told Euronews Travel that the country hosts more than 40,000 festivals each year. And there are three in particular that she highlights for travellers.

“First is the Sinulog, which is in Cebu in the Visayas,” she said. “Sinulog is a celebration of faith. In the Philippines, they celebrate the Señor Santo Niño (the Holy Child Jesus).

"During this time, the whole city stops because everyone is celebrating in the streets. They take out their boats. And everyone has their face painted. The energy is unlike any other.”

In the southern city of Davao, the Kadayawan Festival is a celebration of harvest. “There are different concerts, also street dancing,” she said. “[There are] also the freshest fruits around that time so, we also get a lot of visitors coming in – so it would be nice to come visit and try the fruits of the south of the Philippines.”

Further north of the archipelago is where the month-long Panagbenga Festival takes place. "That is a celebration of the flowers," she said. "So all kinds of flowers are in bloom up the mountains during that time."

World.title: Starring Great Britain: How set-jetting is helping distribute tourists across the regions
World.content:
From the white cliffs of Dover to the lochs of Scotland, Great Britain has so much to offer tourists. Yet for many travellers, the only place they see is London.

 

While the UK capital is fantastic, tourists are missing out by not venturing beyond the M25 – and the regions are failing to benefit from the economic benefits that come from additional visitors, too.

Tourist board VisitBritain is tasked with encouraging people to do just that, and one of its major campaigns is “Starring GREAT Britain”, which highlights the real-life destinations featured in movies and TV shows shot there.

Launched in January 2025, VisitBritain has a map of all the filming locations you can stop at, as well as suggested itineraries split by region. For example, the Scottish Highlands itinerary takes you to scenic spots as seen in Outlander, The Diplomat and Downton Abbey.

The UK is also a popular spot for film crews, so the page is constantly being updated following new launches like Wuthering Heights earlier this year and will be added to after the new Harry Potter series comes out.

Great Britain on screen

At World Travel Market in London, VisitBritain CEO Patricia Yates told Euronews Travel about the campaign.

“It’s absolutely essential to what we do to get visitors to explore more outside of London, and we do that in two ways,” she said.

“One is the practicality – we're a small island, travel is really easy. It’s a couple of hours to Manchester or Liverpool, or you can fly into Manchester, then it's three hours up to Newcastle and Scotland.

“The second way is, of course, why should you go, compelling storytelling. I would say ‘Starring GREAT Britain’ has shown that we can do that using the power of film.

“What we're seeing is that every region has a story to tell. And the tourism industry is coming in behind us and building tourism product that’s bookable for international visitors.”

Set-jetting has been a major travel trend for years now, with destinations seeing big boosts in visitor numbers thanks to shows and films like Game of Thrones, The White Lotus, and Dune.

Alnwick Castle Clement Proust/Unsplash

Tourism has a distribution problem

Many European countries are battling with problematic concentrations of tourists in cities that just can’t handle any more visitors, leading to protests from locals.

While London can handle the number of tourists it currently sees, VisitBritain is careful to not send people to smaller destinations that are reaching their limit.

“It's absolutely imperative that we deliver tourism that benefits businesses, but also benefits local communities, and that is forefront in our minds,” Yates added.

“We do that by looking at where we send visitors, making sure we're promoting places that have the infrastructure, have the capacity and want visitors at that time of year. And we don't promote places that don't want visitors and that are feeling the pinch a bit.”

Like all tourism boards, VisitBritain also wants to attract “good” visitors.

“It is someone that comes and explores and wants to know more about a destination, and it is someone who spends longer and takes time,” she said.

“I think that is a trend that we're seeing with all international travel. We all want that emotional, personal connection and time to slow down a little.”

Head to England’s north east

Aside from all of the set-jetting itineraries, Yates highlighted the north east of England as somewhere to add to your must-visit list.

The historical theme park Kynren just opened there in July, and sees 1,200 local performers telling the story of England.

Plus, for Potterheads, the stunning Alnwick Castle in Northumberland is where Harry Potter learned to ride a broomstick.

World.title: US measles cases exceed 5,000 in 2026, reaching their highest level in 35 years
World.content:
A total of 5,182 confirmed cases of the highly contagious but vaccine-preventable disease have been reported nationwide in 2026, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the country's leading public health agency.

 

The figure is more than double the 2,289 cases recorded throughout 2025 and represents the highest number reported by the CDC since 1991.

State health authorities have reported at least eight measles-related deaths, including among very young children.

Measles deaths raise alarm among doctors

Paediatric infectious disease specialist Adam Ratner told AFP that such fatalities were “tragic, and that is completely preventable”.

Measles was declared eliminated in the United States in 2000, largely as a result of widespread vaccination. However, the disease has made a significant comeback in recent years, fuelled by declining vaccination rates and growing public distrust of health authorities.

US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., a long-standing vaccine sceptic, has faced criticism for contributing to that distrust.

“Robert F. Kennedy Jr. does not believe that measles is a big problem and does not want to believe that there are deaths from measles,” Ratner said.

“The burden of these diseases will fall on children, who are not the ones who are making these decisions,” he added.

Measles typically causes fever, respiratory symptoms and a characteristic skin rash. In more serious cases, it can lead to complications including pneumonia and inflammation of the brain, potentially resulting in lasting health problems or death.

Before the introduction of the measles vaccine in 1963, an estimated 400 to 500 people died from the disease every year in the United States, according to the CDC.

World.title: Foreign buyers push Spanish home sales to record 16% amid record prices
World.content:
The presence of foreign buyers in the property market keeps growing. During the third quarter of the year, their transactions accounted for 16.05% of all home sales, the highest share since records began. In absolute terms, more than 26,300 transactions were completed, according to the latest data published by the College of Registrars.

 

More than half of these purchases, specifically 54.7%, were made by citizens of the European Union, while a further 17.8% corresponded to buyers from the rest of Europe.

By nationality, British buyers topped the ranking, with 7.5% of all purchases made by foreigners. They were followed by Moroccan citizens, with 6.4%, and Dutch buyers, with 5.8%.

The weight of international demand was particularly significant in island and Mediterranean markets. The Balearic Islands led the table, with 37.2% of sales in foreign hands, followed by the Valencian Community, with 30.4%. In the rest of the autonomous communities, this share was below 30%.

House prices hit new highs again

The residential market continues to show strong upward pressure on prices. The College of Registrars' Repeat Sales House Price Index recorded a year on year increase of 15.8% in the third quarter, while compared with the previous three months it rose by 5.2%. Both movements took the index to a new all time high.

The average home price reached 2,512 euros per square metre. By type, existing homes stood at 2,462 euros/m2 after posting a quarterly increase of 0.6%. New build homes reached 2,701 euros/m2, with a rise of 2.5%.

Despite these figures, the evolution of average prices points to a moderation in the pace of growth. According to this methodology, the increase was 1% on a quarterly basis and 9.3% compared with the same period a year earlier.

By autonomous community, Madrid recorded the highest average price, at 4,565 euros/m2, followed closely by the Balearic Islands, at 4,502 euros/m2. Next came the Basque Country (3,693 euros/m2), Catalonia (2,989 euros/m2) and the Canary Islands (2,850 euros/m2).

The ranking by provincial capitals once again puts San Sebastián in first place, with 6,662 euros per square metre. Madrid is in second place, with 5,597 euros/m2, followed by Barcelona (5,124), Palma (4,408) and Bilbao (3,877).

Home sales fall for the third consecutive quarter

Against the backdrop of rising prices, activity in the residential market is starting to show signs of cooling. During the third quarter, home sales fell by 5.9% year on year, according to the registrars' data.

The comparison with the previous quarter is also negative. Transactions fell by 2.3%, marking three consecutive quarters of declines. Between July and September 164,148 sales were recorded, the lowest volume in the last nine quarters.

By segment, new build homes accounted for 34,611 transactions, 0.9% fewer than in the previous quarter. Existing homes generated most of the activity, with 129,537 transactions, although they also saw a drop of 2.6%. Quarterly declines spread across ten autonomous communities and 27 provinces.

Mortgages also fall in the third quarter

Mortgage financing followed a similar trend. Between July and September, 124,145 mortgages on homes were registered, a quarterly reduction of 3.9%. This figure is equivalent to 75.6% of all home sales recorded during the period.

However, the balance for the last twelve months remains positive. In that time, 519,388 mortgages on homes were taken out, 6% more than in the previous twelve months.

Andalusia recorded the highest number of mortgage transactions in the third quarter, with 23,635, followed by Catalonia with 23,268. The Community of Madrid registered 18,240 transactions and the Valencian Community 15,692.

As for the mortgage amount per square metre, Madrid was again in the lead, with 3,158 euros/m2. The Balearic Islands were in second place, with 2,987 euros/m2, followed by the Basque Country (2,392) and Catalonia (2,248).

The data depict a property market marked by an apparent contradiction: while prices continue to break records and foreign demand becomes more prominent, the number of sales has been falling for several quarters.

World.title: Nearly 1,000 migrants rescued from seven boats off El Hierro in Spain
World.content:
Spain's Maritime Rescue Service (Salvamento Marítimo) has assisted 854 migrants aboard seven small, open motorised fishing vessels in waters off the Canary Island of El Hierro since the early hours of Friday morning. The boats were escorted to the harbour of La Restinga, in the municipality of El Pinar, where those on board received medical attention.

 

Of those brought ashore, 350 were transferred to Tenerife on the scheduled morning ferry service. The Spanish authorities are planning to relocate a further 350 migrants on Friday afternoon's crossing to ease pressure on reception facilities on El Hierro.

Several of those rescued required hospital treatment. Nine people remain at Nuestra Señora de los Reyes Hospital after arriving on El Hierro aboard different vessels in recent days, suffering from various health problems.

Friday's rescue operation involved three Salvamento Marítimo vessels: Salvamar Navia, Diphda and Mizar. The first intervention took place four miles from the port of La Restinga, where the first boat was located. Salvamar Navia escorted it to the quay, which it reached at around 1:00 am with 134 people on board.

The remaining boats arrived at staggered intervals throughout the morning. The second cayuco docked at 4:45 am, carrying 174 people, followed by a third vessel just 15 minutes later with 166 migrants on board.

The largest boat of the day arrived at 8:30 am, carrying 235 people. A fifth boat brought a further 54 migrants ashore at around 9 am, while another 39 disembarked from the sixth vessel, which reached the harbour at approximately 10:15 am. The final boat arrived at La Restinga at 12:30 pm with 52 people on board.

According to information provided by health and emergency services, those aboard the seven vessels were of sub-Saharan African origin. Most were men, although women and minors were also among the passengers. Their points of departure and the specific countries of origin of those on board have not yet been established.

The operation at La Restinga harbour involved members of the Red Cross Immediate Emergency Response Team (ERIE), the Canary Islands Emergency Service (SUC), port security personnel, the Civil Guard and the National Police.

Following initial medical and humanitarian assistance, the migrants were transferred to the Temporary Foreign Nationals Reception Centre (CATE) in San Andrés, in the municipality of Valverde. There, they will receive support from the NGO Corazón Naranja-Ebrima Sonko and remain in police custody pending their transfer to other reception facilities outside El Hierro.

More arrivals in Gran Canaria and Lanzarote

Migrant arrivals along the Canary Islands route have also been reported on other islands in the archipelago. At around 10 pm on Thursday, Spain's Maritime Rescue Service brought ashore an as-yet unconfirmed number of people rescued at sea in Arguineguín, on the southern coast of Gran Canaria.

On Lanzarote, two further groups of migrants arrived between 9 pm on Thursday and 8:30 am on Friday. The first group comprised 27 men of North African origin travelling in a small boat, while the second consisted of a further 61 people.

World.title: Trump appoints immigration hardliner Stephen Miller as new chief of staff
World.content:
US President Donald Trump on Friday appointed Stephen Miller, one of the most influential architects of his hardline immigration policy, as his new White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles just days after the Republican Party suffered a major defeat in the midterm elections.

 

Miller, 41, currently deputy chief of staff and homeland security adviser, will assume the position on Monday, November 9, Trump announced on his Truth Social platform.

“I am pleased to announce that Mr. Stephen Miller, the current Deputy Chief of Staff of the Trump Administration, and one of my most trusted advisors, will become the Chief of Staff,” Trump wrote.

Wiles, 69, the first woman to serve as White House chief of staff, will move to Trump's political operation. The president praised her performance, describing her tenure as outstanding.

Wiles confirmed her departure in a statement on X, saying that serving Trump in the White House had been “the honor of a lifetime”. She highlighted the administration's record on border security, tax cuts and its economic policies.

Miller has been one of Trump's closest advisers for more than a decade, dating back to his first presidential campaign in 2016. He has played a central role in shaping the administration's restrictive immigration policies, including its drive to carry out mass deportations during Trump's second term.

His promotion places one of the administration's most outspoken advocates of tougher immigration enforcement at the centre of White House decision-making.

The appointment also comes amid growing scrutiny of the administration's immigration operations, particularly following the fatal shootings of two protesters by immigration agents in Minneapolis in January, which triggered widespread demonstrations and criticism of federal enforcement tactics.

The personnel change follows a bruising midterm election for Republicans, with Democrats winning control of both chambers of Congress. The result represents a significant political setback for Trump and is likely to intensify scrutiny of his administration's domestic agenda.

Wiles had been widely regarded as an important organisational force within Trump's inner circle, helping manage competing interests and maintain discipline in the White House. Her departure also follows weeks of speculation about possible personnel changes, although the administration had previously rejected reports that she was about to be replaced.

By moving Wiles to his political operation and promoting Miller, Trump is reshaping his closest circle of advisers at a politically sensitive moment.

World.title: Paraguay Senate dismisses President Santiago Pena over bank crisis
World.content:
Paraguay’s Senate has ousted President Santiago Pena over the collapse of a major bank tied to his government. Millions of customers' accounts are frozen, with public pension and health care funds also tied up.

Paraguay's Senate on Friday impeached President Santiago Pena over a banking crisis that left millions of people unable to access their deposits.

Senators voted overwhelmingly to remove Pena for misconduct in office.

The move cleared the way for Vice President Pedro Alliana to succeed him. He will serve the rest of the presidential term, which ends in August 2028.

Pena had already resigned on Thursday, but by impeaching and convicting him instead of accepting his resignation, senators stripped him of the lifetime Senate seat and immunity granted to former presidents, leaving him vulnerable to prosecution.

Following the Senate vote, prosecutors ordered the arrest of the ousted president alongside former central bank chief Carlos Carvallo as part of a criminal investigation.

Officials later said Pena was placed under house arrest pending a decision by the public prosecutor's office on the final charges against him.

Dozens of ​protesters gathered outside ​his residence ‌in the capital Asuncion, while police maintained ​a ⁠security cordon around the property.

Why did Pena face impeachment?

Pena's rapid downfall came amid mounting pressure over the collapse of digital lender Ueno, one of the country's biggest banks, with which he had ties.

The bank's accounts — also used to process pension payments — are frozen, leaving millions of customers unable to access their money. Ueno also held hundreds of millions of dollars in public funds.

Pena's resignation on Thursday followed the withdrawal of support by Congress President Basilio Nunez and ruling conservative Colorado Party leader Horacio Cartes.

Thirty-five opposition lawmakers and ruling-party dissidents had submitted impeachment articles in the 80-seat Chamber of Deputies, accusing Pena of conflicts of interest, misuse of pension funds and institutional cover-ups linked to Ueno.

Pena sold his shares in Ueno Holding, whose businesses include the bank, in April 2025. Lawmakers also cited two loans he received from Ueno as part of allegations of improper financial gain.

They alleged improper presidential interference in the Social Security Institute, known as IPS, and preferential treatment for Ueno. IPS manages pension and health care funds for most Paraguayan workers and held $355 million at the bank — about 9% of its investments, according to financial manager Gladys Vera.

The motion also questioned Pena's 2023 appointment of central bank chief Carvallo, who previously chaired Financiera Ueno. According to the document, the central bank approved the company's conversion into a bank just 83 days after his appointment.

What happened to Ueno Bank?

Ueno served about 2.94 million customers, roughly 60% of Paraguay's adult population.

As of last month, the bank said it held roughly $800 million in public-sector deposits — about a quarter of its total deposits — including money from the operators of Paraguay's giant hydroelectric dams.

People took the the streets of Asuncion on Wednesday Image: Jorge Saenz/AP Photo/picture alliance

Paraguay's central bank ordered a resolution or closure process Tuesday after finding that Ueno's solvency ratio had fallen below half the required minimum.

Ueno's app, card payments and transfers stopped working, while branches closed, leaving customers queuing outside unable to withdraw their savings.

Hundreds of employees of Ueno and other companies in its parent conglomerate protested outside the Labor Ministry Thursday, demanding unpaid wages and severance.

Retirees, depositors, students and workers had marched through Asuncion a day earlier, demanding Pena's impeachment and holding signs saying "Give us back our money."

What have authorities done?

Authorities detained eight senior executives, including founder Miguel Vazquez and bank president Juan Manuel Gustale. Prosecutors also charged 27 bank officials and business associates with offenses including breach of trust and attempted fraud.

Lawyers for several detainees said they needed time to review the allegations before commenting.

Pena had sought to reassure customers in a video message Wednesday, pledging legislation "that will return to every saver what they are entitled to as quickly as possible."

The crisis also forced him to cancel his attendance at the Ibero-American summit in Madrid.

Pena, a conservative economist, took office in August 2023 for a five-year term.

Editor's Note: This piece, originally published on November 5, was updated on November 7 to reflect the latest developments.

World.title: Pope Leo arrives in Uruguay at start of South America tour
World.content:
Pope Leo has arrived in Uruguay at the start of a 12-day trip through three South American nations. His trip, which is intense with a packed itinerary, comes just weeks after his lung cancer surgery.

Pope Leo XIV arrived in Uruguay on Friday at the start of a grueling 12-day tour through three South American countries, just weeks after his lung cancer surgery.

The 71-year-old pontiff told reporters he was very happy to be in Uruguay, having flown a nearly 14-hour flight from Rome to get to Montevideo.

"I confess that from the first day, I had no doubt and was convinced that this trip had to go forward," he told reporters aboard the papal plane.

Leo hit the ground running on arrival, drawing huge crowds in Montevideo as he pulled into town in his open-sided popemobile.

The Vatican estimated 30,000 people had turned out to watch him go by and attend his first event in a country that is largely secular and where membership in the Church is declining.

"In an age ‌when ​differences can easily become a source of conflict, persevering ​in respect for the law, negotiation and the ⁠patient ​search for ​agreements is a service ​that Uruguay ‌can continue to offer its neighbors," ​Leo ⁠told crowds in Montevideo's main square.

Uruguayan President Yamandu Orsi, leader of the center-left alliance, was present there too.

Leo is then planning to visit the Casavalle neighborhood, which is notorious for its high rates of poverty and violence.

With starting in Uruguay, Leo marks the first papal visit to the country in nearly four decades, with Pope John Paul II having last visited in 1988.

What to know about Pope Leo's taxing itinerary

The pontiff will spend three days in Uruguay before heading on to Argentina on Sunday.

He then travels to Peru, where he spent half his priestly life, before he was elected pontiff last year. He became a naturalized Peruvian citizen in 2015.

Latin America is home to around 40% of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics, for whom the pope is their spiritual leader. However, fewer and fewer people on the continent identify as Catholic.

Enthusiasm around Leo's visit a surprise in Uruguay

Uruguay, the most secular Latin American country, was the first country in the world to legalize recreational marijuana use and has since legalized abortion, same-sex marriage and assisted dying, all against opposition from the Catholic Church.

However, the enthusiasm around Leo's visit has come as a bit of a surprise, with tickets for his prayer vigil at Montevideo's Centenario Stadium selling out in just two days.

The pope is expected to express opposition to some of the more liberal policies enacted in Uruguay Image: Lucas Aguayo Araos/Anadolu/picture alliance

What will Pope Leo do in Argentina?

On Sunday, Leo will cross over to neighboring Argentina, the home of his papal predecessor Francis, who, however, disappointed his native compatriots by never returning home as pope.

At the beginning of Francis's papacy, some 71% of Argentinians identified as Catholic, according to the Pew Research Center. By 2024, this had fallen to 58%.

Leo will hope his visit makes up for the refusal by his predecessor to visit his home country Image: Agustin Marcarian/REUTERS

Leo is set to meet with Argentinian President Javier Milei, who has come under criticism from the Catholic Church for his sweeping cuts that have hampered programs for the poor and needy.

He is also planning to meet with business leaders, trade unions, workers and social representatives.

Pope Leo to return to Peru for last leg of trip

The final leg of the trip, on Wednesday, will see Leo return to Peru, where he lived and preached for two decades.

There is excitement about his visit to Peru, with the pope planning to celebrate Mass in his old diocese of Chiclayo as well as in the mountain village of Santa Cruz de Succhabamba.

The pope will also celebrate Mass in the former Incan capital city of Cusco before honoring Peru's indigenous population by traveling to Pucallpa in the Peruvian Amazon.

The excitement can be seen in the street vendors selling T-shirts and rosaries with his likeness, while bakeries have been selling Leo bread.

Peru has also seen a weakening of the faithful in recent years, with the Catholic population falling from 76% in 2013-2014 to around 67% now.

World.title: Tankers carrying Russian diesel to the US change course
World.content:
Despite an ostensible deal between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin to bring diesel to the US, tankers are reportedly unable to dock due to existing sanctions.

Several sanctioned tankers headed for the US carrying Russian diesel are said to have changed course, one toward Brazil and the other into the Mediterranean, according to data from marine data company Kpler and vessel traffic site MarineTraffic.com.

The tankers reportedly departed from the Baltic Sea port of Primorsk last month and had declared their destinations as the US east coast.

This all comes after US President Donald Trump eased sanctions on Russian oil last month, in a deal with with Russian leader Vladimir Putin to secure a large amount of diesel directly to the US at a time when diesel prices have skyrocketed across the country.

The agreement caused shock and drew criticism in Ukraine and Europe. But it also was a logistical challenge, given that sanctions against Russia still remain in place.

It was also widely reported at the time that the amount of diesel in question was a fraction of the US daily demand.

Russia says reports are 'fake'

UK newspaper The Financial Times (FT) reported Wednesday that two of the tankers appeared to have changed their destination and were no longer headed to the United States.

Russian envoy and negotiator Kirill Dmitriev said on Thursday that the US-bound diesel tankers were still on course.

"Fake. Tankers destined for the US continue on course," Dmitriev said on X, linking to the FT story.

Putin's spokesman Dmitry Peskov said detail of shipments were a "commercial" matter that could not be made public.

"All diesel will find its buyers," he added, without elaborating.

A third vessel was still in the North Atlantic headed toward the US but changed its destination from New York to a vague "for orders," without listing an unloading point.

Can Trump’s diesel deal bring down US fuel prices? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

NJ governor threatens 'harsh penalties'

Despite the fact that the US Treasury Department temporarily authorized Russian diesel transactions, New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill warned port and terminal operators to turn away ships carrying the fuel.

In a letter earlier this week, she warned that "any effort to profit from the illegal trade in Russian fuel will be met with harsh penalties.”

Sherrill accused the Trump administration of lacking authority in overriding the import ban enacted by Congress more than four years ago.

She said New Jersey would act to prevent state facilities and companies from handling Russian fuel.

In a letter dated October 27, Connecticut Senator Richard Blumenthal warned shipping companies against violating US sanctions forbidding imports of Russian fuel.

"No president can unilaterally override a statute. Trump's license will not absolve you of legal and moral accountability," the letter read.

World.title: Stephen Miller named by Trump as new White House chief of staff
World.content:
Trump said he would be replacing Susie Wiles for the top advisory role. Miller is a controversial figure, known as a key architect of the administration's hardline immigration policies.

US President Donald ‌Trump announced on ⁠Friday ⁠that his ​deputy chief of ​staff and architect of his administration's strict immigration policy, Stephen Miller, will become his new chief of staff.

Miller replaces Susie Wiles, who had been in the post since Trump's inauguration. With the nod, Miller becomes the top aide to the president.

Trump announced the move, saying Miller was "one of my most trusted advisors," adding that Wiles has done an outstanding job, and would be "moving over" to the "Trump political operation."

"He gets it" and is "very good politically. And he's a very good man. He'll do a great job, great manager," Trump said.

Wiles also commented on her exit from the White House, saying that her work there was "the honor of a lifetime."

The move comes after Trump's Republican Party lost control of the House and Senate after a midterm election rout at the hands of Democrats.

One of Trump's longest-serving aides

The 41-year-old is one of Trump's longest-serving advisers, having joined Trump's longshot 2016 presidential campaign as a speechwriter.

Although his portfolio as deputy chief of staff was wide-ranging, Miller is most responsible for Trump's policies and rhetoric on immigration.

Miller's appointment is a signal that Trump intends to continue on with his hardline immigration policies, despite voters rejecting Republicans around the country.

Miller is known for taking controversial positions, and is one of the Trump administration's most vocal advocates, frequently making media appearances to defend extreme positions.

Miller a controversial figure

On immigration, his ideas have included calling for federal agents to make 3,000 arrests every day, while allowing the agency to target migrants who have lived in the US for decades. He is widely created with helping expand the remit of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

When ICE comes knocking: the fight against Trump's deportations To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

On foreign policy, Miller has defended extrajudicial strikes on boats in Caribbean Sea allegedly used by drugs smugglers, and defended the administration's military operation to snatch Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro in January.

In January 2026, Miller went on broadcaster CNN and claimed that the US had the right the seize Greenland, after Trump said controlling the Danish territory was a strategic necessity.

"We live in the real world, Jake, that is governed by strength, that is governed by force, that is governed by power. These are the iron laws of the world since the beginning of time," Miller told CNN's host Jake Tapper.



Miller also has not held back on attacking the administration's opponents.

During the midterm campaign, Miller called Democrats "extremists, freaks and America-hating lunatics" on social media.

He also promoted claims about election fraud in California and Alaska, which were not substantiated.

As Trump has lost control of both chambers of Congress, Miller has been credited with working in the background to create an obstructionist strategy for the White House to block Democratic legislation. Trump has taken to the strategy and has said, "I guess I'll become Mr. Veto."

Democrats vow to 'fight' Miller's agenda

After Trump's announcement, New York Democratic Congressman Hakeem Jeffries, who could become the next speaker of the House, posted on social media that Miller was a "dangerous xenophobe and reckless extremist who has American blood on his hands," referring to the deaths of US citizens protesting ICE raids.

Senator Chuck Schumer issued a statement saying the Trump had "learned nothing" after the Republican's election drubbing.

"Stephen Miller is the architect of the most barbaric, inhumane policies of this administration," said Schumer, who is positioned to become the next Senate majority leader in January.

"Trump couldn't have made a worse choice. Our Democratic majorities will fight him every step of the way," he said.

World.title: Ueno Bank scandal plunges Paraguay into political crisis
World.content:
Suspected financial fraud, public money at risk and millions of customers affected: Paraguay is in serious crisis following the sudden collapse of Ueno Bank. President Santiago Pena is facing impeachment.

The Ueno Bank collapse is turning into one of the biggest financial and political scandals in the history of Paraguay. At issue are suspected banking irregularities, hundreds of millions of dollars in public funds, and business ties between the bank and the country's president, Santiago Pena.

The crisis was triggered on November 3, when the Paraguayan central bank (BCP) initiated resolution procedures against Ueno after determining that it had breached minimum solvency requirements. The public prosecutor has since announced three investigations into suspected financial crimes. 27 individuals have already been formally charged.

Pressure on President Pena intensified. On November 5, he tendered his resignation, but the Paraguayan Congress did not accept it. Instead, the Chamber of Deputies voted unanimously to impeach him. A joint session of both legislative chambers was called to consider the resignation, but the session was not quorate, so no decision could be taken. Pena remains in office for now, and the Senate has opened impeachment proceedings.

Lawmakers in the Paraguayan Congress have voted to impeach their president Image: Cesar Olmedo/REUTERS

What is Ueno Bank, and what happened?

Ueno Bank is a Paraguayan digital bank belonging to the Grupo Vazquez, a big Paraguayan conglomerate. Launched in 2021, it expanded remarkably fast: It recently had around three million customers, almost half the population of Paraguay. At the same time, there were warnings that the bank might have extended excessive loans to companies associated with its owners.

On November 3, 2026, the Paraguayan Central Bank (BCP) intervened, having determined that the bank had breached minimum solvency requirements: It no longer had sufficient capital to provide security for risks it had incurred. Business operations were abruptly suspended, leaving millions of customers unable to access their accounts.

Police officers had to guard branches of Ueno Bank against protesting customers who couldn't withdraw their money Image: Daniel Duarte/AFP

What caused the crisis?

Investigations are primarily focused on three potential problems.

First, Ueno Bank is believed to have extended credit to other companies from the same group, and these may have exceeded legal limits.

Some business dealings may also have served to conceal the lack of capital, and make the bank's financial situation appear better than it actually was.

There is also the question of why the Central Bank didn't intervene sooner, despite indications that there were problems.

How much public money is managed by Ueno Bank?

Ueno Bank held huge deposits of public money. Its most important investors include the Instituto de Prevision Social (IPS), the Paraguayan social security agency responsible for pensions and social welfare payments. According to media reports, Ueno Bank administers public funds totalling as much as 800 to 850 million US dollars.

Not only is the size of the amount problematic, so is the concentration of public funds in a single financial institution — one that has had to be placed under state control. Other state institutions are also said to have continued to deposit funds with the bank.

This raises questions about how state institutions make their investment decisions, and the risks to which they have exposed public funds.

What are the bank's connections to Santiago Pena?

There is Pena's business relationship with Grupo Vazquez, to which the Ueno Bank belongs. The Paraguayan president maintained business connections with the conglomerate until March 2025, long after his election as head of state. However, he denies having had any direct involvement with the bank.

In the Paraguayan Congress, a man holds up a sign calling for President Pena's impeachment Image: Cesar Olmedo/REUTERS

On the other hand, Pena's appointment of Carlos Carvallo as president of the Central Bank in 2023 has come under scrutiny. The decision is controversial because until then Carvallo was the chair of the finance company that became Ueno Bank, Financiero Ueno. It raises questions about possible conflict of interest, and the independence of banking supervision.

Carvallo resigned on November 3, at Pena's request.

Who else is under suspicion?

On November 4, the public prosecutor's office formally charged 27 people: eight Ueno Bank executives, and 19 others with connections to companies associated with the bank.

The investigations are looking into suspected breach of trust, attempted fraud, breach of duty in crisis situations, and violation of the legal obligation to keep records.

On November 5, a judge remanded several former bank executives in custody, including Federico Miguel Vazquez Villasanti, the president of Grupo Vazquez. Two other accused were placed under house arrest.

What will happen now?

The Central Bank has initiated winding-up proceedings against Ueno Bank. Deposits of sums up to the equivalent of 37,600 US dollars per customer are protected by law. A law has also been passed that will enable around 20,000 US dollars per saver to be paid out early. However, it is still not clear when the affected customers will actually get their money back, or what will happen to deposits greater than the legally protected maximum.

Paraguayans protest outside the Congress building in the capital, Asuncion. Around half the population is directly affected Image: Anadolu/picture alliance

The political situation is more complicated. Santiago Pena tendered his resignation, but remains in office. A joint session of the two chambers of Congress could not decide whether or not to accept his resignation as the meeting was not quorate. The Senate has now initiated impeachment proceedings on charges of serious breaches of duty. Pena has announced that he will face the proceedings and exercise his right to defend himself.

What is at stake here is political immunity. If Pena leaves office in a regular way – by resigning — he will automatically become a senator for life, and this will give him parliamentary immunity from prosecution. If he is impeached, he loses this status, and can be prosecuted.

Should Pena leave office, the constitution decrees that his vice-president, Pedro Alliana, would take over as president. Congress would then have to elect a new vice-president. The current term of office runs until August 2028.

This article has been translated from German.

World.title: Critics say Democrats should look into Trump's Middle East deals in future corruption investigations
World.content:
After their victory in the US midterm elections, the Democrats have promised to investigate corruption in the Trump administration. Critics say the president's Middle East deals is an area they should focus on.

Several polls of US voters taken around the recent midterm elections show that an overriding concern about the Trump administration is corruption.

Just days after the midterms, senior figures in the Democratic Party were quick to proclaim that they will be investigating corruption accusations when they take their seats in January.

It's highly likely that many of those investigations will center on the Trump administration's and the Trump family's links to wealthy Middle Eastern countries.

"The incoming Democratic majority in Congress will no doubt aggressively use their powers to investigate the administration's alleged wrongdoings," Amy Hawthorne, a non-resident fellow at the Washington-based think tank, the Arab Center, wrote in a commentary after the midterms. "Cases involving the Middle East will be their top targets."

Financial disclosures made by President Trump in the middle of this year showed that during 2025, his businesses made about $2 billion in income. This was triple the income he reported the previous year, observers noted.

"According to the information available … Middle Eastern countries and businesses have directly contributed to the bottom line of Trump's family businesses — more so than any other region of the world," Brian Katulis, a senior fellow and expert in US foreign policy at the Middle East Institute in Washington, wrote in a July text after the presidential disclosure. "Gulf entities paid around $300 million to the president's businesses in 2025."

Billions in cryptocurrency

A lot of the money Trump made in 2025 came from the sale of a stake in a cryptocurrency company, World Liberty Financial, Katulis noted.

The company was founded by the Trump and Witkoff families in 2024 — Steve Witkoff is Trump's special envoy to the Middle East — and in 2025, a large portion of it was sold to an investment firm backed by a senior United Arab Emirates official, Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan. The latter serves as the UAE's national security advisor and is also the brother of the UAE's president.

The deal was done in January 2026 behind closed doors, shortly before Trump's inauguration as president. In May 2026, the US agreed to allow the UAE access to advanced artificial intelligence chips, despite objections from some national security advisers.

Trump's critics allege a connection, the Trump administration denies it.

Trump cryptocurrency: A law suit filed in late October alleges a UAE investment fund chaired by Tahnoon also spent about $2 billion on a World Liberty cryptocurrency to inflate the value of the company Image: Niklas Larsson/BILDBYRÅN/picture alliance

There are also other alleged instances of Trump administration corruption with links to the Middle East.

Trump Towers in the Middle East

Various Trump deals with Saudi and Emirati real estate developers are also being questioned because of possible conflicts of interest.

The Gulf real estate developers, which have close ties to their governments and respective royal families, have agreed to build Trump-branded golf resorts, hotels, mansions, skyscrapers and towers in Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar and the Maldives.

In 2025, Trump reported $59.5 million in foreign real estate licensing income, ten times more than he made in 2023, business media outlet CNBC reported in August. Nearly two-thirds of that money came from projects in the Gulf, CNBC said.

Ethics watchdogs argue that, "the deals create conflicts between Trump's political leadership role and private interests" because some of those Gulf states and their developers were also "pursuing major US investments, seeking government permits or pressing for favorable economic and diplomatic relations."

Qatar's flying gift

When the Qatari royal family gifted Trump a luxury jet, worth around $400 million, in May 2025, politicians and ethics experts asked about the propriety of taking such a pricey present from a foreign government.

After his presidency ends, Trump was apparently planning to donate the plane to his Florida-based project, the Donald J. Trump Presidential Library Foundation. Currently, it is unclear whether the Qatari plane will end up there and there's been speculation Trump will try to keep it for personal use.

The luxury plane, described as a "flying palace," had to be retrofitted with additional security for an unspecified cost that's thought to be in the millions Image: Elizabeth Frantz/REUTERS

The library is a non-profit and has received tens of millions in funding — an investigation by the CBS network traced over $100 million in donations — from lawsuits and via corporate donors.

Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren has already said the library project would be investigated. "Giant corporations and foreign governments should not be able to buy influence in Washington with donations to the president's library," she told CBS.

Gaza's 'Board of Peace'

Plans for the so-called Board of Peace were created in September 2025 and the body was to facilitate a ceasefire and reconstruction in Gaza.

It was set up to be a kind of multilateral international organization, similar to the United Nations, except that Trump would serve as its chairman indefinitely and member countries donating $1 billion if they want to sit on the board permanently.

The Board of Peace has not achieved much in Gaza, experts say, and there have been several worrying developments.

Four months after its establishment, the World Bank account set up to manage Board of Peace funds was empty, the Financial Times newspaper reported in May . Instead, money had been deposited into a private JP Morgan bank account, over which there was no oversight.

There have apparently been contributions of around $3 million from Morocco and $20 million from the UAE, as well as pledges of $7 billion from board members and $10 billion from Trump.

The board's legal status was also changed to make it into an international non-governmental organization. This change in legal status may aim "to avoid US congressional oversight and keep much of its activity opaque," Zaha Hassan, an attorney and senior fellow at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, warned in a June commentary . It also "gives Trump ultimate decision-making authority, including over financial matters," she noted.

'Trump crime family'

"The Trump crime family is the top of our investigative priorities," the most senior Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, Robert Garcia, said after the midterms .

And he has already expressed concerns about the behavior of Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner in the Middle East.

Most of the issues around Kushner involve potential conflicts of interest. Kushner is acting as a volunteer envoy in the Middle East and has been deeply involved in negotiations to end the Gaza conflict and the Iran war.

Kushner (right) next to Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and Steve Witkoff (left): Kushner's status as a 'volunteer' envoy means he is not subject to the same scrutiny as an elected official Image: Chen Junqing/Xinhua/IMAGO

In early October, CNN published an investigation that detailed links between Kushner's private equity company, Affinity Partners, and investments into leading Israeli military manufacturers.

It's also been reported that while he was travelling in the region, Kushner was trying to raise billions for his equity firm.

In March, Democratic politicians, including Garcia, wrote letters to the president's office, saying they had "serious concerns about whether the White House is letting Mr. Kushner use his influence for personal financial gain."

The potentially most damaging claims against Kushner come from a recent book, "Prince and Thieves," published late October by American investigative journalist Matthew Cole.

Cole alleges, "Kushner worked with the UAE to shape US policy across the Middle East and that, in the course of this work, he was given access to bank accounts containing roughly $2 billion," the New York Times wrote in its review .

Kushner denies the allegations about any such slush fund held by an Israeli bank and has threatened to sue Vanity Fair magazine, which published excerpts from the book.

But, as the New York Times concluded, "Cole's work is sufficiently calm, detailed and forensic to necessitate a large-scale and urgent congressional inquiry."

World.title: Ilse Aigner tipped by party allies as next German president
World.content:
German media reports suggest that Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner's chances of becoming the next president are on the up. Long favored by her Bavarian CSU, now it seems Christian Democrats nationwide plan to back her.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democrats (the CDU) and their Bavarian sister party, the CSU, want to nominate a joint candidate to be the next president of Germany when the special "Bundesversammlung" committee that elects one votes at the end of January.

It's long been clear that the CSU favor the current speaker of Bavaria's parliament, Ilse Aigner, for the role.

But on Friday, multiple German news outlets like Spiegel, the Süddeutsche Zeitung and the DPA news agency cited sources in the CDU as saying that party's leadership had also decided on putting Aigner forward.

DPA reported that Merz would officially recommend Aigner as a candidate at a meeting of the CDU's leadership that will convene in Berlin on Sunday and Monday.

On the record, however, party officials would neither confirm nor deny the reports, pointing only to the upcoming meetings on Monday.

Aigner appears to have the backing of both Bavaria's Markus Söder and Chancellor Friedrich Merz, visible in the background on the main stage at the CSU party conference in this photo Image: Peter Kneffel/dpa/picture alliance

Germany's first woman as president?

If chosen, Aigner would be the 13th person and the first woman to take up the role as post-war Germany's head of state, which is a more ceremonial one with primarily symbolic power, while the bulk of the political and legislative power resides with the chancellor.

She would also be the first CSU politician to hold the office.

Aigner, 61, is currently the speaker of the state parliament in Bavaria.

The youngest of four sisters and the daughter of an electrician, she worked in the family business in her early adult life before going into politics. She's a Roman Catholic, single and has no children.

Aigner began her parliamentary career in the Bavarian legislature in 1994, then moved to the Bundestag federal parliament in 1998, before returning to the Bavarian chamber in 2013.

She spent five years as federal agriculture minister under then-Chancellor Angela Merkel.

She would also be the first CSU politician to hold the office.

Current President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, a heavy hitter for years for the Social Democrats before becoming head of state, is nearing the end of his second five-year term in the role, having assumed the office in March 2017.

Aigner is the speaker or president of Bavaria's state parliament at present, she's also a former federal agriculture minister Image: Rolf Poss/IMAGO

What steps remain on the path to Germany picking a new president?

The CDU/CSU's junior coalition partners, the Social Democrats (SPD), have also made it clear they would back a presidential bid from Aigner.

"If the CDU steering committee does indeed officially assert itself on Monday and put forward Ilse Aigner, then on behalf of the SPD I can only say that we would welcome this and support it," SPD chairman Lars Klingbeil said at an event in Berlin.

A large committee known as the Bundesversammlung chooses the German president. It will vote on January 30, 2027.

It's made up of all 630 Bundestag parliament members, and another 630 people assigned to represent the various German states — weighted according to each state's share of the national population.

Most of these are regional lawmakers, but municipal politicians and people from other walks of public life are also sometimes given a vote.

The CDU/CSU and SPD combined have a majority of roughly 50 seats in the special committee.

Beyond this, Merz is expected to try to rope in support for Aigner from the Greens, a party that has long championed more female representation at the top of politics and that would not seem to have a realistic chance of propelling a candidate of its own into the role.

This suggests that if Aigner's nomination were to materialize and solidify, she should have fairly good chances of succeeding Steinmeier.

World.title: Meghan Markle's father arrested in US over child sex abuse material
World.content:
US federal agents arrested Thomas Markle in Florida. The Duchess of Sussex and television actress Meghan Markle, who is estranged from her father, said she was "deeply distressed" by the charges.

Meghan Markle's father, Thomas Markle Sr., was arrested Friday morning by federal agents in Florida on charges related to child abuse, including sexually explicit photographs of himself with prepubescent girls,US federal prosecutors said .

Thomas Markle Sr. was charged with one count of possession of child sex abuse imagery, prosecutors said in a statement.

The 82-year-old was arrested outside the city of Tampa on Florida's west coast.

The director of Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Kash Patel, said that "Mr. Markle allegedly targeted innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions."

Patel said their agents "moved quickly" to identify and locate the explicit material, and then arrested Markle Sr. in Florida.

Sex abuse images discovered in storage units

First Assistant US Attorney for central California Bill Essayli said federal agents searched two storage units in the Los Angeles area and "seized approximately 78 items, including slides, film negatives, and books" that contained suspected child sexual abuse images.

"Mr. Markle is accused of possessing child sexual abuse material, including photographs depicting himself with minor girls," said Essayli in a statement. "These allegations are extremely serious, and we will prosecute Mr. Markle to the fullest extent of federal law."

If convicted, Thomas Markle Sr. would face a statutory maximum sentence of 20 years in federal prison.

Markle Sr. was first reported to the police in the Philippines and to the FBI last month by his son, Thomas Markle Jr, after he claimed to have found child sex abuse material at his father's home in the Philippines, according to reports by the UK newspaper The Sun.

Meghan Markle, the wife of Prince Harry, recently said she was "deeply distressed" by allegations that a collection of child sexual abuse images had been found at her father's home.

She revealed that a letter containing "troubling allegations" about him had been sent to London police in 2018.

The FBI said last month that it would assist Philippine authorities with the case where possible.

Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, said last month she was deeply troubled by allegations surrounding her entranged father. [FILE: 2021] Image: Photoshot/Avalon/picture alliance

Meghan's father famously didn't attend her wedding at Windsor Castle

Meghan, an American citizen who starred in the US television drama "Suits," married Harry at Windsor Castle in 2018.

Her father did not attend their wedding, prompting extensive coverage in the British media of Meghan's estrangement from her father.

Thomas Markle Sr., a retried television lighting and photography director, was living in the Philippines earlier this year when he suffered a stroke and had his left leg amputated.

That forced him to return to the US.

"I have supported, cared for him and helped him for years — but that stops now," Markle Jr. told The Sun. "I won't speak to my father ever again unless I’m called to give evidence against him."

World.title: Pedro Sánchez llama a la movilización en su retorno a la precampaña: “Si se pudo en Brasil y EE UU, en España también”
World.content:
El secretario general del PSOE y presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, durante el minuto de silencio con que se ha abierto el mitin de este viernes en el poliderpotivo Cabanyal-Canyamelar de Valencia.

El mitin de Valencia, más contenido que los anteriores y sin bailes, empieza con un minuto de silencio por las víctimas de Urda. El presidente reivindica “la ejemplaridad” por la dimisión de Puente en un acto que supera las expectativas de afluencia

El estrépito y los vitores por la entrada del presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, se han acallado de inmediato este viernes por la tarde en el pabellón de El Cabanyal de Valencia, lleno a rebosar de gente dentro y fuera, cuando se ha pedido un minuto de silencio por las 69 víctimas mortales del accidente ferroviario de Urda (Toledo) del pasado 28 de octubre. Solo se ha oído el llanto de algún bebé. El homenaje ha concluido con la interpretación de la canción Si tú no estás aquí, de la cantautora Rosana, ante 2.200 personas en el interior, y más de 2.500 en el exterior.

En el primer mitin de Sánchez tras la brutal colisión de un AVE con un Iryo no ha habido bailes ni declaraciones de amor y ni la alegría desbordante (rayana a veces con la impostura) de encuentros anteriores. Sí se ha respirado el ambiente de autoafirmación festivo, inherente a la naturaleza del mitin, pero ha sido más contenido.

Sánchez ha dedicado buena parte de su discurso al contexto internacional, sin dejar de mencionar a las víctimas del accidente, a la solidaridad mostrada por la sociedad española y a la dimisión del ministro de Transporte, Óscar Puente. “España ha sido el faro que ha demostrado que la esperanza es mas eficiente que el odio para la prosperidad, conquistas sociales y estar en el lado correcto de la historia. Ya vemos lo que ha pasado en Brasil, en Estados Unidos, si España ha resistido, el 29-N vamos a dar un paso al frente para ganar a la ultraderecha y la derecha que ha claudicado ante la ultraderecha”, ha afirmado.

En este punto ha hecho un llamamiento al voto útil: “La movilización es la fórmula, en Brasil ganó el progreso gracias a la movilización, y en EE UU, y si en Brasil y EE UU se pudo, en España también votando al PSOE. Demos una lección al mundo”. “La victoria de la derecha no es inevitable, es indeseable”, ha afirmado.

“Hemos asumido la responsabilidad política con la dimisión de un gran político como es Óscar Puente”, ha proseguido. “El PP y Vox han criticado primero que no dimitiera y cuando ha dimitido también le han criticado, porque el ejemplo de dignidad y de ejemplaridad que ha ejercido ellos jamás lo practican ante ninguna crisis, ni ninguna tragedia que ellos hayan podido gestionar al frente del Gobierno”.

“Si hay una lección que extraer de esta tragedia ferroviaria, como de todas aquellas que hemos sufrido durante estos últimos ocho años al frente del Gobierno, es que los servicios públicos importan. Hemos tardado 15 años en revertir los recortes en inversión ferroviaria que infligió Mariano Rajoy cuando era presidente del Gobierno. Los recortes y la motosierra no son la solución. Y eso también es lo que nos jugamos el próximo 29 de noviembre: o reforzar lo público o recortar lo público”, ha reiterado.

Milei y la dana

Pilar Bernabé, exdelegada del Gobierno y candidata a la alcaldía de Valencia que encabeza la lista socialista por la circunscripción, ha abierto las intervenciones y ha caldeado el ambiente al aludir a los referentes de la actual alcaldesa, María José Catalá, que mañana recibe a la presidenta madrileña, Isabel Díaz Ayuso, para dar un mitin. “Solo le falta traer a Milei”, ha ironizado, antes de levantar al público asegurando que sus referentes son “los alcaldes de las poblaciones afectadas por la dana” que provocó la muerte de 234 personas en la provincia de Valencia en 2024.

Bernabé ha incidido en el ejemplo de las víctimas de la dana y de sus principales asociaciones, que no “han sido recibidas por la presidencia de la Generalitat”. También lo ha hecho la ministra de Ciencia y secretaria general del PSPV-PSOE, Diana Morant, que ha agradecido la decisión del exministro de Transportes, Óscar Puente, de dimitir “por demostrar dignidad en los momentos en que hay que empatizar con el dolor”. El público ha coreado entonces el nombre del exministro.

Morant ha cargado contra “el Gobierno del Ventorro”, que es una categoría", en referencia al restaurante donde Carlos Mazón pasó cuatro horas la tarde de la dana. El entonces presidente de la Generalitat, Carlos Mazón, se “desentendió de la emergencia”, al igual que su Consell. “Que se vayan los que no se quieren hacerse cargo de la vida de la gente“, ha afirmado la también candidata a la Generalitat.

Con un aforo máximo de 2.200 personas por los planes de evacuación, el Polideportivo de El Cabanyal se ha quedado pequeño. La asistencia ha superado las expectativas y más de 2.500 personas se han quedado fuera en la calle, donde se han dispuesto 500 sillas frente a una gran pantalla para seguir el mitin. Por ahí ha entrado el presidente del Gobierno para apaciguar los ánimos y darse un baño de gente, que le gritaba “presidente, presidente”, “Pedro, Pedro” y “No estás solo, Valencia está contigo”. Lo mismo que cuando ha accedido al pabellón.

Pedro Sánchez a su llegada al acto en el Polideportivo Cabanyal-Canyamelar de Valencia. Mònica Torres

Muchos simpatizantes y militantes han llegado en autobuses. Como Marta y Elba, dos simpatizantes de 21 y 23 años, respectivamente, del pueblo castellonense de Onda, a las que les hacía “mucha ilusión verlo en persona”, y más ahora que la situación “está tan complicada”. Los militantes Eloísa y Paz son más veteranas en las lides mitineras. “Teníamos que venir a apoyarlo, por supuesto. y también a la que será alcaldesa de Valencia que se portó muy bien en la dana”, comenta la primera, en alusión a Pilar Bernabé, exdelegada del Gobierno, que encabeza la lista socialista por Valencia.

Barrio de voto socialista

Dos grandes carteles con el gran lema de la precampaña La fuerza de la gente, en castellano y valenciano, flaquean el escenario, sin presencia de la otra idea fuerza del amor.

El polideportivo de El Cabanyal ya ha sido empleado en otros ocasiones por los socialistas para sus mítines. En las últimas elecciones generales, los socialistas ganaron en los barrios del frente marítimo de Valencia (Cabanyal, Canyamelar, el Grao, Nazaret), con el 32,5% de los votos, por el 28% del PP. Nada que ver con el barrio de L’Eixample de la ciudad, donde mañana la presidenta madrileña, Isabel Díaz Ayuso, dará la réplica al jefe del Ejecutivo en el mercado modernista de Colón. Aquí, los populares superaron el 60%.

Pedro Sánchez, durante el mintin de este viernes en Valencia. Mònica Torres

La estrategia del PP en esta precampaña no ha variado tras la dimisión del ministro de Transportes, Óscar Puente Puente. Alberto Núñez Feijóo, y el presidente del PP de Castilla y León, Alfonso Fernández Mañueco, intervienen mañana, sábado, a partir de las doce, en un acto junto a la candidata número uno al Congreso por Valladolid, María Pardo, el presidente provincial del PP de Valladolid, Conrado Íscar, y el alcalde de la ciudad y candidato al Senado, Jesús Julio Carnero.

World.title: Saber qué hacer con el dinero: la importancia de aprender a tomar decisiones financieras
World.content:
En tiempos donde se multiplican las opciones de inversión (y los peligros de consejos dudosos en redes sociales), “una sociedad con mayor cultura financiera es más resiliente y sostenible”, como defienden desde Mapfre. Para educar al respecto, apuestan por campañas en todos los canales y formatos novedosos

La gestión del dinero es una preocupación cotidiana. Ahorrar para comprar una casa, preparar la jubilación, hacer frente al coste de los estudios de los hijos o asegurar que el patrimonio no se devalúe son objetivos por los que uno puede hacer mucho más que guardar dinero en su cuenta corriente. Pero, eso sí, con la asesoría apropiada “para planificar bien el futuro y tomar decisiones más responsables”, como explica Mónica Zuleta, Directora Corporativa de Sostenibilidad de Mapfre.

Cuanto más complejo sea un asunto, más urgente resulta encontrar palabras claras y sencillas para explicarlo. Nuevos lenguajes y formatos que lleguen a todo el mundo. Porque si bien hace tiempo invertir fue una actividad reservada a una minoría con grandes patrimonios y conocimientos específicos, hoy el abanico es amplísimo, con opciones aptas para cada bolsillo.

“Hace décadas las opciones eran limitadas y estaban reservadas a perfiles concretos; ahora existe una enorme oferta de productos, información y plataformas. Se ofrecen más oportunidades, pero se genera más confusión”, explica Zuleta, que recalca que “la mejor manera de navegar en ese entorno no es tratar de convertirse en expertos de la noche a la mañana”, ni mucho menos fiarse de la guía de gurús hallados en mentideros de las redes sociales.

“Entender los conceptos básicos y conocer el nivel de riesgo que cada cual está dispuesto a asumir sigue siendo la mejor brújula para tomar buenas decisiones”, afirma Zuleta, que resume algunas de las muchas iniciativas que Mapfre lleva años poniendo en marcha para divulgar sobre estos aspectos y proporcionar formación apropiada: “Hemos promovido herramientas pioneras como Empatía, un asistente de Inteligencia Artificial que permite resolver dudas a través de WhatsApp y que ha logrado solventar en tiempo real el 100% de las consultas que hacen los clientes”.

Juego de mesa de educación financiera de Fundación Mapfre.

Fundacion Mapfre desarrolla juegos de mesa diseñados ad hoc para la impartición de talleres, como Play Pension, escape rooms [juegos de escape] de temática financiera, como Finexit. Mapfre impulsa otro tipo iniciativas como aplicaciones de internet, vídeos formativos adaptados al tipo de comunicación imperante en canales como Instagram o TikTok o incluso una serie de cuatro capítulos, titulada Vecinos a todo riesgo. Ningún formato posible se les escapa

Marta Pachón, del equipo de comunicación financiera de la compañía y una de las impulsoras de esta estrategia de nuevos lenguajes cercanos de Mapfre, explica la premisa de esta serie divulgativa: “Sofía, de 32 años, acaba de firmar la hipoteca de su primera vivienda y se pregunta cómo volver a ahorrar tras ese enorme desembolso inicial. Carlos, de 47, tiene tres hijos adolescentes y necesita planificar los gastos en que incurrirá al enviar a estudiar fuera a una de sus hijas. Rosa, por su parte, tras un triste suceso, debe decidir qué hacer con una herencia… A partir de estos escenarios comunes se plantean cuestiones que nos incumben a todos: cómo se elige un seguro y qué coberturas debe tener, cómo se decide qué producto de inversión te conviene…”.

La gamificación, como describe Pachón al hecho de implicar al lector o espectador —en los vídeos tendrá que responder a preguntas que irán surgiendo durante el episodio— es una de las claves del éxito de esta propuesta. El mejor simulacro de cómo aprender tomando decisiones.

Ya a comienzos de los años setenta del pasado siglo, la Fundación Mapfre fue la impulsora del Diccionario de Seguros, un lexicón hoy consultable en línea (como el de la RAE) con un propósito claro y todavía vigente: traducir el vocabulario técnico a términos comprensibles para ayudar a los ciudadanos a entender todos esos conceptos abstrusos relacionados con las aseguradoras, la protección del patrimonio, el ahorro o la gestión de riesgos.

Se trata de un aspecto que, insiste Zuleta, lleva en el ADN de la compañía aseguradora más de medio siglo. “La educación financiera y la cultura aseguradora solo es útil si las personas la entienden y pueden aplicarla en su vida cotidiana. Por eso nos esforzamos por utilizar formatos cada vez más cercanos, prácticos y adaptados a los hábitos de aprendizaje actuales”.

Un universo nuevo de posibilidades (y de ruido)

Si bien la Bolsa española nace en 1831, en su primer siglo de vida aquel parqué está reservado casi en exclusiva a grandes fortunas, terratenientes, bancos o corporaciones. El primer gran hito popular de la inversión en España fue el que, a finales de los sesenta, en pleno desarrollismo económico, protagonizaron las Matildes, sobrenombre que recibieron por causa de la celebérrima campaña publicitaria del actor José Luis López Vázquez las acciones de Telefónica.

La era de internet y las redes sociales ha traído consigo otro cambio de profundo calado: se ha democratizado el acceso a las múltiples formas y vehículos de inversión, pero también se ha expandido la difusión de mensajes que, en opinión de Zuleta, son “simplistas o poco rigurosos o contrastados”. El discernimiento, la capacidad de pensamiento crítico, es más importante que nunca. “Nuestro papel nunca va a ser decir a las personas qué hacer con su dinero, sino dotarles del conocimiento y las herramientas para decidir con criterio y confianza”.

La brújula primordial debe ser siempre el objetivo que uno se marca: ¿para qué necesita ahorrar? “No es lo mismo”, cuenta Pachón, “intentar juntar dinero para celebrar una boda en el plazo de un año que ahorrar con la vista puesta en tu jubilación, dentro de 20 o 30 años”. Y, por lo tanto, no se puede asumir el mismo riesgo cuando se trata de un dinero que sí o sí vas a necesitar en pocos meses que cuando puedes mantener la inversión ahí, trabajando durante décadas (los horizontes temporales más largos permiten estrategias menos susceptibles a las oscilaciones de mercado).

Ahorrar no depende de grandes sumas: reservar una cantidad pequeña de forma constante puede marcar una gran diferencia con el tiempo Mónica Zuleta, directora Corporativa de Sostenibilidad de Mapfre

En ese camino, el acompañamiento de un profesional puede suponer el salto entre fracasar y cumplir el objetivo. Mapfre cuenta con una unidad específica, Mapfre Gestión Patrimonial, dedicada a la planificación financiera y al ejercicio de ese asesoramiento personalizado, un servicio que, como los tiempos, también se adapta hoy a cualquier tipo de cliente. Su propuesta parte del análisis de la situación para ayudarle a definir qué metas son plausibles y en qué plazos para, una vez definido eso, construir una estrategia. No se trata solo de recomendar un producto financiero u otro, sino de poner en orden las finanzas para establecer la mejor ruta posible en cada etapa de la vida. Como le ocurre a los protagonistas de Vecinos a todo riesgo.

Porque el ahorro es, sobre todo, un hábito que se aprende con dedicación y constancia, tal como aseguran desde Mapfre. Incluso cantidades pequeñas, si se reservan de manera sistemática, pueden tener un efecto significativo. Cambiarnos en algo la vida. Es un saber útil, imprescindible en una sociedad como la de hoy, y qué mejor que aprenderlo de la mano de quien lo enseña con llaneza, sin esconderse detrás de palabros incomprensibles.

World.title: Una red que garantiza buena salud
World.content:
La conectividad ya es una parte esencial de la atención sanitaria. Vodafone Empresas ayuda a organizaciones como ASISA a mantener operativos sus servicios, incluso cuando las circunstancias ponen a prueba toda la infraestructura

Una consulta médica ya no depende solo de la conversación entre paciente y profesional. Detrás de cada diagnóstico hay historias clínicas digitales, pruebas almacenadas en la nube y sistemas que conectan hospitales y especialistas en tiempo real. La sanidad se ha digitalizado a gran velocidad, apoyándose en una infraestructura tan esencial como invisible: las redes de comunicaciones.

Su importancia se hace evidente cuando algo falla. Una interrupción no significa solo quedarse sin internet. Puede impedir el acceso a pruebas diagnósticas, dificultar la coordinación entre equipos médicos, obligar a cancelar operaciones o desviar ambulancias. La actividad continúa, pero la operativa se vuelve más compleja.

Evitar que la conectividad se convierta en un punto vulnerable es una de las prioridades del sector.
