Vodafone Empresas combina redes fijas y móviles, gestión de infraestructuras, herramientas para garantizar la disponibilidad de aplicaciones críticas y soluciones de ciberseguridad. La experiencia de ASISA, uno de los grandes grupos aseguradores y sanitarios de España, muestra la importancia de contar con una infraestructura capaz de mantener la actividad diaria.

La infraestructura invisible de las redes

La transformación digital de la sanidad no consiste solo en incorporar nuevos equipos o desarrollar aplicaciones más avanzadas. También requiere redes capaces de mover grandes volúmenes de información de forma segura, ágil y sin interrupciones.

Para dar respuesta a estas necesidades, Vodafone Empresas combina conectividad fija y móvil, soluciones IoT, redes privadas, capacidades de edge computing y servicios en la nube. Un ecosistema tecnológico diseñado para entornos complejos, donde conviven múltiples sedes, miles de dispositivos conectados y una exigencia constante de disponibilidad.

José Antonio Martínez, Director de Cuentas Estratégicas de Vodafone Empresas, apunta tres tecnologías que están acelerando esta transformación. La primera es el 5G, que, precisa, “ha ampliado las capacidades de conexión, el ancho de banda y la disponibilidad de las comunicaciones”, facilitando el acceso en tiempo real a imágenes médicas de gran tamaño, como las resonancias magnéticas, que antes se entregaban en soportes físicos.

El 5G ha ampliado las capacidades de conexión, el ancho de banda y la disponibilidad de las comunicaciones José Antonio Martínez, Director de Cuentas Estratégicas de Vodafone Empresas

A ello se suman la inteligencia artificial (IA), que empieza a impulsar la modernización de procesos y servicios en las organizaciones sanitarias, y la nube, “que permite centralizar sistemas, almacenar imágenes médicas y garantizar que los profesionales autorizados puedan acceder a la información de forma rápida y segura desde distintos centros”.

Arquitectura de una sanidad digital

Con más de 3,5 millones de asegurados y una red de hospitales, clínicas, centros médicos y oficinas repartidos por toda España, ASISA depende de unas comunicaciones que deben funcionar de forma ininterrumpida. La gestión de citas, el acceso a las historias clínicas, la coordinación entre centros o la atención al asegurado descansan sobre una misma infraestructura digital.

Para modernizarla, Vodafone ha desplegado una red corporativa inteligente SD-WAN, ha renovado las redes locales de comunicación y ha reforzado la infraestructura WiFi de la compañía. El objetivo es dotar a la organización de una arquitectura más robusta, capaz de responder a las exigencias de una actividad asistencial cada vez más digitalizada.

“Buscábamos entrar en el siglo XXI como merecía nuestra actividad y aprovechar todas las posibilidades que ofrecían los avances tecnológicos”, aclara José Pereira, director de Medios de ASISA. La rapidez de las comunicaciones, añade, es determinante para la toma de decisiones: “Si las señales no llegan o no lo hacen con agilidad, las decisiones no se toman a tiempo, se toman mal o ni siquiera se dispone de la información necesaria para tomarlas”.

José Antonio Martínez, Director de Cuentas Estratégicas de Vodafone Empresas. Cedida por Vodafone

Las consecuencias pueden traducirse en retrasos en consultas y pruebas, dificultades para acceder a información clínica crítica, problemas de coordinación entre equipos y mayores riesgos para la seguridad de los datos. Pero una conectividad adecuada no solo reduce estos riesgos. También amplía las posibilidades de atención. “Cuanto mejor sea esa conexión y mayor la información que podamos intercambiar, más posibilidades se abren. En última instancia, hablamos de la salud y la vida de las personas”.

El día que la conectividad se puso a prueba

El apagón eléctrico de 2025 evidenció hasta qué punto las infraestructuras esenciales están interconectadas. “Existe una estrecha relación entre el sistema eléctrico, las telecomunicaciones y el sistema asistencial”, puntualiza Martínez. Por aquel entonces, ASISA ya contaba con la infraestructura de Vodafone. “Mantener la conectividad fue un alivio y nos permitió seguir operando en un momento especialmente complejo”, recuerda Pereira.

La incidencia puso a prueba la resiliencia de las redes. Vodafone logró mantener operativa su red móvil durante más tiempo gracias a una combinación de planificación previa, capacidad de respaldo y protocolos de emergencia. Según explica Martínez, la compañía tenía más autonomía en sus estaciones base y priorizó los servicios esenciales para prolongar la conectividad. Entre ellos se encontraban clientes estratégicos y organizaciones de misión crítica, como ASISA.

La experiencia también reforzó una idea compartida por ambas compañías: en situaciones de crisis, la tecnología es tan importante como la coordinación. “Existe una relación de colaboración”, afirma Pereira. Martínez coincide: “La confianza nos permite compartir los retos y la innovación nos ayuda a encontrar nuevas formas de afrontarlos”.

Innovar sin bajar la guardia

La IA abre nuevas posibilidades para la sanidad, desde el apoyo al análisis clínico hasta la personalización de la atención al paciente. Sin embargo, su adopción también plantea importantes desafíos. Entre ellos, la protección de los datos, la fiabilidad de las respuestas y el coste asociado a un uso intensivo de esta tecnología.

Mantener la conectividad [en el apagón eléctrico de 2025] fue un alivio y nos permitió seguir operando en un momento especialmente complejo José Pereira, Director de Medios de ASISA

También resulta clave definir en qué ámbitos puede aportar más valor. Como recuerda Pereira, “la IA puede ampliar la información disponible para el médico, pero las decisiones clínicas deben seguir apoyándose en su criterio profesional y en las circunstancias personales, sociales y médicas de cada paciente”.

Martínez coincide en que el coste puede convertirse en uno de los principales frenos a su implantación. Por ello, Vodafone apuesta por lo que denomina IA soberana: modelos que se ejecutan en la propia infraestructura de las organizaciones, reduciendo la dependencia de servicios externos y permitiendo una gestión más previsible de los recursos.

La otra gran preocupación es la ciberseguridad. A medida que la IA amplía sus capacidades, también lo hacen las herramientas de las que disponen los ciberdelincuentes para intentar acceder a sistemas sanitarios, robar información sensible o secuestrar datos. “No tenemos otra alternativa: los ataques pueden producirse en cuestión de segundos y alcanzar un volumen que dificulta la respuesta humana por sí sola”, señala Martínez. En este escenario, tanto los operadores tecnológicos como las propias organizaciones sanitarias tendrán que reforzar sus capacidades de prevención, detección y respuesta para proteger una infraestructura cada vez más crítica.

World.title: Cabinet sets out AI plan, seeks partners beyond US and China
World.content:
The cabinet is establishing a vision of how to integrate AI into Dutch society so as to take advantage of its benefits, control reliance on foreign powers and strengthen national security.

Digital economy minister Willemijn Aerdts released 28-page vision letter to parliament on Friday, acknowledging that AI will “largely determine our future”.

“We want a Netherlands where AI makes everyone better and helps us move forward. Where a nurse has more time for patients, entrepreneurs can grow, and technology helps us with the major challenges of our time,” she said.

“That requires choices. Where do we want to lead the way and where do we draw the line? We don’t have to be able to do everything ourselves, but we do want to decide for ourselves which direction we take.”

The vision names Canada, Japan, Singapore and South Korea as “middle powers” the Netherlands wants to work with, alongside other EU member states.

It also says the Netherlands will keep working on “stable and predictable relations” with the US and China. The letter notes that the Netherlands has joined Pax Silica, a US-led partnership on chips, computing power and AI infrastructure.

The only funding figure in the vision is €120 million for Dutch participation in an EU-wide AI project, which was already set aside in September. The letter says more “targeted and structural investment” is needed in infrastructure, talent and research, but gives no amounts.

“This is a toothless tiger,” Volt leader Laurens Dassen told broadcaster NOS. “AI should be a top priority. It isn’t if there is no budget.”

Plans for computing power and datacentres, which use large amounts of electricity and water, will follow in the first quarter of 2027.

The cabinet is also exploring whether to set up a Dutch AI safety institute modelled on the UK’s AI Security Institute. An advisory report is due in December.

Aerdts and the education minister plan to agree a “media pact” with public and private media organisations, which will also cover how AI systems use journalistic content. No details on that have been given yet.

World.title: Activists occupy site of Microsoft data centre in Amsterdam
World.content:
Police are clearing a building site in Westpoort after pro-Palestinian activists occupied it this morning in protest to the city’s plans to build a massive data centre there, which will be leased to Microsoft.

Microsoft has acknowledged selling cloud and computing software to the Israeli military. The action was originally organised by the climate and justice group Geef Tegengas and joined by Extinction Rebellion and other groups. Other groups turned up and some stormed the site, and hung up Palestinian flags.

There was a confrontation between the police and activists this morning, according to broadcaster NOS, although the demonstration was allowed to continue after police surrounded them.

Some activists climbed onto cranes and the roof of the construction.

The €1 billion, 78MW campus is being built by Pure DC and is let in full to Microsoft. Critics say it gets round the 2022 national ban on hyperscale data centres because on paper it is three smaller data centres. According to NRC, it will use as much electricity in a year as the whole of Amsterdam.

Microsoft told NOS that it is aware of the demonstration. “We understand that this project stirs up strong emotions and respect people’s right to express their opinions peacefully. However, we do not condone actions that violate the law or endanger people’s safety.”

World.title: Cancelled Jewish exhibition back on table after mayor steps in
World.content:
Amersfoort Mayor Lucas Bolsius has said he wants a cancelled Jewish exhibition at the Amsersfoort Museum to go ahead, and the museum has now agreed to look at how it can be staged. The museum announced earlier this week that it was cancelling the exhibition due to the situation in the Middle East and rising global tensions.

The exhibition, “300 Years Amersfoort Shul”, has been years in the making, and its last-minute cancellation has caused outrage in the Jewish community.

“Apparently, many struggle to distinguish between Jewish identity and Israel. The reflex to cancel performances in situations like this is becoming increasingly common across the cultural sector,” Alexander van Dijkhuizen, chairman of the Jewish Community of Amersfoort, is reported as saying in US Jewish newspaper The Algemeiner.

“It is essential not only to reflect on the past, but also to acknowledge the difficult circumstances facing the Jewish community today.”

Hard to manage

When museum director Paul Baltus cancelled the exhibition, he said possible reactions to it were hard to manage.

“As a small and vulnerable organisation, I do not want to expose my staff to that kind of pressure,” he told the AD. “While security guards can be hired and cameras installed, the reality is that our volunteers would still have to deal with a range of possible reactions.”

But the mayor said he wasn’t informed about that decision, and he met with the museum and Amersfoort’s Jewish community on Thursday to discuss how the exhibition can go ahead.

“I am enormously saddened,” the mayor told the city council on Wednesday. “Jewish history and present-day life belong to our city. That must get the attention it deserves.” He said it was painful that the community was being made to feel it is not permitted to exist.

After Thursday’s meeting, the city said in a statement that the city, the museum and the Jewish community would look together at how 300 years of Jewish life in Amersfoort could be shown in an exhibition. “It was a good and intensive conversation,” Bolsius said. “We jointly concluded that we consider it important that there is an exhibition telling the story of 300 years of Jewish culture in Amersfoort.”

The Amersfoort Synagogue dates back to 1727 and is the oldest functioning Ashkenazi synagogue in Western Europe. The Jewish community has planned a wide-ranging programme of concerts and performances to mark the synagogue’s 300th anniversary.

Earlier this week, a Jewish student association lecture at Maastricht University was cancelled less than an hour before it was due to start, with the university saying it couldn’t guarantee participants’ safety.

World.title: Skaters get three hours on natural ice as first frost arrives
World.content:
The first frost has appeared after temperatures dropped below freezing overnight in parts of the Netherlands, in Brabant, Limburg and parts of Zeeland, according to the national weather service KNMI.

It also allowed the season’s first natural ice skating in Gelderland for a couple of hours in early morning.

The lowest temperature was recorded in Woensdrecht in Brabant, at minus 1.2°. Ell in Limburg reached minus 1.1° and Westdorpe in Zeeland minus 0.4°.

It does not yet count as an official frost day though. For that, the temperature at the KNMI’s base in De Bilt, near Utrecht, has to fall below zero. Overnight it stayed at 0.8° there.

In Winterswijk, in Gelderland, the local skating club opened the country’s first natural ice rink of the season, even though there was only ground frost there. The club uses special techniques to make ice quickly.

“When you tell people that, they say ‘it can’t be done’. But it can,” chairman Auke Spijkstra told broadcaster NOS. “It’s wonderful to see all those enthusiastic people.” About 20 skaters took to the ice. The sun soon melted it, and the rink closed again at around 10am.

World.title: Verwey-Jonker Institute facing bankruptcy amid AI rise
World.content:
The Verwey-Jonker Institute, an independent research institute in Utrecht, appears to be on the brink of bankruptcy, citing budget cuts and the rise of AI as the culprits. The Institute has applied to court for a suspension of payments.

Moving to a less expensive location and downsizing its board hasn’t been enough to save the beleaguered Institute. Broadcaster NOS also reported there’s been unrest within the agency’s leadership.

The Verwey-Jonker Institute, founded in 1993, addresses societal issues, providing research to governments, municipalities and others with “social value and impact”, according to its website. They work on issues such as poverty, youth, education, discrimination and domestic violence, among others.

The Institute says technological developments mean many of their clients are now using AI instead of engaging researchers.

While they say they want to continue their work, it will now be up to an administrator to see just how they can do that.

World.title: Graffiti group posts video of attack on Amsterdam metro
World.content:
A group of some 20 masked and hooded graffiti writers stopped a metro in Amsterdam Nieuw-West and sprayed the entire train with paint within minutes, leaving passengers inside stranded.

The action took place at the Henk Sneevlietweg stop last Saturday on Halloween. A video uploaded Tuesday on YouTube by the anonymous graffiti writers’ group Locos Worldwide, titled “Amsterdam Nightmare”, shows the sprayers entering the station and speed-spraying the train in orange, purple and black before running away cheering.

They also threw a bicycle onto the tracks and spray painted the driver’s window, leaving the train unable to move.

Shaken and shocked

“Our driver is quite shocked by the incident,” a spokesman for Amsterdam transport company GVB said. “We can also imagine that this was a frightening situation for travellers.”

The GVB, which called the incident a “serious form of vandalism”, has filed a police report. It’s still not known who is responsible for the action, but the GVB says it plans to seek compensation from the “perpetrators” when they are identified.

They tagged the train with apparent acronyms ‘NSPSKU’ and ‘LCSNTC’. NSPS has been tagged on transit vehicles in the past.

Police say they are taking the incident “seriously” and have appealed to the public to come forward with any video images they may have.

The GVB says that while graffiti does happen, the scale of the Halloween night action is extraordinary. Not only was the driver severely shaken, but the ordeal was a “potentially terrifying situation for passengers as well”.

And, according to the GVB, it put them at risk. “There was not only a subway smeared, but also a bicycle thrown on the track. That entails major security risks,” a spokesman said.

Five years ago, Locos Worldwide uploaded another video showing a masked group spray painting an in-service Amsterdam metro. The group also posts similar actions that have taken place across Europe, including in Paris, Madrid and Copenhagen.

World.title: Five of seven Dutch reptile species in decline, CBS says
World.content:
Five of the seven reptile species found in the Netherlands have declined over the past 12 years, according to new figures from national statistics office CBS and research foundation RAVON.

Only the wall lizard has grown in number since 2014, while the slow worm has stayed stable. On average, reptile populations have fallen since 2014 and are now roughly back at their 1994 level.

The viviparous, the common lizard, has fared worst, with numbers down almost 75% since 1994. The smooth snake has fallen by more than 60% since 1997, and the adder and grass snake are also in decline.

CBS said climate change may be hitting species that prefer cooler, wetter conditions, such as the common lizard and the adder. Overgrown habitats and fewer insects to eat are also likely factors.

Wall lizard numbers, by contrast, have risen more than five-fold since 1995, helped by the warmer climate.

World.title: 2,000-year-old Vandal artefacts anonymously handed to Polish museum
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A collection of artefacts associated with the Vandals and dating back almost 2,000 years has been handed anonymously to a museum in eastern Poland. The collection includes a sword, spear and javelin heads, shield components and spurs. Museum staff do not know who originally discovered the burial or exactly where it was located, leaving the circumstances of the find largely a mystery. The Father Stanisław Staszic Museum in Hrubieszów announced in a Facebook post that the objects had been passed to them anonymously through an intermediary. The items are in poor condition and will undergo urgent conservation, with the iron components of the weapons particularly vulnerable after centuries in the ground. They were also exposed to high temperatures during a burial practice in which the deceased was burned along with their personal belongings. The museum says that the nature of the objects indicates that their owner held a high social position. The most notable object is a sword preserved in three pieces, reflecting the Vandal practice of deliberately breaking or bending weapons and other grave artefacts as part of funeral rituals. The collection also contains two spearheads, both broken. Other items include a shield boss with a spike, a shield grip, a fragment of a knife, a belt buckle and two spurs. Fragments of a bone comb and a bronze fibula, used to fasten a cloak, were also recovered. The circumstances surrounding the discovery and recovery of the objects remain unknown, but the museum says that, according to the information it has received, the burial site was discovered in an agricultural field several years ago in the municipality of Werbkowice. “We intend to verify the exact location through archaeological excavations, most likely next summer,” they added. “Based on the information we have gathered, there are strong indications that there may be more similar burials in the area that have been disturbed by agricultural work.” The opportunity to recover the objects and transfer them to an appropriate institution arose only recently. The museum said that a local metal detectorist played a key role in arranging the transfer, acting as an intermediary in securing the artefacts. The recovery of the artefacts follows another recent archaeological discovery in the same region. In August, the museum announced that a metal boss from a warrior’s shield dating to the second century was found at a scrap metal yard near Hrubieszów. The Vandals were an ancient Germanic people believed to have reached the territories of present-day Poland around the 3rd or 2nd century BC. They lived in the region for several centuries and are generally associated by researchers with the Przeworsk culture, which flourished across parts of present-day Poland during the Iron Age and Roman period. Around the turn of the 4th and 5th centuries AD, amid the expansion of the Huns, they left Central Europe and moved westwards into the declining Roman Empire. As the Vandals left Central Europe, the Slavic population gradually moved into the region over the following centuries. ​ Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Polish deputy PM proposes “constitutional reset” to resolve crisis around top court
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The leader of one of the parties in Poland’s ruling coalition has put forward plans for a “constitutional reset” that he hopes can resolve the crisis around the country’s top court. The proposal, presented on Thursday by deputy prime minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, head of the centre-right Polish People’s Party (PSL), would remove all current judges on the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) and allow new judges to be chosen only with the approval of 60% of members of parliament and the president. To take effect, the measure would require amending Poland’s constitution, something that has happened only twice since the document was adopted in 1997 and which also requires a three-fifths majority in the Sejm, the lower house of parliament. Deeskalacja sytuacji wokół Trybunału Konstytucyjnego jest konieczna aby przywrócić obywatelom niezależny sąd konstytucyjny. Apelują o to przedstawiciele organizacji społecznych, Rada Przedsiębiorców, Naczelna Rada Adwokacka, Helsińska Fundacja Praw Człowieka i Episkopat Polski.… pic.twitter.com/3RCsKRlSiM — Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz (@KosiniakKamysz) November 5, 2026 Kosiniak-Kamysz’s announcement comes amid the fallout from events last Friday, when eight new judges elected to the TK this year by the government’s majority in parliament seized control of the court. They announced that its chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, had been suspended for failing to fulfil his duties, including by refusing to allow most of those judges to take up their seats on the court. Święczkowski denounced the takeover as an illegal “coup d’état”. He has been backed by the tribunal’s remaining six judges, who, like him, were appointed under the former Law and Justice (PiS) government, which brought the TK under its political influence when it ruled from 2015 to 2023. As well as pitting judges aligned with the national-conservative PiS, which is now the main opposition party, and the current more liberal government against one another, the dispute also centres around the legitimacy of certain judges. The government points to the fact that PiS unlawfully appointed three judges to the TK in 2015. As a result, both Polish and European courts have found the tribunal in its current form to be illegitimate. Meanwhile, Poland’s president, Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with PiS, has refused to swear in five of the eight judges appointed by the government’s parliamentary majority this year, citing concerns over how they were chosen or their qualifications. The International Commission of Jurists has criticised the takeover of Poland’s constitutional court, saying it “contravenes international standards on the independence of the judiciary” But it also criticised the president for refusing to swear in judges https://t.co/2kBv3GT20d — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 4, 2026 The standoff has led some NGOs and experts to call for a “constitutional reset”, whereby the TK would be reformed to make the process of selecting judges more consensual and less politicised. Indeed, the current government even proposed legislation in 2024 that would have required new TK judges to be approved by a three-fifths parliamentary majority. The plans would also have removed unlawfully appointed judges from the PiS era and annulled rulings they were involved in. That prompted the president at the time, Andrzej Duda, who was also aligned with PiS, to send the bills to the TK, which was still packed with PiS-era judges, for assessment. The tribunal rejected them as unconstitutional the following year. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 Now, Kosiniak-Kamysz has proposed new legislation intended to resolve the issue. His solution would create a mechanism under which parliament, at the request of the National Council of the Judiciary (KRS), could declare the TK “permanently incapable of performing its duties”. Such a status could only be declared with the support of a three-fifths majority of both houses of parliament – the Sejm and the Senate – combined. It would have to come at the request of the KRS because, says Kosiniak-Kamysz, the terms of judges cannot be shortened without the participation of other judges. The process of appointing new TK judges would involve the speaker of the Sejm proposing candidates after obtaining the opinions of the heads of the Supreme Court and the Supreme Administrative Court – which are separate from the TK – as well as professional bodies representing legal professions. The candidates proposed by the speaker would also have to receive the prior consent of the president. For a new TK judge to be approved, they would have to receive the support of three fifths of members of the Sejm and Senate combined. 💬 336 głosów posłów i senatorów. To wykracza poza większość jakąkolwiek koalicyjną dzisiaj sformułowaną – @KosiniakKamysz w Warszawie pic.twitter.com/iLUuM5TSxQ — 🍀 PSL (@nowePSL) November 5, 2026 Whereas TK judges currently all serve nine-year terms, under Kosiniak-Kamysz’s proposal, five of the judges would serve three-year terms, five of them six-year terms, and the final five would serve for nine years. Unlike now, the new judges would not have to swear their oath before the president, but before parliament. Kosiniak-Kamysz emphasised, however, that the measure was intended as a “one-time” emergency tool. “Later, we will return to the method of selecting judges described today in the constitution, or a better one, if there is a majority for it.” The current method of choosing new TK judges requires only the support of a majority in the Sejm. However, judges must then swear an oath “before the president”, an issue that has become a bone of contention this year. The standoff between the government and president over Poland’s constitutional court deepened today, as Maciej Berek, whom the prime minister recently described as his “right-hand man”, took his oath as a new judge without the presence of the president https://t.co/MrExiJRsEN — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 14, 2026 Kosiniak-Kamysz’s plans would require changes to Poland’s constitution, which specifies the manner in which TK judges are chosen. A constitutional amendment requires the support of a three-fifths majority in the Sejm and a simple majority in the Senate. It does not need presidential approval. PSL itself has only 28 members of the 460-seat Sejm and four senators. Kosiniak-Kamysz acknowledged that “it won’t be an easy road” to win the necessary support for his idea. He appealed not only to his fellow ruling parties, but also to opposition groups that have expressed their backing for a constitutional reset, such as the centre-right Development Plus (Rozwój Plus) and far-right Confederation (Konfederacja). On Thursday evening, one of Confederation’s leaders, Sławomir Mentzen, shared a photo of himself meeting Kosiniak-Kamysz, with the caption: “It’s going in the right direction”. However, some voices within the ruling coalition expressed scepticism towards the idea. Borys Budka, a former leader of the centrist Civic Coalition (KO) – which is the largest governing party – said it was “hard to imagine changing the constitution alongside someone like PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński”. Tomasz Trela of The Left (Lewica) likewise said that, “if anyone thinks The Left will change the constitution arm in arm with PiS, they’re mistaken”, reports Polsat News. World.title: Chinese fashion platform Shein to invest €500 million in Polish logistics hub

Chinese fast fashion platform Shein has announced a €500 million (2.2 billion zloty) investment to expand its logistics centre in Poland, a move it says will create around 2,000 new jobs by the end of this year. The announcement comes amid growing controversy over the impact of Chinese e-commerce platforms on European businesses and follows a recent decision by the European Union to introduce a special fee on low-value parcels sent from outside the EU and European Free Trade Area. SHEIN investește 500 mil. euro în Polonia. Extinde hub-ul logistic europeanhttps://t.co/WNbib4dFta pic.twitter.com/KiI1AB4wFM — Cristi Dorombach (@piticu21) November 4, 2026 The investment will expand Shein’s existing logistics facility in Magnice, near the city of Wrocław in southwestern Poland, which has been operating since 2022. The expansion will bring total employment at the site to around 10,000 by creating 2,000 jobs in logistics, supply chain management, technology and warehouse operations, according to local news service Wroclaw.pl. The facility will also host 6,500 autonomous robots for sorting items. Shein says that the move will help it cut delivery times in Europe, allowing some orders to arrive within 48 hours. “This investment in Poland clearly demonstrates our commitment and belief in the potential of the European market,” said Leonard Lin, the firm’s global head of public affairs. “Poland has become one of the pillars of our operations in Europe,” he added. “This latest investment is a testament to our confidence in the country’s potential, the competencies of its workforce, and its business environment.” The expansion comes as Shein faces a tougher trading environment in Europe. Its sales in the region fell by 13.9% year-on-year to $3.77 billion in the second quarter, while net profit dropped by 67%. The decline comes as the EU steps up efforts to curb the influx of low-cost imports from Chinese platforms such as Shein, Temu and AliExpress, which European retailers say pose unfair competition. In July, the bloc introduced a €3 fee on parcels worth less than €150. From 1 November, a further €2 handling fee was added to all imported parcels, regardless of their value, to cover customs processing costs. China overtook Germany to become Poland’s biggest source of imports for the first time in July, ending a period of around 35 years in which Germany had consistently held top spot https://t.co/U6rQwfEJ7I — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 16, 2026 Shein has also faced accusations of labour-law violations at its facilities in China, including concerns that it may use cotton produced through forced labour. The company disputes many of the allegations, saying that it prohibits forced and child labour and regularly inspects working conditions at its suppliers. China is an increasingly important trading partner in Poland. In July, it overtook Germany to become Poland’s largest source of imports for the first time, driven by rising purchases of cars, computer hardware and consumer goods. Poland has detained and charged six people – five Poles and one Russian – suspected of running an operation to illegally supply Russia with military components. Investigators say that over 2 million zloty (€450,000) worth of equipment was smuggled into the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. The arrests, which took place on 21 October and 2 November, were announced on Thursday morning by Poland’s Internal Security Agency (ABW) and National Prosecutor’s Office. 🚨 ROSYJSKI WYWIAD. PRZEMYT CZĘŚCI DO PRODUKCJI UZBROJENIA. 6 ZATRZYMANYCH.@ABW_GOV_PL rozbiła grupę podejrzaną o działalność na rzecz rosyjskich służb specjalnych. 🔴6⃣ osób zatrzymanych, 🔴2⃣1⃣przeszukanych lokalizacji, 🔴 4⃣osoby z zarzutami szpiegostwa – wszystkie trafiły… pic.twitter.com/L90n3rf5rY — ABW (@ABW_GOV_PL) November 5, 2026 Prosecutors report that all six suspects have been charged with participating in an organised criminal group that sought to export weapon components from Poland to Russia in violation of a ban on such trade. Four of the suspects have also been charged under Poland’s espionage law, accused of acting on behalf of Russian intelligence in return for financial benefits. Those four individuals have been placed in pretrial detention. The other two were released with preventative measures put in place. The ABW says that the criminal group “illegally supplied Russia with significant quantities of military components, including those used in the production of ammunition and weapons systems”. “This type of activity may lead to the strengthening of the Russian arms industry and the military capabilities of the Russian Federation, and thus pose a serious threat to Poland’s security and interests,” wrote the agency. Prosecutors say that the group operated at least between June 2023 and December 2025 in Poland, Lithuania and Russia. Members were responsible for procuring goods and transporting them to Kaliningrad, which borders Poland and Lithuania. “Vehicles equipped with hidden compartments were used to transport the goods,” wrote the prosecutor’s office. “The suspects repeatedly crossed the Polish-Russian border, and some of the transports were intercepted by Polish border guards.” Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister in charge of the security services, revealed that the six suspects include five Polish citizens, aged 25 to 52, and one Russian woman, aged 37. Onet, a leading news website, reports, based on unnamed sources, that the Russian citizen acted as a liaison between the group and the foreign intelligence agency behind the operation. Funkcjonariusze @ABW_GOV_PL zatrzymali 6 osób podejrzanych o udział w zorganizowanej grupie przestępczej działającej przeciwko Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej. Wśród zatrzymanych jest pięciu Polaków w wieku od 25 do 52 lat i 37-letnia Rosjanka. 🛑 Sąd – pod zarzutem szpiegostwa -… — Tomasz Siemoniak (@TomaszSiemoniak) November 5, 2026 Poland has seen a huge rise in espionage cases in recent years. The ABW launched 48 investigations related to espionage last year, more than twice as many as in 2024. In those two years taken together, there were more espionage investigations than over the previous three decades combined. Last month, a Polish man was jailed for five and a half years for spying on behalf of Russia. The tasks assigned to him included reconnaissance of an airport as part of a possible plan to assassinate Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky while he travelled through Poland. In July, a Russian married couple with refugee status in Poland were convicted of working as spies on behalf of Moscow. In October, a member of Poland’s military reserve, who holds both Polish and Ukrainian citizenship, was detained on suspicion of espionage. World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun will again stand trial, after prosecutors filed an indictment against him for a series of anti-Ukrainian, anti-Jewish, anti-LGBT and anti-EU acts committed during his presidential election campaign last year. Braun is already separately on trial for a number of other alleged crimes, including an attack on a Jewish religious ceremony in parliament. He is also facing further charges for a range of other alleged offences. Grzegorz Braun stanie przed sądem. Prokuratura Okręgowa w Warszawie skierowała dziś akt oskarżenia za zuchwałą kradzież flag Ukrainy w Białej Podlaskiej i Unii Europejskiej w Katowicach, zniszczenie wystawy LGBT w Sejmie oraz zniesławienie organizatorów akcji Żonkile i Muzeum… — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) November 4, 2026 On Wednesday, the district prosecutor’s office in Warsaw announced that it had indicted Braun for four alleged crimes. It was able to do so after the European Parliament, where Braun sits as an MEP, stripped him of immunity earlier this year. One of the charges, for criminal defamation, stems from Braun’s claim, during a televised presidential debate in April last year, that the yellow paper daffodils distributed each year in Warsaw to mark the anniversary of the 1943 Jewish Ghetto Uprising against German Nazi rule are “symbols of shame”. Prosecutors say that Braun’s words were “extremely xenophobic, manipulative and aggressive”, and that they defamed the organisers of the daffodil campaign, in particular the POLIN Museum of the History of Polish Jews in Warsaw. During the same debate, Braun also warned about the “Judaisation” of Poland, saying that “Jews have far too much say in Polish affairs”. That prompted protests by some of his opponents, one of whom filed a notification to prosecutors. Two other charges relate to thefts of flags. In one incident, Braun and his supporters removed a Ukrainian flag hanging outside city hall in the town of Biała Podlaska during a campaign event. In another, he removed a European Union flag from the industry ministry in the city of Katowice and set it on fire. Braun regularly rails against what he calls the “Ukrainisation” of Poland, warning of the supposed dangers of having so many Ukrainian refugees and migrants in the country. He is also a vocal critic of the EU. On those and other issues, Braun’s rhetoric often echoes Russian propaganda. The final charge, of destruction of property, relates to an incident in June 2025, when Braun vandalised an exhibition about the LGBT+ community in the Polish parliament. He regularly condemns what he calls the “perversions” of LGBT+ people, and has called for homosexuality to be criminalised. The European Parliament has again stripped Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun of immunity to face charges of denying Nazi crimes. The decision marks the sixth time it has lifted Braun’s immunity, and the second time for charges of Holocaust denial https://t.co/O9FN1YbchE — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 16, 2026 The charges Braun faces carry prison sentences of up to five years in the case of destruction of property, and up to one year in the case of criminal defamation and theft. Additionally, the deputy leader of Braun’s Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP) party, Roman Fritz, was indicted for assisting in the theft of the EU flag, while four other men (who have not waived their right to anonymity under Polish law) were indicted for their alleged roles in stealing both the EU and Ukrainian flags. All four incidents for which Braun has been indicted took place when he was campaigning for the May 2025 presidential elections, in which he finished a surprise fourth, with 6.3% of the vote. Since then, KKP has continued to perform strongly in polls, with its support currently standing at around 9%. If it obtained that kind of result at next year’s parliamentary elections, it would be likely to play a major role in deciding what kind of government could be formed. Our essential guide to Poland's parliamentary elections, which will take place one year from now. How does voting work? What do polls suggest the outcome will be? Which issues may animate the campaign? And what role will President Nawrocki play? https://t.co/fmdoFpBaxz — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 15, 2026 Much of Braun’s political brand has been built around provocative statements and actions. The politician is already on trial for his attack on a Jewish Hanukkah ceremony taking place in parliament, at which he put out the candles with a fire extinguisher. In their statement on Wednesday, the Warsaw prosecutor’s office noted that the latest hearings in that trial had been cancelled after Braun presented a medical certificate justifying his absence. However, the prosecutors pointed out that, last Friday, the day that the hearings had been due to begin, Braun attended a protest by opposition supporters outside the Constitutional Tribunal in Warsaw, which that evening had been taken over by government-backed judges. Braun was pictured “jostling with police riot police, addressing the crowd and giving interviews”, showing “no signs of health problems that would prevent him from attending the hearing”, wrote the prosecutors. They have therefore asked the court to investigate the doctor who issued the medical certificate. World.title: “Democracy won in America”: Polish leaders react to US midterm election results
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Polish political leaders have reacted to the results of Tuesday’s US midterm elections, in which the Democrats won control of both houses of Congress from President Donald Trump’s Republicans. The outcome was welcomed by Poland’s ruling coalition, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk declaring that “democracy won”. The response was more muted from the right-wing opposition and the office of conservative President Karol Nawrocki, who is a Trump ally. 🚨 🇺🇸 Tusk gives Trump some great advice. But will the US president listen? Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk urged the US president to seek compromises after the Republicans' defeat and not to rely on vetoes as his main way of governing. Trump had earlier threatened to become… pic.twitter.com/s3E6G5zIQT — NEXTA (@nexta_tv) November 4, 2026 Tusk addressed the election results on Wednesday afternoon local time at a press conference alongside his Czech counterpart, Andrej Babiš. “Today, democracy won in America,” said a smiling Tusk. “I love democracy; it is a beautiful thing.” “As President Donald Trump himself said just after the election, the Democrats did a good job, and I really could not agree more with him this time,” added Tusk. “I hope that the result will stabilise the situation also in our region.” Although the United States remains Poland’s most important security partner, Tusk’s government – a broad, pro-EU coalition that ranges from left to centre right – has at times had uneasy relations with the Trump administration. It has been critical of Trump’s conciliatory approach towards Russia, his often tough stance on Ukraine, as well as his pursuit of US control over Greenland. Meanwhile, the head of the parliamentary caucus of Tusk’s centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party, Zbigniew Konwiński, told broadcaster Polsat News that “personally, I was happy with the Democrats’ victory”. “We know how Donald Trump behaves, how volatile he is in his political declarations, how he can sometimes put Ukraine in a more difficult position than Russia, so I would rather look for the positives in what happened,” said Konwiński. “If we look at recent years, the more Democrats, the stronger the Democrats, the better for Poland,” he added. .@Konwinski_PO: Cieszę się z wygranej Demokratów w USA, bo to lepszy scenariusz dla Polski. @marcinfijolek pic.twitter.com/gJ3TnlMn0l — Graffiti_PN (@Graffiti_PN) November 4, 2026 The speaker of Poland’s parliament, Włodzimierz Czarzasty, who is also the leader of one of KO’s junior coalition partners, The Left (Lewica), has clashed with the US ambassador to Poland twice this year over Czarzasty’s criticism of Trump. Today, Czarzasty shared and commented on a social media post by Trump, published in the wake of the Democrats’ victory, in which the US president showed an image of his signature red cap with the word “VETO” on it. “Where have I heard this before?” wrote Czarzasty, referring to the fact that Nawrocki has vetoed a record number of bills passed by parliament, where Tusk’s coalition has a majority. Czarzasty then went on to list a series of characteristics that he suggested both Trump and Nawrocki share, including “arrogance”, “lack of respect for women”, a “suspicious past”, “transactional exploitation of their position”, and “admiration for politicians with fascist tendencies”. Skąd ja to znam? Arogancja. Buta. Nieuzasadniona pewność siebie. Brak szacunku dla kobiet ( a to popchnę jakąś dwojga nazwisk, a to zakpię prymitywnie). Dziwna przeszłość. Instrumentalne traktowanie dziennikarzy. Pieniądze za spotkania. Transakcyjne wykorzystywanie funkcji.… pic.twitter.com/ryT2BMOZb2 — Włodzimierz Czarzasty 📚📖 (@wlodekczarzasty) November 4, 2026 Nawrocki has closely aligned himself with Trump. During last year’s Polish presidential election campaign, Trump invited Nawrocki for a private meeting at the White House. His then-homeland security secretary, Kristi Noem, visited Poland to endorse Nawrocki. Nawrocki himself has not thus far commented on Tuesday’s midterm election results. However, Marcin Przydacz, the head of the president’s International Policy Bureau, did address the issue in a social media post. “As predicted, in the US midterm elections voters decided on change,” wrote Przydacz. “Poland will continue its good cooperation with the US, because it is our ally, and collaboration is in our mutual interest.” Przydacz also added that the results were “a reminder for Tusk” that “no government lasts forever”. In Poland, too, “the moment will come when voters will decide on change – and it might be quite soon”, added Przydacz, in a nod to next year’s Polish parliamentary elections. Zgodnie z przewidywaniami w wyborach połówkowych w USA wyborcy zdecydowali o zmianie. Wcześniej wygrywali Republikanie, dziś Demokraci. Polska będzie kontynuować dobrą współpracę z USA, bo jest to nasz sojusznik, a kooperacja jest w naszym wspólnym interesie. O tym, kto sprawuje… — Marcin Przydacz (@marcin_przydacz) November 4, 2026 Tusk’s foreign minister, Radosław Sikorski, meanwhile, used the US election results to revive his long-running feud with Elon Musk, who is no longer part of the Trump administration but donated enormous amounts of money to support the Republicans ahead of the midterms. Last year, Musk and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio criticised Sikorski after he suggested that Musk had threatened Ukraine. In a post on his social media platform, X, Musk told Sikorski to “be quiet, small man”. On Wednesday, Tusk shared a screenshot of a tweet he had published last year, after Musk left the Trump administration, in which Sikorski wrote: “See, big man, politics is harder than you thought.” Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: International Commission of Jurists criticises takeover of Polish constitutional court
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The International Commission of Jurists (ICJ) has criticised the takeover of Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) by a group of government-backed judges. It says that the move “contravenes international standards on the independence of the judiciary”. However, the ICJ, a Swiss-based NGO led by judges, lawyers and academics from around the world, also chastised Poland’s opposition-aligned president, Karol Nawrocki, for his role in the crisis surrounding the TK, in particular his refusal to swear in judges elected by parliament. 🚨#Poland’s constitutional crisis must be resolved through the rule of law. The ICJ urges all authorities to respect judicial independence, follow lawful procedures, and comply with European court rulings. 🔗More information: https://t.co/NWmca9mpUx — ICJ (@ICJ_org) November 3, 2026 On Friday, eight judges who were elected to the TK this year by the government’s parliamentary majority effectively took over the tribunal. They announced that the chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, and his deputy, Bartłomiej Sochański, had been suspended for failing to properly fulfil their duties. Meanwhile, large numbers of riot police were deployed outside the court, holding back protesters, including opposition politicians, and preventing Święczkowski and Sochański from entering the grounds. Święczkowski denounced the takeover of the court as an illegal “coup d’état”. He has been backed by the tribunal’s remaining six judges, who, like him, were appointed under the rule of the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, which brought the TK under its political influence. Nawrocki has likewise denounced the actions of the government-backed judges. In the early hours of Saturday, he dramatically forced his way into the court, where he clashed physically and verbally with the judges who had taken over the TK. During a visit to the Constitutional Tribunal last night, President Nawrocki clashed physically and verbally with judges involved in an attempt to take control of the court. The president is today seeking talks with political leaders to discuss the crisis https://t.co/7HmBnuIaDG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 31, 2026 In a statement on Tuesday, the ICJ expressed regret that the latest developments have “deepened the crisis over the tribunal”. It called on Polish “state institutions to seek solutions…that comply fully with the rule of law, including the principle of the independence of the judiciary”. The ICJ’s secretary-general, Santiago Canton, noted that Nawrocki has refused to swear in five of the eight TK judges elected by parliament this year. That “violates international standards and is contrary to the interim measures indicated by the European Court of Human Rights”, said Canton. In May, the ECHR issued an interim order for all judges elected by parliament to be allowed to serve on the court. However, that has been ignored by Nawrocki and Święczkowski, who argued that the ECHR does not have the authority to make such a decision. The ICJ also noted that the roots of the crisis at the TK date back a decade, to the time when the PiS government took actions – including unlawfully appointing judges to the tribunal – that rendered the court illegitimate. “At the same time,” continued Canton, “the suspension of the president and vice-president of the tribunal without a fair and appropriate procedure established by law, carried out with the involvement of the police, contravenes international standards on the independence of the judiciary.” In its statement, the ICJ added that “criminal and disciplinary proceedings must respect all the guarantees of a fair trial and must never be used as a means to change [a court’s] composition”. Later on Tuesday, after the ICJ had issued its statement, the eight government-backed judges held their first general assembly, at which they moved forward with disciplinary proceedings against Święczkowski and Sochański. The justice minister, Waldemar Żurek, has also submitted six requests to the TK to lift Święczkowski’s immunity from prosecution so that he can face charges for a range of alleged crimes relating to both his time as chief justice and his previous role as a senior prosecutor under the PiS government. Skierowałem do Trybunału Konstytucyjnego kolejny, szósty już wniosek o uchylenie immunitetu Bogdanowi Święczkowskiemu, dołączając go do pięciu wniosków przekazanych w piątek. Dzisiejsza sprawa dotyczy zakupu systemu szpiegowskiego Hermes w czasie, gdy pełnił funkcję Prokuratora… — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) November 3, 2026 The takeover of the TK has also stirred controversy among Polish legal experts. The issue has even caused an unprecedented split at the Helsinki Foundation for Human Rights (HFPC), a well-respected NGO. On Saturday, the HFPC’s management board issued a statement, signed by its president, Maciej Nowicki, saying that it “sees no clear legal basis” for the actions taken on Friday by the government-backed judges to suspend Święczkowski and take control of the tribunal. It warned that the situation “set a dangerous precedent” and “does not contribute to fixing the tribunal”. However, HFPC also made it clear that the crisis at the court dates back a decade and reiterated its view that Nawrocki “has no right to block or invalidate the election [of judges] by parliament”. That statement prompted six of the eight members of HFPC’s council – a separate body from the management board – to resign. Those to depart included a former chief justice of the TK, Andrzej Rzepliński, and a former deputy human rights commissioner, Hanna Machińska. Machińska announced their resignation in a social media post. She said that the reason for her decision had been the management board’s statement, “with which I disagree”. Speaking later to broadcaster TVN, Machińska said that “we believe that the legal basis [for the TK takeover] was clearly defined”. Poland’s government, including Prime Minister Donald Tusk, has also argued that the takeover of the tribunal was necessary to ensure that legally appointed judges can take up their seats and that the court’s legitimacy can be restored. However, on Tuesday evening, Tusk shifted to a more conciliatory tone, offering to hold a one-on-one meeting with Nawrocki to discuss the crisis around the Constitutional Tribunal and “try to find solutions that will protect Poland from any political upheaval”. World.title: Disputed Polish constitutional court holds first meeting after takeover by government-backed judges
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The group of eight government-backed judges who last week took control of Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) have held a meeting at which they made a number of key decisions, including moving forward with disciplinary proceedings against the court’s chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski. However, the situation is mired in controversy and uncertainty. Święczkowski and the opposition-aligned president, Karol Nawrocki, do not recognise the judges who are now claiming control of the court, describing their actions as a “coup d’état”. Meanwhile, there are doubts as to whether today’s general assembly even had a valid quorum, given that the chief justice and six other judges appointed under the former government did not attend. PILNE: Zgromadzenie Ogólne Sędziów TK przyjęło, że kworum to osiem osóbhttps://t.co/SYEf9Ead3L — Rzeczpospolita (@rzeczpospolita) November 3, 2026 The meeting was called by Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, who on Friday declared that Święczkowski and the deputy chief justice, Bartłomiej Sochański, had been suspended for failing to fulfil their duties. Korwin-Piotrowska said that she herself, as the longest-serving judge on the court, was taking control. Large numbers of riot police were deployed outside the court, holding back protesters, including opposition politicians, and preventing Święczkowski and Sochański from entering the court. However, Nawrocki himself did enter the premises, where he clashed physically and verbally with Korwin-Piotrowska. For a general assembly of the TK to be valid, two thirds of the court’s judges need to be present. Normally, given that the tribunal has 15 positions, that would mean at least 10 judges being present. However, only eight judges attended today’s meeting. They were all appointed to the TK by the government’s parliamentary majority this year. But Nawrocki has refused to swear in five of them, meaning that their legal status has become disputed. The TK’s seven other judges, including Święczkowski and Sochański, were all appointed to the court under the former Law and Justice (PiS) government, which was widely seen to have brought the court under its political control, including by unlawfully appointing three judges. None of them attended Tuesday’s general assembly. Nevertheless, the eight judges present at the meeting, which was broadcast live for the first time in the TK’s history, decided that a quorum had been reached. They did so on the basis that three of the TK’s judges were not authorised to attend: Święczkowski and Sochański, because they are suspended, and Jarosław Wyrembak, because he inherited his position from one of PiS’s unlawfully appointed judges. That meant only 12 judges were authorised to attend, and two thirds of that number is eight, meaning that a quorum had been reached. Zgromadzenie Ogólne TK: JEST KWORUM! 👏 Według przedstawionej interpretacji liczy się je od 12 uprawnionych osób. 2/3 × 12 = 8. Prawo i matematyka.👏 pic.twitter.com/77v2ep9HbT — Pani Prezes 👠 (@PaniNaSzpilkach) November 3, 2026 Once that issue was agreed, the eight judges present proceeded to decide upon a number of key issues. First, they adopted a draft budget for the TK for 2027, something that Święczkowski had been unable to achieve, which was used as an argument for his ousting. Second, they drew lots to decide which of the TK’s judges would sit on disciplinary panels for Święczkowski and Sochański in relation to their suspension from the court. However, some legal experts have expressed doubt as to whether a legal quorum was established at today’s meeting. Ryszard Piotrowski, a prominent constitutional scholar, called the meeting “illegal”, reports news website Onet. Przemysław Rosati, the president of the Supreme Bar Council, also expressed his doubts. Obniżenie progu kworum na skutek zawieszenia prezesa i wiceprezesa otwiera puszkę Pandory. To jest mechanizm, który pozwala dowolnie obniżać kworum na Zgromadzeniu Ogólnym TK – wystarczy, że prezes zawiesi 10 sędziów i będzie mógł na Zgromadzeniu podejmować decyzję w trzy osoby.… — Marcin Matczak (@wsamraz) November 3, 2026 Święczkowski himself rejected the legitimacy of what he called a “social gathering”, saying that Korwin-Piotrowska is a “usurper” who has no right to call a general assembly at all, reported Polsat News. Shortly before the meeting at the TK, Nawrocki also met with the prime minister, Donald Tusk, for the first time since the crisis at the court broke out last Friday. They had convened at the presidential palace for a meeting of the National Security Council that Nawrocki had called before the TK crisis. During public remarks broadcast before the confidential meeting got underway, Nawrocki accused the government of “illegally taking over the Constitutional Tribunal”. He added that Tusk “bears full responsibility for…all these illegal actions”. Grubo! Karol Nawrocki do Tuska: „Pełną odpowiedzialność za wszystkie nielegalne działa w Trybunale Konstytucyjnym ponosi jeden człowiek, który jest obecny – premier Donald Tusk” pic.twitter.com/WMPnWTZIKt — chrzanik (@chrzanikx) November 3, 2026 Tusk and his government have argued that the source of the crisis is, in fact, Nawrocki’s refusal to swear in judges appointed by parliament, as he is required to do, and then Święczkowski’s resultant refusal to accept those judges onto the court. They also note that the TK has not been legitimate for a decade, since PiS unlawfully appointed judges and brought the court under its political influence. Speaking to broadcaster TVN on Tuesday before the general assembly, justice minister Waldemar Żurek said that the actions being undertaken by Korwin-Piotrowska are the only way “to rebuild the independence of the tribunal”.
