Lawmakers from Mr. Pena’s own party backed his impeachment. Mr. Pena, 47, apologized during an address to the nation on Thursday (November 5, 2026).

“It was never my intention to betray the trust you placed in me,” he said in a video statement.

‘Hurt’

Around 250 people were gathered outside Congress awaiting the outcome of the trial, one of them waving a sign that read: “Pena in prison.”

On Thursday (November 5, 2026), thousands protested for a third consecutive night in Asuncion and other cities to demand the return of their money.

“Santiago Pena has hurt so many Paraguayans, so many families, business owners and small business people, including my own son, who had savings in Ueno Bank,” Cynthia Farina told AFP at a protest in the capital that police dispersed with tear gas and water cannons.

Advance payments to an unspecified number of impacted depositors began on Thursday afternoon, Jose Maciel of the Central Bank’s Deposit Guarantee Fund told AFP.

The first phase of aid deposits, up to around $1,600, will go to clients who don’t have loans and have an account at another bank or institution in Paraguay to receive the funds, Mr. Maciel said.

The next beneficiaries “will be announced progressively over the course of the payment process,” he said.

Ueno began as a small fintech company with a digital-first model that attracted low-income customers, rapidly becoming a major bank that handled state pensions and the accounts of several state entities.

The opposition accuses Mr. Pena of a conflict of interest, which he denies.

The Attorney General said it was investigating him for “acts related to the supervision and resolution of Ueno Bank S.A. and the placement of public funds in said entity.”

The U.S. Embassy in Paraguay expressed “its solidarity with the Paraguayan people” on Friday (November 6, 2026), without mentioning the president.

‘Victims’

Ueno’s downfall shocked the South American country, which is generally considered economically and politically stable.

By impeaching him rather than letting him resign, lawmakers have prevented Mr. Pena from becoming a senator for life and enjoying immunity from prosecution, constitutional experts and lawmakers told AFP.

Vice President Pedro Alliana is preparing to complete the current mandate until 2028.

The scandal has claimed the heads of Central Bank President Carlos Carvallo and Interior Minister Enrique Riera.

Eight Ueno executives have been arrested.

Prosecutors on Friday (November 6, 2026) raided the offices of technology company ITTI, which is part of Grupo Vazquez, confiscating hard drives, computers and other items.

“We found a large amount of documents that will be useful for the investigation,” prosecutor Francisco Cabrera told reporters.

Nearby Argentina felt the impact of the crisis as some 1,000 ITTI employees were suspended for 30 days without pay.

Football also took a hit.

Ueno Bank sponsors several first division teams as well as the national team.

“We were also victims of this situation,” members of the national team said in a statement on X.

World.title: Unhappy Milind Deora shoots a letter to BMC chief over event exclusion
World.content:
Member of Parliament Milind Deora wrote a letter to Ashwini Bhide, Commissioner of the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), on Friday regarding an omission. Mr. Deora stated that the BMC did not invite him to an inauguration in Colaba.

Mr. Deora is a Rajya Sabha MP from the Shiv Sena, which is part of the ruling alliance in Maharashtra. Colaba falls in the area he represents.

The event was for a housing project under the Ashray Yojana on November 6, 2026, with Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde attending. Speaker Rahul Narwekar, Mayor Ritu Tawde, and Deputy Mayor Sanjay Ghadi also attended. The BMC distributed keys to workers under the scheme.

Mr. Deora wrote in the letter that representatives require notice of events in the areas they represent, noting that the event took place without informing him. He wrote that coordination and courtesy towards representatives must accompany initiatives, stating that representatives need to receive information about developments for the people they serve.

The MP requested Mr. Bhide to look into the matter and asked the Commissioner to ensure that protocol is followed to prevent an omission. He requested that officials receive advice to ensure coordination with representatives for functions.

World.title: Wave of resignations from U.S. Justice Department after midterms
World.content:
Several senior U.S. Justice Department officials have resigned, including its civil rights chief and a prosecutor investigating allegations of conspiracy against President Donald Trump.

U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche, a former personal lawyer for Mr. Trump, announced on Thursday (November 5, 2026) that he had accepted the resignation of Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights Harmeet Dhillon.

In this role, Mr. Dhillon was directly involved in unsuccessful attempts to obtain voter registration lists from some 30 states ahead of this week’s midterm elections that dealt heavy defeats to Mr. Trump’s Republican Party.

In her resignation letter, cited by U.S. media outlets, Mr. Dillon said that she submitted it in October and agreed to remain in her position until the election.

Ms. Blanche also announced on Friday (November 6, 2026) the resignations of Assistant Attorney General for National Security John Eisenberg, and Jason Reding Quinones, U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Florida.

Mr. Quinones oversaw an investigation into former intelligence officials whom Mr. Trump accused of seeking to remove him from power.

The Justice Department under Mr. Trump has pursued cases against a number of perceived enemies, and several prosecutors have lost their jobs over their reluctance or inability to bring charges.

In one high-profile case brought by the department, James Comey, the former director of the FBI, was indicted in April for allegedly threatening Mr. Trump’s life in an Instagram post of seashells.

World.title: Disallowed Friday prayers, under house detention for 6th day: Mirwaiz
World.content:
Kashmir chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq on Friday (November 6, 2026) said the authorities disallowed him from leading the congregation prayers at Jama Masjid, apparently in response to the sermon delivered on the previous Friday on the Kashmir issue.

“My house detention continues unabated for the past week, with police deployment and barricades in place. Unfortunately, I will not be able to deliver the Friday sermon at Jama Masjid Srinagar to the faithful today,” said the Mirwaiz in a post on X. He also shared videos of the barricading by security forces outside his residence in Srinagar’s Nigeen area.

Terming the move of the authorities as “arbitrary and authoritarian measures”, the Mirwaiz said, “It was aimed to curtail freedom of movement and speech, and also betray the official narrative of ‘normalcy’ in Kashmir”.

On the previous Friday, the Mirwaiz mentioned in his sermon the findings of the International Crisis Group report on Jammu and Kashmir and highlighted the concerns over political prisoners, civil liberties and the need for meaningful political engagement and reconciliation.

“Since then, the Mirwaiz has remained confined to his residence, preventing him from fulfilling his religious responsibilities, including addressing scheduled religious gatherings and leading the Friday congregation at Jama Masjid,” said a spokesman for the Mirwaiz, in a statement.

World.title: CPI(M) leader Biman Basu retracts after holding Jyoti Basu responsible for LF government’s industrial policy
World.content:
Senior Communist Party of India (Marxist) (CPI[M]) leader Biman Basu on Friday (November 6, 2026) retracted his remarks, holding the veteran party leader and former West Bengal Chief Minister Jyoti Basu responsible for any issues with the industrial policy of the State during the regime of Left Front.

“The Left Front government’s industrial policy was adopted and announced under the leadership of Comrade Jyoti Basu. If there were any problems with that industrial policy, it was Jyoti Basu’s fault. Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee was given the responsibility to implement that industrial policy,”

Mr. Sau said on Thursday (November 6, 2026). The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government in West Bengal on Thursday (November 5, 2026) came up with an investment promotion policy offering incentives to new industries that will be set up in the State.

Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Thursday (November 5, 2026) blamed the policy of forcible land acquisition during the regime of former Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee for the decline in industrial prospects of the State. The remark by the senior CPI(M) leader on Thursday sparked speculation on whether Mr. Basu came to the defence of Mr. Bhattacharjee by putting the blame on Jyoti Basu, the longest serving Chief Minister of the State from 1977 to 2000.

On Friday (November 6, 2026), Mr. Basu clarified that he did not talk about any divisions between the regime of the two Chief Ministers of the Left Front government. “The industrial policy was announced in the eighties by the then Chief Minister, Comrade Jyoti Basu. Accordingly, industries have developed. Thermal power plants have been built,” he said.

The CPI(M) leader said that the fact that no industries came to the State during the past 15 years of the Trinamool Congress regime should not be blamed on the Left.”I did not make any differentiation. I said, the industrial policy was not announced by Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee. His predecessor Jyoti Basu announced it,” Mr. Basu added.

Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee, who was the Chief Minister of West Bengal from 2000 to 2011, is considered to have made an earnest attempt to revive the industrial prospects of the State, but fell into the trap of forcible land acquisition, which brought the Trinamool Congress to power in 2011. The political opponents of the CPI(M), including Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, blame militant trade unionism in the State for the flight of capital from the State.

World.title: Samserganj encounter: Civil Rights group’s report flags loopholes; demands CID officers’ suspension
World.content:
Days after a 40-year-old man accused in the murder of a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) worker in Murshidabad was killed in a police encounter, the civil rights group, Association for Protection of Democratic Rights (APDR) flagged several loopholes in the action. It demanded the suspension of all the police officers of the Crime Investigation Department (CID) involved in the case.

Samaul Sheikh, who was a key accused in the murder of BJP worker Sujit Mondal on August 28, was shot dead in a gunfight with police in Murshidabad at around 3 p.m. on October 27.

According to the police, the accused, Sheikh, was taken to a place in Dhulian under Murshidabad’s Samserganj police station to reconstruct the crime. However, he allegedly snatched the service weapon of an officer and tried to flee the spot. He died in retaliatory firing during the incident

A seven-member APDR team reached the spot on November 2 to probe the matter. In its fact-finding report published on Friday (November 6, 2026), the organisation questioned the absence of CCTV cameras at the spot, position of the bullet shot on Sheikh’s head, and keeping his family in dark before taking him to the crime scene.

According to the APDR, the encounter took place in a small room on the second floor of a building located in a market area. “We spoke to some shopkeepers and found that the police took all the CCTV cameras from the area on August 28. They are not installed as of now. Therefore, there is no record of the movement of the police during the incident,” APDR said in its report.

It also said that there was only one bullet mark right above Sheikh’s ear, as his family members reported. APDR questioned why there was no other injury mark that might have indicated the clash between the police and Sheikh when he was trying to flee.

“It’s such a small room that it’s not easy to flee. Why couldn’t the police shoot at his leg or stop him by using physical force? It looks like that SheikhS was made to sit on his knees and was shot from a point-blank range,” said APDR.

A day before the encounter, Sheikh’s family members went to visit him at the jail, but they were still not informed that he would be taken to the crime scene the next day for investigation.

APDR also stated that the police have yet to recover the body of Sujit Mondal. “They only found a portion of a chopped leg. It is still not confirmed whether it belongs to Sujit. Sheikh’s family members alleged that the police falsely implicated him in the case. The investigation is also pending. It seems Sheikh’s killing was pre-planned.”

The organisation demanded that the government initiate a judicial inquiry into the matter under the supervision of a judge from the Calcutta High Court. They also demanded that all the CID officers present that day during the encounter. A second autopsy of Sheikh’s body at a hospital under the central government and compensation of Rs 50 lakh to his family members are also among their key demands.

About 12 hours before Sheikh’s death, Prahlad Das, accused of raping and murdering a minor girl in North 24 Parganas’ Gaighata, was shot dead in an encounter at around 3.30 a.m. This is also the third such incident in the State in four months, since the BJP government came to power. On July 8, a similar encounter took place in the South 24 Parganas Baruipur area, when police took Prabhas Mondal, the prime accused in the rape and murder of a minor girl, to reconstruct the crime scene.

World.title: Antilia case: Bombay HC sets aside Waze's bail, holds that terror threat against citizen cannot be tolerated
World.content:
The Bombay High Court on Thursday (November 5, 2026) cancelled the bail that a trial court had granted to Sachin Waze in the Antilia explosives case. It held that the material placed by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) meets the threshold of Section 43D(5) of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), which bars bail when the accusations appear true on a reading of the record.

The Bench also found that the lower court ignored the principles that govern bail.

A Bench of Justice Girish Kulkarni and Justice Neela Gokhale delivered the ruling in a judgment. It said that an industrialist or any other citizen should not face even a remote threat of terror, and that bail for Mr. Waze would go against public interest.

Ingredients of a terrorist act

The Bench examined the allegations that Mr. Waze used the car belonging to Mansukh Hiran, obtained number plates that were forged, procured gelatin sticks, loaded the car with them and parked it near the Ambani residence in Mumbai. It held that these acts, on a first reading, link directly to Section 15 of the UAPA.

The court said the record points to an act that threatens the unity, integrity and security of the country, including the security of its economy, and that is likely to strike terror among people. It noted that the target was the family of an industrialist whose group contributes to the country’s economy, as the NIA had argued.

The plot as the Bench read it

According to the Bench, the material indicates that Mr. Waze reported the car as taken, replaced its plates, left it outside the Ambani residence with explosives and placed a threat note inside. After the car was found, a message appeared on a Telegram channel in the name of a terror group and claimed responsibility. The group then issued a statement that disowned the act.

The Bench said the use of the group’s name shows an intent to create fear among people and to spread the belief that a bomb threat existed. It recorded the NIA’s case that Mr. Waze would then step in as the “super cop”, offer protection to industrialists and extract money from them. The Bench said the scheme resembles a film plot, but the consequences amount to serious offences.

Waze’s standing in the force

The NIA told the court that Mr. Waze was under suspension for 16 years, from March 2004 to June 2020, and wished to rebuild his image as a “super cop” after his return. The Bench noted that he held the rank of Assistant Police Inspector, yet owned luxury cars and obtained investigations for himself, including cases registered at police stations outside his jurisdiction.

On a first reading of the record, the court said he drew on the help of police personnel below him in rank and stood well outside the position of an ordinary government servant. It referred to his links with senior officials and to the extortion racket he is alleged to have run, in which he threatened hoteliers and bar owners with raids that had no basis. The court said this shows his ability to influence witnesses.

The Bench held that his release would risk the trial through tampering with evidence and witnesses, and that a police officer, who is meant to protect citizens’ rights, has no room to commit such acts. It said Mr. Waze cannot be treated as an honest public servant.

Criticism of the lower court

The Bench expressed concern over the manner in which the trial court handled the bail plea. It described the observations in the order as strange and as a departure from the principles of judicial reasoning, and said they showed no reliance on the criteria for bail.

It rejected the trial court’s view that framing of charges needs a lower degree of satisfaction than bail, and called it a legal perversity, since the trial court had itself found substance in the accusations.

The Bench also rejected the trial court’s reading of the High Court’s earlier order, which allowed Mr. Waze to file a new bail plea. The trial court took the order to mean that the High Court saw merit in his case. The Bench said the earlier order only directed that the plea be decided on merits and in accordance with law, and did not permit the trial court to set aside the material before it.

The Bench then quashed the order of the trial court.

World.title: Tiger Shroff firing case: Accused claims to be minor, court orders age verification within 15 days
World.content:
A special Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) court on Friday (November, 6, 2026) ordered an inquiry into the age of Phool Singh, an alleged shooter arrested in connection with the firing at Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff’s car, after he claimed to have been a minor at the time of the incident. The court directed the police to verify his age and submit a report within 15 days.

Mr. Singh was among 12 accused produced before Special Judge S. Navandar at the end of their police remand. The court extended the police custody of Mr. Singh and four other accused until November 11, while the remaining seven were remanded to judicial custody.

During the hearing, Mr. Singh claimed that he had previously been denied access to his lawyer and was therefore unable to inform the court about his age. His lawyers, Sidhanth Mor and Divyam Gaur, reportedly submitted a birth certificate issued in Haryana and his Aadhaar card to support his claim that he was approximately 17 years and 10 months old when the incident occurred.

The court questioned why Mr. Singh or his lawyer had not raised the issue during three earlier remand proceedings. It also declined the defence’s request to send him to a juvenile home pending verification of his age, observing that the claim could have been raised to avoid custodial interrogation.

The court subsequently directed the authorities to investigate Mr. Singh’s claim and submit an age-verification report within 15 days. If he is found to have been below 18 at the time of the alleged offence, the proceedings against him would have to be considered under the applicable provisions of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act.

Meanwhile, the 13th accused, Suneha Pandit, who was arrested in Karnal, Haryana, on November 3, 2026, remains in police custody until November 16 under a separate remand order. Ms. Pandit is the sister-in-law of wanted accused Anil Pandit, an alleged associate of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. Investigators have alleged that she was involved in financial transactions linked to the conspiracy.

The case pertains to the firing at Mr. Shroff’s car in Mumbai’s Juhu area on the evening of October 18, 2026. According to the police, two shooters allegedly fired five rounds at the vehicle as the actor was leaving a football ground. While Shroff escaped without serious injury, his driver and a bystander, identified as a vlogger, sustained bullet injuries.

The Mumbai Crime Branch registered the case on October 19 under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Arms Act. Provisions of MCOCA were subsequently invoked on October 27 after approval from the competent authority, as investigators examined the alleged organised crime conspiracy and suspected links to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang.

World.title: Petrol price down by Rs6.59 per litre, high-speed diesel by Rs4.25 in fifth straight reduction
World.content:
The government on Friday once again decreased the price of petrol by Rs6.59 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs4.25, in the fifth consecutive cut in fuel prices.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs346 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs378.

The prices are applicable from Nov 7 (Saturday) to Nov 10 (Tuesday) due to a public holiday on Nov 9, according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Monday for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

Addressing a press conference on Tuesday, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said efforts were being made to introduce a similar system for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

On Sept 13, PM Shehbaz also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, the petroleum minister announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Trump promotes Stephen Miller to chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles
World.content:
US President Donald Trump replaced chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller on Friday, elevating the architect of some of his toughest domestic policies to run the White House after Republicans lost control of Congress in this week’s midterm elections.

The shake-up puts a longtime Trump loyalist and firebrand policy adviser in charge of steering Trump’s agenda as the president prepares to confront a Democratic-led House of Representatives and Senate, and an expected wave of congressional investigations.

White House officials told Reuters that Miller’s selection suggests Trump will take an aggressive approach to domestic policy and politics.

Miller is a veteran of Trump’s first term in office in 2017-2021. Since Trump’s return to the White House in 2025, Miller has officially been deputy chief of staff under Wiles, but he wielded outsize influence across much of Trump’s domestic agenda and has had the ear of the president.

He is perhaps best known for driving Trump’s aggressive immigration crackdown, setting a target of 3,000 arrests a day. In pursuit of that target, federal immigration agents expanded their list of targets to include migrants who had been living in the US for decades.

In a social media post, Trump called Miller “one of my most trusted advisers,” and he praised Wiles for doing “an outstanding job”.

Trump said the change would take effect on Monday.

Wiles, who submitted her resignation on Thursday night, will move to Trump’s political operation, according to a White House official.

Wiles, 69, who announced recently that she had been given the all-clear from breast cancer, said in a statement on X that Friday would be her last day in her job.

“Serving President Trump in the White House has been the honor of a lifetime,” she wrote.

“I’m so proud to have been a part of what we’ve accomplished together from securing our border and cutting taxes to strengthening our economy and putting America First.”

Trump had been displeased with his political and communications operations in the run-up to Tuesday’s election as his public approval ratings fell near record lows.

This week, he said the White House needed to be “more aggressive” as Democrats retake congressional power, according to a person briefed on the matter.

Wiles’ allies in the White House began sharing concerns with others on Wednesday about her potential replacement, the person said.

“He’s rewarding those most loyal to him. He’s not changing course,” said another White House official.

World.title: Banks, utilities among services put on alert against AI-enabled cyberthreats
World.content:
The National Cyber Emergency Response Team (NCERT) has warned of an increased use of artificial intelligence (AI) and automated bots to carry out credential-based and coordinated cyberattacks, noting that critical infrastructure and financial services are at particular risk.

NCERT, in an advisory dated Nov 5, said an increase in “AI, automated bots, botnets and agentic tools to automate reconnaissance, identify vulnerabilities, conduct credential-based attacks and launch coordinated cyberattacks” has been observed recently.

“These capabilities may help threat actors and sophisticated cybercriminal groups to broaden the scale, speed and sophistication of their operations,” it added.

“This advisory is relevant to all sectors/organizations. However, two sectors require particular attention,” it stressed, referring to financial services, along with operational technology (OT) and critical infrastructure.

It warned banks that they could face attacks targeting core banking systems, digital banking platforms, payment systems and customer-facing applications, with potential scenarios including the disruption of online services, automated credential attacks, and manipulation of displayed account balances.

In terms of critical infrastructure, NCERT warned: “Third-party service providers, connected IoT (internet of things) devices, vulnerabilities in industrial control systems and insecure remote access may expose oil and gas facilities, water utilities, power generation and distribution networks, manufacturing, transportation and other essential services.

“A compromise could disrupt physical processes and critical services,” it added.

NCERT cited recent incidents in Europe, where supermarket refrigerators and freezers were targeted in cyberattacks, as examples of the “physical and commercial consequences of attacks against connected operational systems”.

“However, AI involvement in said incidents has not been confirmed yet,” it added.

Threat indicators

The advisory listed anomalies which may indicate a potential cyberattack targeting financial institutions, such as frequent automated login attempts, repeated authentication failures, and unusual application programming interface (API) requests.

Abnormal transaction patterns, differences between core banking records and the displayed account balance, and unauthorised payment access were other indicators.

For critical infrastructure, NCERT said changes to refinery, pipeline, grid, power generation or distribution parameters could indicate an attack, as could unexpected changes to pressure, temperature, cooling or heating control settings.

Unexpected remote access sessions or changes to IoT/OT device configurations could also point towards a cyberattack.

Recommendations

NCERT recommended that financial institutions check their core banking security, APIs, third-party integrations, payment gateways and digital banking applications.

It further urged them to use multi-factor authentication and protection against automated login attempts, while enforcing integrity checks between consumer-facing applications and core banking records.

The team also suggested monitoring bot-driven attempts, potential service disruption and abnormal API activity.

For utility providers, NCERT’s advice was to limit direct internet exposure and remote access and check the security of IoT assets and industrial control systems.

“Enforce OT/IT network segmentation and continuously monitor access to operational systems,” it recommended. “Keep applying security updates and maintain backup operating procedures for essential processes.”

NCERT also urged all organisations to check their preparedness against bot-driven AI cyberattacks, maintain incident logs and enhance arrangements for incident response, business continuity and security monitoring.

World.title: CDF Munir, Sudan's interior minister discuss avenues to enhance bilateral cooperation: ISPR
World.content:
Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Sudan’s Interior Minister Lieutenant General (Police) Babiker Samra Mustafa Ali on Friday discussed avenues to enhance bilateral cooperation between their countries.

Lt Gen Ali called on CDF Munir at General Headquarters (GHQ) in Rawalpindi during his visit to Pakistan, according to a statement by Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR).

“During the meeting, matters of mutual interest, evolving regional and global security dynamics and avenues for enhancing bilateral cooperation were discussed,” the statement said.

“Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening relations between the two countries, particularly in the fields of security, counterterrorism and institutional cooperation.”

The visiting dignitary “appreciated Pakistan’s role in promoting regional peace and stability and acknowledged the longstanding fraternal ties between Pakistan and Sudan”, according to ISPR.

CDF Munir reaffirmed Pakistan’s desire to “further deepen bilateral engagement with Sudan and underscored the importance of close cooperation in addressing shared security challenges”.

Earlier in the day, Ali called on Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

DPM Dar “reaffirmed Pakistan’s steadfast support for Sudan’s sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity”, the Foreign Office said.

He underscored the importance Pakistan attached to its relations with Sudan and its commitment to further strengthening the brotherly ties between the two countries.

Meanwhile, the Sudanese minister expressed his “appreciation for Pakistan’s support and continued solidarity with Sudan”.

“He highlighted the strength of brotherly relations between the two nations and underscored Sudan’s desire to further deepen cooperation across areas of mutual interest.”

Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry also attended the meeting.

Meeting with PM Shehbaz

On Thursday, a delegation led by Lt Gen Ali had met PM Shehbaz Sharif at the PM House.

The premier affirmed that Pakistan attaches “great importance to its longstanding and fraternal relations” with Khartoum, the PM’s Office (PMO) said.

“We want Sudan to emerge from its current crisis as a peaceful, stable, and prosperous country,” he was quoted as saying, expressing Pakistan’s desire to strengthen trade and investment ties with the North African country.

“There are vast opportunities for bilateral cooperation in sectors such as agriculture, defence, education, and others,” the prime minister added.

The Sudanese minister expressed gratitude to the premier for the humanitarian and medical assistance provided by the Pakistani government and people during difficult times, according to PMO.

He also commended Pakistan’s support on international forums regarding efforts to restore peace and security in Sudan.

Sudan remains the ​world’s largest displacement crisis more than three years after war broke out in 2023, when the Sudanese army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces clashed over issues including how to ​integrate their forces in a planned transition to civilian rule.

Around 8.6 million ​people remain displaced within the country, while more than 4.6m have fled across borders. ‌More ⁠than 5.2m people have also returned to their areas of origin, often finding homes, infrastructure and basic services destroyed.

World.title: Bilawal urges federal govt to engage all political forces instead of ‘fighting everyone’
World.content:
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Friday urged the PML-N-led federal government to engage all political and social stakeholders rather than “fighting everyone”.

Responding to a query at a ceremony in Larkana, the PPP chairman highlighted that people around the world were bearing the economic burden of the US-Israeli war on Iran.

“This is a backbreaking burden. We have not seen this phenomenon in the past,” the former foreign minister said, adding that even if the war ended tomorrow, its economic consequences were unlikely to end soon.

Bilawal contended that regardless of whether a country was directly involved in the war or not, supporting its people had become the biggest test for many governments.

“I advise the federal government that this is the time to engage with the political, social and provincial stakeholders rather than fighting everyone,” he remarked.

The PPP chairman further stressed that the coalition government’s focus should be on the economic difficulties faced by the people, not on their “differences with each other”.

“If the federal government and the relevant stakeholders focus on the problems faced by the people, only then we can emerge successful in this test, no matter how long it goes on for,” he said, referring to the economic consequences of the Middle East conflict.

However, Bilawal cautioned that if “we continue to fight among ourselves” and keep fighting with PTI and Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman — alongside the fight against terrorists, India, Afghanistan and others — then they might end up remaining engaged in that.

“Our priority should be the problems faced by the people,” he stressed.

Bilawal’s remarks follow exchanges of harsh remarks in recent weeks between Fazl and federal ministers, after the JUI-F chief accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights.

Fazl has been critical of the federal government over the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. He has accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments amid his efforts to mediate between the federal and KP governments.

Meanwhile, the PTI-led opposition and the Centre have been at odds over various issues, particularly the counterterrorism policy.

On Oct 16, without naming anyone, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had claimed that a “head of a party” was “extremely upset over being denied a role in the new setup in KP and not getting the governorship”.

The next day, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif and State Minister for Interior Tallal Chaudhry rebuked Fazl directly, who later clarified his criticism was aimed at policies, not state institutions.

The row played out in the Parliament as well, where Fazl questioned Asif’s absence and Naqvi’s presence at a meeting of the Makkah pact countries and Iran in Tehran.

In his response the next day, the interior minister explained his participation and went on to assail the JUI-F for “continuously crossing the line” and accused it of “extracting wealth from the state”.

Bilawal defends imposition of governor’s rule in KP

In his remarks, the PPP chairman rejected the accusations that counterterrorism was a pretence to dismiss the elected PTI government in KP by imposing the emergency and governor’s rule.

“This claim is not based on facts,” he asserted.

“The PPP maintains that the democratically elected governments are always in a better position to deal with all matters, including terrorism,” Bilawal said.

However, he noted, the recent surge in terrorist activities and the number of fatalities had never been witnessed since around 2007-2008.

“After the change of the government in Afghanistan, the terrorists’ threats to Pakistan have increased. This is a ground reality,” the ex-foreign minister said.

Bilawal contended that during PTI’s rule in KP, individuals imprisoned on charges of terrorism had been released.

He further said Sohail Afridi — the chief minister who has been rendered non-functional due to governor’s rule — had failed to combat terrorism and protect the people of his province, thereby leaving no constitutional or legal reasons for the president to reject the summary for emergency.

Thanking the federal government for engaging with the PTI on his party’s recommendation, the PPP chairman recalled the breakdown of the talks between the opposition and the government, attributing their failure to the KP CM.

“Even the opposition leaders who were negotiating with us know that they cannot blame anyone, including the prime minister, for this move,” Bilawal said.

“Even today, I invite the PTI to negotiate and request the government to engage with them. Do not close the door for talks,” he urged, stating that if a consensus is reached on countering terrorism, he would be the first person calling to end the governor’s rule.

The Centre imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The decisions were later endorsed by the Parliament amid protests by the opposition.

Electoral reforms ‘fundamental issue’

On electoral reforms, the PPP chairman termed it a “fundamental issue” and called the proposed Parliamentary Committee on Electoral Reforms (PCER) a primary platform to address the concerns.

Addressing political parties that have alleged rigging in various elections, including PTI, Bilawal maintained that the reforms committee could be the starting point to resolve such grievances.

Noting that opposition leaders in both the National Assembly and Senate had been empowered by PTI founder Imran Khan to make decisions regarding dialogue, Bilawal reiterated his call for them to exercise their authority by “unconditionally” naming their representatives for the PCER.

“If the opposition has some other perspective, the PPP is ready to engage with them or with the government, too,” he said, emphasising that all the political parties should become part of this committee for strengthening democracy in Pakistan.

“After all the efforts, if PTI does not take part in this committee, then the people of Pakistan should not pay heed to their cries against electoral rigging,” he remarked.

While reaffirming his party’s call for empowering the Parliament, the PPP chairman stressed that the opposition bore an equal responsibility in achieving this, and said it had an equal role in weakening the Parliament along with the government.

“If the opposition boycotts committee proceedings, then how can it criticise that the Parliament is frail?”

Bilawal added, “We have to begin from somewhere; that’s why I invite the opposition to participate in the electoral reforms committee.”

World.title: Activists breach Microsoft data centre construction site as protests spread in Europe
World.content:
Protesters broke into the construction site of a Microsoft data centre in Amsterdam on Friday at the start of two days of rallies that are part of a growing global backlash over the rapid build-out of computing power needed for AI.

Activist groups have announced actions in 16 countries on Friday and Saturday, according to the “Stop Dirty Data Centres” coalition, which is rallying environmental groups and digital rights campaigns behind calls to pause large-scale construction.

In Amsterdam on Friday, more than 100 activists gathered at the construction site of a Microsoft AI data centre, marching arm in arm before breaking into the site, climbing cranes, hanging balloons and dancing while police stood by. Some carried placards with messages reading: “Screw your data centre”.

“These data centres are destroying our world. It’s becoming uninhabitable because of all the resources they consume. That’s why we’re here today,” protester Sam van der Beek said.

Site owner Pure Data Centres, which plans to invest more than $1 billion and is backed by Brookfield-owned Oaktree, said it was committed to engagement with local stakeholders.

“We respectfully ask those on site to leave safely and engage with us in dialogue about the development and any concerns they may have,” it said.

Other planned actions include a march in Dublin, a protest outside the parliament building in Warsaw, and a demonstration against a different Microsoft data centre in Denmark.

Microsoft said it understood that people had strong feelings about the project and respected their right to express them peacefully but did not condone any unlawful actions.

Concern over AI drives stock market rout

Pushback is growing from Spain to India and the United States, where technology stocks fell sharply on Thursday over concern that Democratic control of Congress could mean tougher regulation curtails the AI boom.

Campaigners say data centres pressure electricity and water supplies, compete with housing and other businesses for scarce resources and threaten climate goals. They also point to job losses and potential risks to personal and national security from private and big tech concentrating power.

Technology companies argue that data centres are essential to meeting global demand for artificial intelligence and cloud computing and provide critical infrastructure for businesses, governments and consumers.

Stop Dirty Data Centres says it is not anti-progress or calling for existing data centres to be closed but that major construction should be halted until governments establish clearer rules.

Europe is divided between its ambition to catch up with the US and Asia on AI to boost productivity and to maintain what are generally more stringent controls and public protections.

Speaking to Reuters on Thursday, EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen said Europe needed more data centres to power AI development, though she added it needed to be done with care.

“AI, of course, is a super important technology and we need to have our own capacity,” Virkkunen said, pointing to investments being made in chip-making capacity, AI startups and a plan to build out gigafactories around the region.

However, she added, “It’s very important for citizens that they can trust that their energy bills are not skyrocketing and there are no electricity blackouts because of data centres, or they are not destroying the environment with these projects.”

A Google project in Finland faces a criminal probe over land clearances, Italy and Portugal are tightening environmental regulation for data centres, and Microsoft pulled out of a UK data centre project that was hit by infrastructure delays.

The Netherlands has about 200 data centres either planned, under construction or in operation.

World.title: Makkah Defence Alliance secretary general to assume duties in Riyadh soon: FO
World.content:
The Foreign Office (FO) on Friday said that the secretary general of the Makkah Defence Alliance, retired Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood, is expected to assume his responsibilities in Riyadh soon.

Mahmood was appointed on Sep 23 as the first secretary general of the alliance between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, signed on Aug 7, empowers the three members to consider an armed attack on one member an attack on all.

Speaking at the FO’s weekly press briefing on Friday, Spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan further said that the three members would jointly decide on convening a meeting of their alliance.

The Makkah Defence Alliance has garnered particular attention as Saudi Arabia faces attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels, including a deadly strike that closed Riyadh’s international airport for two weeks last month.

Pakistan is providing “whatever support is needed” to defend Saudi Arabia amid the Houthi attacks, the military’s spokesperson Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said in mid-October.

However, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) director general also clarified that all members of the Makkah Defence Alliance were “absolutely clear […] that this alliance has no offensive intent; it is purely defensive”.

The DG ISPR added: “Pakistan is giving very strong signals that this collective deterrence is at play, has already been actualised and we will take all necessary steps for the security and territorial integrity of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the Haramain Sharifain (The Two Holy Mosques).”

Islamabad has two defence pacts with Riyadh aimed at collective deterrence — the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement between the two and the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement that also includes Turkiye.

On Thursday, the Turkish parliament approved a bill ratifying the Makkah pact, paving the way for the trilateral security pact to come into force.

On its part, FO said late last month that Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already completed the ratification processes, noting that each country followed its own constitutional and legal procedures to approve and ratify international agreements.

Pakistan, others actively making efforts for peace in Middle East

In his briefing, Khan also touched upon the crisis in the Gulf, saying that Pakistan would continue its efforts to facilitate dialogue in the conflict involving Iran and the United States.

He said Islamabad had brought the two parties under one roof despite them having remained out of contact for decades and supported a peaceful resolution through dialogue and diplomacy.

Khan cited the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between the warring parties on June 18 as “a testament to Pakistan’s commitment to […] promoting peace and stability in our region”. He added that Pakistan, Qatar and other countries were actively contributing to mediation efforts.

The FO official emphasised that peace in the region must be established through “political dialogue and diplomacy” rather than war.

While acknowledging that the process of negotiations could be time-consuming, Khan asserted, “I believe that peace will eventually prevail and that countries will be able to resolve these matters peacefully.”

Elaborating further, the FO spokesperson said Israel was playing the role of a “spoiler” in the ongoing US-Iran war.

Criticising Israel’s expansionist policies, he said peace in the region was not in Israel’s interest and that its expansionist ambitions were among the major causes of the current regional crisis.

These ambitions were not limited to Iran, he said, adding that Palestine, Syria, Lebanon and other countries in the region were also affected by Israel’s expansionist designs.

When asked about the recent midterm elections in the US, the FO spokesperson said elections were an internal matter of that country and reiterated that Pakistan maintained close relations with Washington.

Democrats seized control of the US Congress earlier this week, capturing the Senate and House of Representatives in a stunning, nationwide rejection of Donald Trump set to put the brakes on the final two years of his presidency.

None harmed in strike on LNG tanker

The FO spokesperson was also asked about a vessel carrying Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) to Karachi, Al Mayeda, being hit by projectiles last week.

Shah said none of the 25 crew on board, including Pakistani nationals, were injured when the LNG carrier was hit while “transiting eastbound through the Persian Gulf in international waters”.

“The incident caused a small fire on board, but all crew members remained unharmed,” he said, adding that the vessel returned to Qatar.

“The concerned Pakistani authorities are coordinating with the relevant parties to establish further details of the incident,” he added.

The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) strongly condemned the attack on the tanker on Sunday, describing it as a “dangerous escalation”. Doha also denounced the targeting of the tanker “a dangerous act that threatens the safety of maritime navigation and the security of global energy supplies”.

World.title: Meghan Markle's estranged father arrested for child pornography possession: US authorities
World.content:
Thomas Markle, father of Prince Harry’s wife Meghan Markle, has been arrested for possessing child pornography, the US Justice Department said on Friday.

Markle, 82, of Lakeland, Florida, is charged with one count of possession of child pornography, the US Attorney’s Office for the Central District of California said in a statement. He is expected to appear in court in Tampa on Friday.

Markle is accused of possessing child sexual abuse material, including photographs depicting himself with minor girls, First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli said.

“These allegations are extremely serious, and we will prosecute Mr Markle to the fullest extent of federal law.”

A Justice Department official said the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) had arrested Thomas Markle.

A spokesperson for Meghan Markle did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Markle was taken into custody by FBI agents early on Friday at the retirement home where he lives in Lakeland, Florida. He could face up to 20 years in prison if convicted of possession of child sex abuse material (CSAM).

The Justice Department said Markle allegedly kept CSAM, including “sexually explicit photographs of himself with prepubescent girls, in two Los Angeles-area storage units he rented for nearly two decades”.

“Inside the units, agents seized approximately 78 items, including slides, film negatives, and books that contained suspected CSAM,” it said.

Daily Mail, citing unnamed sources, said material had also been found in a storage unit in Mexico as well as the Philippines, it reported on Friday, citing unnamed sources.

Authorities in the Philippines, where Markle had previously lived for some time, began investigating him last month over the allegations.

British tabloid The Sun reported last month that Markle’s son, Thomas Markle Jr, had discovered the child sex abuse images while going through boxes found in his father’s former home in the Philippines.

British police last month said they would refer allegations about him to overseas law enforcement agencies after finding that the claims had not been passed to other authorities when they were first received.

He has denied the accusations, telling the Daily Mail they were untrue and “sick lies”.

Meghan, an American who married King Charles’ younger son in 2018, has said she was “deeply distressed” over the allegations. She said she had blocked contact between him and her children over previous “troubling and disturbing” allegations.

In December 2025, Meghan got in touch with her estranged father after he had his left lower leg amputated in the Philippines.

The relationship between Meghan and her father broke down in the run-up to her wedding to Prince Harry in 2018. The fallout saw him pull out of his daughter’s wedding just days before the ceremony in Windsor, citing health problems.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.

The barriers are clear: high duties and VAT, high financing costs of 10–12 percent or more, limited access to easy loans, slow approval processes, net metering delays, high LC margin, weak Merchant Power Policy, lack of clear policies for rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, floating solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage, weak local manufacturing, and insufficient grid digitalisation. Addressing these collectively can accelerate Bangladesh's renewable journey, uniting stakeholders in a common goal.

One urgent reform is customs assessment. The current weight-based assessment system does not reflect the actual value of solar equipment. It can create artificial overvaluation and raise duties by three to four times. Bangladesh should shift to transaction-value-based assessment using pro forma or commercial invoice values, in line with international practice and WTO customs valuation principles.

The second urgent reform is the elimination of customs duty on renewable energy equipment. This should apply to Solar PV Module, Photovoltaic Cell, Solar Inverter, DC Cable, Data Logger, Aluminium Mounting Structure, Battery Pack, Battery Cell, BMS Circuit Board, PV DG Controller, Hybrid Controller, Solar Plant Safety Aluminium Walkway Mesh, Safety Accessories, and related components.

Current TTI rates are high. Solar PV Module carries 26.90 percent, Photovoltaic Cell 25.75 percent, Solar Inverter 28.73 percent, DC Cable 58.40 percent, Data Logger 37.25 percent, Aluminium Mounting Structure 58.40 percent, Battery Pack and Battery Cell 58.40 percent, BMS Circuit Board 31.50 percent, pack materials 37.25 percent, PV DG Controller or Hybrid Controller 89.08 percent, and Solar Plant Safety Aluminum Walkway Mesh 37.25 percent. These should be reduced to zero percent for renewable energy expansion.

The third reform is a tax holiday. Rooftop solar power producers and project companies should receive benefits comparable to those of utility-scale renewable energy producers. A practical structure could be a 100 percent tax holiday for the first 10 years, 50 percent for the next 3 years, and 25 percent for the next 2 years. This should apply to CAPEX, OPEX, IPP, and MPP models. A broader 10–20 year tax holiday for renewable energy projects should also be considered.

Bangladesh has a remarkable solar opportunity already waiting on its rooftops. About 7 percent of the country’s land is covered with concrete or other built structures. This means more than 10,000 square kilometres, or about 10 billion square meters of built surface. If only 30 percent is usable, that would give around 3 billion square meters. At 10 square meters per kW, this can create nearly 300 GW of solar potential. Bangladesh’s peak demand is only around 16–18 GW. The opportunity already exists on rooftops, factories, warehouses, schools, hospitals, government buildings, and commercial establishments.

Rooftop solar should therefore be relaunched nationwide with a clear business model. Utility-scale solar also needs support through unused khas land, transparent tendering, and grid readiness. Floating solar, river-based solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage should receive separate policy attention.

The suspended solar projects must also be revisited. A total of 31 solar power projects, with a combined capacity of more than 3,000 MW, were previously suspended or cancelled. Many were being developed by foreign investors, with more than USD 200 million reportedly already invested. If implemented, these projects could save around BDT 10,800 crore annually in energy import costs. They should be reassessed and revived quickly.

Energy storage is another missing pillar. Solar and wind need storage support to become more reliable. Duties on lithium-ion batteries, BESS, and other storage systems should be reduced to zero. This will help stabilise renewable power and support future grid flexibility.

Electric vehicles can also become part of the solution. In China, Japan, and the United States, EVs are increasingly seen as mobile energy storage systems. A typical EV battery has a capacity of 40–70 kWh, enough to power an average household for 1–2 days. If Bangladesh had 1 million EVs, the country would have 40–70 GWh of distributed storage. This is several times higher than the daily peak demand gap. Solar-powered EV charging, vehicle-to-home, and vehicle-to-grid systems should be included in future energy planning.

If Bangladesh had 30–40 percent of the grid powered by solar, along with solar-powered EVs, the country would be far less exposed to global fuel market shocks. Long fuel lines, online schooling, shorter office hours, and industrial disruption could be reduced. Solar, storage, and EVs should now be planned together.

Finance will decide how fast this transition happens. Renewable energy projects cannot grow at interest rates below 10–12 percent. Long-term financing should be available at an interest rate of 3.5–4.5 percent. A 10–15-year financing facility at a maximum interest rate of 5 percent should be introduced. Bangladesh Bank’s green refinancing fund should be expanded. Rooftop and residential solar customers should be eligible for collateral-free loans. The LC margin for renewable equipment should be limited to 5%.

Net metering must be simplified. Approval should be completed within 15–30 days through a one-stop service. Approval, interconnection, inspection, billing adjustment, and utility coordination should all be simple and time-bound. Wheeling charges for renewable energy should also be kept reasonable and low. The Merchant Power Policy should be clear, simple, and investment-friendly so that industries and commercial consumers can directly procure renewable electricity.

Agriculture should also be included in the solar transition. Bangladesh can set a target to convert 1.5 million diesel irrigation pumps into solar pumps. This will reduce diesel imports, lower farmers’ production costs, and protect the environment. The program should include duty-free facilities, low-cost loans, investment support, and local service networks.

Waste-to-energy should also receive policy support. City corporations need clear rules, easy financing, and private-sector participation to enable urban waste management and distributed power generation to work together.

Bangladesh now needs a phased national roadmap for renewable energy.

In the short term, within 0–6 months, customs duty, VAT, and taxes on renewable energy equipment should be reduced to zero. Duties on lithium-ion batteries, BESS, and energy storage should be withdrawn. Approval for net metering should be obtained within 15–30 days. Industrial and commercial solar installations should be eligible for special incentives. The 31 suspended solar projects should be reassessed. Wheeling charges should be rationalised. Solar, storage, and EV charging should receive urgent policy support. Collateral-free lines of credit should be introduced for rooftop solar. NBR should quickly implement assessment reform and a 0 percent duty.

In the medium term, within 1–3 years, renewable energy financing should be available at a maximum interest rate of 5 percent for 10–15 years. The LC margin should be limited to 5 percent. Land banks and grid infrastructure should be developed for utility-scale solar. Merchant Power Policy and MPPA should be simplified. Rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, and hybrid solar-storage projects should receive a 10–15-year tax holiday. A national program should convert 1.5 million diesel pumps into solar pumps. Rooftop solar should be made mandatory or incentive-based for government buildings, industrial zones, EPZs, economic zones, and large commercial buildings. EV solar charging and distributed storage policies should be developed. Renewable energy skill development and employment programs should also be launched.

In the long term, within 3–10 years, Bangladesh should aim to reach more than 10,000 MW of solar power by 2030. Offshore and onshore wind should be developed. Floating solar, river-based solar, and agrivoltaics should be implemented. A National Energy Storage Strategy should be prepared. Smart grid and power sector digitalisation should be accelerated. Local assembly and manufacturing of solar panels, inverters, mounting structures, battery packs, BMS, and EV charging equipment should be encouraged. Regional power trade should be expanded. The Renewable Purchase Obligation should be introduced. Fossil fuel subsidies should be gradually redirected to a renewable energy transition fund.

Image Visual: Anwar Sohel

The benefits can be large. Energy import costs will fall. Pressure on foreign currency reserves will decline. Industrial production costs will reduce. Export competitiveness will improve. The subsidy burden will decrease. New investment will grow. Renewable energy can create 20–25 jobs per MW through rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, solar pumps, EV charging, battery storage, smart grids, manufacturing, installation, operation, and maintenance.

The government may worry about revenue loss from tax and duty exemptions. But this should be seen as an investment. In the short term, there may be a limited impact on revenue. In the long term, Bangladesh can save far more by reducing fuel imports, lowering subsidies, saving foreign currency, strengthening industries, and attracting new investment.

Bangladesh’s energy crisis is a major challenge but also a historic opportunity. The crisis is not only a supply problem. It is a policy framework problem. Renewable energy, especially solar power, storage, and EV integration, can be among the most practical solutions for the country.

The question is no longer whether Bangladesh should adopt renewable energy. The real question is how quickly, how systematically, and how boldly the country can complete this transition.



Mohammad Ataur Rahman Sarker is a renewable energy entrepreneur and the secretary of the Bangladesh Sustainable and Renewable Energy Association.

Md. Tanvir Siraj is a renewable energy researcher.

World.title: The forgotten art of Bengali advertising
World.content:
I have never seen someone at a rustic village market, anklets jingling, shouting slogans for "Khol Company’s Ringworm Ointment." No smooth-talker has ever leaned in, fanning out thin booklets like a deck of cards, whispering rhythmically, "Here are the mysteries of Gopal Bhar, and here—the secret love letters."

I never hid colourful s of a reclining Gauhar Jaan, cigarette in hand, between the folds of shirts in my drawer. I did indeed rummage through my grandfather’s pockets to collect old tram tickets, but none of them bore that curious notice for "Ashtavakra Toothpowder." Perhaps the elders of the house witnessed a tram tearing through the heart of a half-awake city, bearing the Khadi Pratisthan’s pledge for cow protection—but there was no question of me witnessing such a sight.

An iconic early 20th-century  for Bukhsh Ellahie & Co., featuring classical maestro Gauhar Jaan holding a cigarette to promote their brand

Someone’s great-grandfather might have known which drummers came beating the kara and nakara to announce, "Tonight at seven, the Chaitanya-lila folk play commences." I never heard the name of a young "lad" like Dhiren Bal, who reportedly painted the  for "Himkalyan Hair Oil" at a three-way junction in Dinajpur.

While searching the Panjika (almanac) for the auspicious moment of a wedding, I never had the chance to chuckle at the suggestive illustrations for "Libido-Enhancing Tablets." On a morning shortly after Mahatma Gandhi’s assassination, I didn't sit with a newspaper wondering which artist, known only as "Munshi," had used swirling brushstrokes to sketch a portrait as a final tribute on behalf of some bankrupt cotton mill.

I saw none of this because I hadn't been born yet. Most of those who witnessed it are now gone forever. Yet, even without being born in that era, I have managed to 'see' it all. The old, withered newspapers and digital archives acted like Alibaba’s cave, revealing to me a lost jewelry box. To me, those vintage s were not just pages of history; they were the precious Sita-har, the Jhumko, and the Nak-chabi themselves. I saw those 'ornaments'—the lost illustrations—and through them, I glimpsed a world that has otherwise vanished.

Actually, on a sudden whim, I spent a long time digging through ancient newspapers and periodicals. My eyes kept getting stuck on the bizarre s still surviving on the faded, brownish-yellow newsprint of yore. I was looking, most of all, at the illustrations.

As I tasted this history, I remembered a book I read long ago: The Lost Tribes of Israel by Tudor Parfitt. Many believe that since the foreign invasions of Israel in the 8th century BC, at least twelve tribes went missing. Mr. Parfitt scoured the planet in search of them—a search that reportedly continues today. Some even believe the signs of those lost people are visible in the Afghans.

Looking at the drawings for old s, I felt I found a resemblance between those legendary lost tribes and these forgotten illustrators. That is why the book came to mind. It also felt as though there was no such mismatch that could prevent us from linking these unknown artists’ ghosts to their successors, even without a DNA test!

The connection might be clear, but can we not grant them even a small corner in the history of Bengal's illustrative arts?

Renowned figures like the artist Raghunath Goswami continue to say—no, those  drawings or ideas are not even worth considering. They claim it is a "mindless and indiscriminate simplification of art objects." They say the expression has neither grace nor form. Artistic value? Far from it!

For some reason, despite respecting the scholars' verdict, I grew stubborn. As I weighed the pros and cons, even the "ugly" artworks of those who drew s for ringworm cures or hair-growth tonics began to pull at my eyes. I saw in them plenty of humour, and plenty of heartache too. Nevertheless, I began looking for a way to have a long conversation with those early advertising artists.

A representative of a "vanishing species" like O.C. Ganguly (Arun Kumar Gangopadhyay) introduced me to a certain "madman." He had a crow's nest of hair. His lower garment was draped over his chest like a shawl. He wore a striped vest. His hands were shackled in massive iron rings.

It is precisely these kinds of s that art critics have referred to as brainless and ugly art. The  regarding the cure for insanity, however, dates back to 1952. Yet, long before that, a group of young artists from agencies had completely transformed the face of Bengali ads.

Apparently, such a madman would no longer need to be restrained. Why? Because the illness would be cured simply by administering "ABD Pills" and "Dutta Oil." Such was the claim of the "Bengali Asylum" of Dutta Nagar, Dum Dum, whose head office was at 29-A Vivekananda Road (Phone: Jorasanko 5220).

Seeing the address "Jorasanko" in that illustrated ad, I was immediately reminded of the Tagore family—specifically, their members who struggled with mental health. One was Birendranath Tagore, the fourth son of Maharshi Debendranath. He was brilliant at mathematics but suddenly fell victim to "wind-disease" (mental instability). The other was Somendranath, another brother of Rabindranath.

The Nobel laureate poet knew well which medicines helped the "insane." I learned of another —not for the ABD Pills of Dum Dum, but a special notice from "S.C. Roy & Co." at 167/3 Cornwallis Street. They advertised Dr. Umesh Chandra Roy’s world-famous "Great Cure for the Mad," priced at five rupees per bottle. The ad claimed that for over 70 years, this medicine had cured "millions of violent madmen and all kinds of nervous patients." This  would appear with a quote from the poet himself, saying: "...I have been aware of its efficacy for a long time." Was the "Great Cure for the Mad" then used on Birendranath or Somendranath? I know bringing up Rabindranath's name is somewhat irrelevant, but seeing these old drawings makes my mind wander in a thousand directions!

The illustrated  I mentioned was published in 1952—the day I saw the picture of the shackled madman in the paper. That drawing was made several years after legendary artists had already begun to dominate Bengali advertising. By then, Bengalis had seen hundreds of fantastic drawings for various products. A legend like O.C. Ganguly was earning forty rupees a month at Calcutta’s "Stronach Advertising" as early as 1937. An agency named "Paradise Advertising" existed in Calcutta in 1928. No one can really speak of agencies in East Bengal (now Bangladesh) before the Partition. We mostly know of the birth of agencies like Bitopi, East Asiatic, or Interspan in the 1960s. Clearly, advertising production in both Bengals (undivided India at the time) was centred in Calcutta. Be that as it may, an agency required an artist—someone to present the matter attractively to lure customers.

But not all sellers went to agencies. Instead, they took "ugly" creations (by today’s standards) made by local artists to make printing blocks for newspaper offices. The madman illustration is a classic example. The calligraphy in that ad was purely amateurish—something no professional agency would ever approve. Whether that ad ran before 1952 or if that was the first, I do not know.

It is undeniable that finding artists from the era before the establishment of agencies (pre-partition) is extremely difficult.
